[h1]超次元倉庫番パズルゲーム[/h1]

~~~おススメする人~~~

・初めての倉庫番パズルを探している人
・良作倉庫番パズルを探している人
・気楽にパラドックスを引き起こしたい人


~~~概要~~~

　箱を所定の場所に運んだ後に自分を所定の場所に置く、所謂倉庫番パズルゲームですが、このゲームは[b]個性的なギミックが多々ある[/b]のが最大の特徴と言えるでしょう。[spoiler]自分が箱の中に入ったり[/spoiler]、[spoiler]逆に箱を自分の中に入れたり[/spoiler]、[spoiler]問題内で発生するパラドックスを活用する問題[/spoiler]まで多種多様なギミックがプレイヤーを襲います。

　ただし、難易度が難しすぎるかと言われるとそうではありません。新しいギミックが登場すると、そのギミックの使い方を教える基礎問題→そのギミックを使った通常問題→そのギミックを使った応用問題と、階段状に難易度が上昇していくので、プレイしていていきなり訳の分からない状態にはなりにくい構造になっています。それに加えて、応用問題は赤枠や青枠で囲われているのですが、これらの問題は通常クリアを目指す場合は解かなくても大丈夫な設計になっています。こういったゲームが気にはなっているけれど、自分にできるか不安な人は通常問題のみを先にクリアしていき、難しい問題も何のその！な人は全ステージクリアを目指す。そう言った棲み分けができているのが本作のいい点だと思います。


~~~隠し要素のネタバレ含めた感想~~~





　本作は、通常クリアを果たすと[spoiler][b]今までのギミックをフル活用したおまけ問題[/b][/spoiler]が大量に追加されます。[spoiler]ここまでの問題、面白かったけどちょっと物足りないな...[/spoiler]、[spoiler]より難しいステージを解いてみたい！！[/spoiler]、そういった方々に向けた[spoiler]高難易度ステージ[/spoiler]が多数追加されます。全実績解除を目指す場合は[spoiler]これらの問題を含めた全ステージのクリアが条件になっています[/spoiler]ので、本作を遊んでみて、よりたくさん遊びたい方々はぜひ挑戦してみてはいかがでしょうか？

　私自身、全実績解除まで遊びつくさせていただきました。とても質の良い良作倉庫番パズルゲームになってますので、気になった方はぜひお手に取ってみて気軽にパラドックスを引き起こしましょう！！！

212837853.review:
Patrick’s Parabox is the kind of puzzle game that quietly invites you in with familiar mechanics, only to reveal layers of depth that expand far beyond the boundaries of traditional design. Created entirely by Patrick Traynor, the game begins with the simple act of pushing boxes, but it wastes no time in transforming that foundation into an intricate exploration of recursion, spatial paradoxes, and logical abstraction. What first appears to be a minimalist Sokoban-like experience quickly becomes an intellectual journey where every rule you internalize is later twisted, reinterpreted, or expanded into something more surprising. The brilliance of the game lies in its ability to introduce increasingly strange and delightful concepts without ever losing its clarity or elegance.

As you progress, the core mechanic — entering boxes, exploring the worlds inside them, and manipulating nested spaces — becomes a playground for experimentation. Simple layouts evolve into multi-layered structures where your perspective shifts constantly between interior and exterior spaces. The game encourages you to think not just about positioning but about containment, identity, and even the boundaries of the level itself. Some puzzles involve boxes that contain duplicates of the very space you’re standing in, creating loops that test your ability to reason through infinite regress. Others play with scale, sub-rooms, and the possibility of pushing a box into the place that holds its own existence. The result is a deeply satisfying progression of ideas, each puzzle acting as a small revelation that expands your understanding of what the mechanics can express.

The presentation mirrors the purity of the design. The visuals are stark and unembellished, composed of clean shapes and crisp contrasts that ensure nothing distracts from the logic in front of you. This minimalism is not a limitation but a deliberate artistic choice that allows every puzzle to speak for itself. The ambient soundtrack reinforces this contemplative tone, providing soft, atmospheric cues that create an almost meditative rhythm as you work through each challenge. The combination of subdued visuals and soothing audio delivers a space where the mind feels free to wander, dissect, and hypothesize without sensory clutter.

What truly elevates Patrick’s Parabox is its pacing. The game is exceptionally considerate in how it teaches, never overwhelming the player with complicated structures before ensuring the basics are internalized. New concepts appear at just the right moments, giving the player time to discover their implications naturally. Even as the puzzles ramp up in difficulty, there is always a sense that the game trusts you — it hands you a new idea and patiently allows you to unravel its logic. Later puzzles can be formidable, even dizzying in their complexity, yet they never feel unfair. They reward persistence, experimentation, and the willingness to reframe problems from fresh angles.

Despite its cerebral nature, the game retains a sense of warmth and personality. Every solution delivers a small moment of triumph, not because the game pressures you with difficulty spikes, but because its design communicates so clearly that you always feel capable of reasoning your way forward. There is no filler here; each of the many handcrafted puzzles offers a new perspective on the recursive systems at play. Optional challenge levels push the mechanics to their extremes, presenting scenarios that feel like final exams for the intellect, yet even these maintain the underlying elegance that defines the experience.

Patrick’s Parabox stands as a testament to the power of simple ideas explored with depth and imagination. It is a puzzle game that respects its players' intelligence, offering a space where curiosity and logic intertwine in endlessly satisfying ways. For anyone who enjoys puzzles that grow continuously richer the deeper you dig, or games that innovate through pure mechanical insight rather than spectacle, this is an essential experience. It is rare to find a game that feels simultaneously accessible, profound, and original, but Patrick’s Parabox achieves this balance with remarkable confidence, leaving a lasting impression long after the final puzzle is solved.

Rating: 10/10

This is an incredible puzzle game about pushing boxes, pushing looping boxes, create infinite loops and much more. It makes you feel smart without being overly difficult.

The worlds are structured such that each new mechanic is fleshed out with the normal levels and there are "challenge" levels which are harder and integrate mechanics from previous worlds.

Since each world focus on an specific mechanic, it becomes more clear what to do on each level, making the game very approachable to puzzle beginners. Even if the mechanics feel convoluted at first, the game makes a good effort to teach you them.

Steamの倉庫番系パズルはどれもこれも「評価は高いけど難易度も高すぎて…」みたいなのが多いです。が！こちらは難易度も含めて「ちょうどいい」感じなので、入門としても最適です。

很好玩的推箱子解谜游戏，用相对比较简单的底层机制设计出了许多有趣的关卡。第一次遇到递归或无穷的状况时，相信大多数人和我一样，感觉应该是“哇还能这样，既出人意料又在情理之中”。
对于推箱子这类游戏，我认为将它做得很难是很容易的，而将它做得容易又有乐趣则要难得多。我见过那种地图超级大的推箱子关卡，可能要不断地分支、试错，推几百步之后才能解开。但这款游戏不是这样，它的关卡设计能够引导玩家的思考，只要玩家领悟到了这一关想要使用的机制，那操作基本就是水到渠成的。我认为这就是一个好的解谜游戏应当具备的特质。

202907117.review: Patrick's Parabox takes a seemingly simple concept (what if level... in level?) and wrings it dry over the course of a few hundred puzzles. While the steam description states: "Each puzzle contains a new idea; there is no filler", some people will argue that the game may sometimes hold your hand a little in terms of difficulty. Three levels in a row will resemble eachother, the first two revealing an important thing to take into consideration when solving the last in the trio, but really the third level could have been presented on its own and propose an interesting, long, maybe meditative challenge. That's not to say the game doesn't have some interesting challenges - it does - but sometimes you'll feel like they take a little while to show up, or may be undervalued by the presence of the level before them. I still really liked the game though; I feel like it takes an interesting premise and pulls as much "game" out of it as you possibly could. Definite recommend for both experienced sokoban nerds and those looking to give pure puzzle games a try.

An extremely creative yet very fair Sokoban like puzzle game with a recursive twist.

Simple controls and a clever "object entering" mechanic offer 18 (main) worlds of puzzle mechanics. Just when you thought you had seen it all, a new mechanic gets introduced, expecting you to change your viewpoint once again.

Although I had bought this game on its release three years ago, I only recently started playing it regularly during the evening, as my daily comfort game. I definitely do not have the galaxy brain you need for some puzzle games out there, but Patrick's Parabox always offered just the right difficulty to me and every world seemed very fair and solvable, yet challenging. The recursion mechanic sometimes put knots into my brain and forced me to, quite literally, think out of the box.

Maybe, if you are a die-hard puzzle fan, looking for a brutal challenge such as English Country Tune, you may find this game too easy, but if you are on the lookout for a wholesome puzzle game with very creative main mechanic that challenges your skills in thinking ahead, you might have an excellent time with this one. I know I did!

[Mediocre] sokoban game. It's neat, cute, and has interesting mechanics, but it's ultimately boring. About 10% of the game is actually fun and interesting, the rest is not. The game is worth the casual speed-run through main levels just to check out the gimmicks and finish the game.

The first issue is "quantity over quality". Majority of levels are on shape-box difficulty, repeating the pattern you were given in previous levels and simply applying it again, and often again and again. Sometimes it worked well, making it trickier, but more often than not, it was not trickier, just the same in a different layout.

The second issue is resetting difficulty with each "area". You get to the area, you are given new gimmick, about half of the levels are tutorial, maybe 1 or 2 levels that makes you stop and think, then it's over and it resets to the next gimmick, next tutorial and so forth.

In my opinion, the game would've been far more fun if each area had two main paths and a third one for funny nonsense levels (blue ones). One path would be the base puzzle level, while the other one contains the same base as its counterpart but is significantly more challenging. Thus, giving the player a choice, either go through the easy path first and come back to the challenging path. The player would also have a choice to go through the challenging part, which would complete the easy version automatically, therefore, skipping the easy path altogether. Also, the easy version would be a hint/help towards completing the challenging versions, so new players would struggle less while more experienced players would prefer to skip them or use them as a hint.

However, with the current design, those two issues go hand in hand and make playing the game tedious far more often than fun.

200126955.review:
Great puzzle game with lots of aha moments where you suddenly see how the simple mechanics do mindblowing things, but when you think over you find that it "has to be". Lots of games with complicated combo effects often rely on artificial rules or a FAQ section to handle exceptions, but not this game. 

Take this example [mild spoiler alert]: if you are pushing against two open boxes, you-1-2-wall, in this order, then in the early game you might have figured out from experiment that 1 will go into 2, instead of you going into 1. But why? This need not be explained by priority! What happened is that you pushed again 1, then 1 will try to move forward (think of 1 is a temporary you and it hits the forward button). 1 says: OK, I will try to move and report the result to you; if I can move, then I move along, and if I cannot move, you enter me. Then 1 tries to move, and of course it can enter 2, so you get the result.

The excellent puzzle design makes sure that the players can figure out the rules with no verbal instructions except from the one-word theme of each map. And the game makes sure that figuring out the rule and messing around weird combinations is a rewarding process. 

How the author treats paradoxes is quite interesting. It was of course expected that there will be paradoxes, as the game title shows, and the author encourages you to find it (say, steam achievements), much like the game Recursed (my profile pic!). What's beyond my expectation is that there are puzzles designed around each of the paradoxes, which soundly proves the point that paradoxes are not just a "cool thing to break the game", but something that has beautiful consequences you wouldn't realize at first. [Spoiler alert] For example, in the "Cycle" chapter, riding on the conveyor belt using the infinite push paradox is very cute, and so as the eat and poop puzzle in the "Player" chapter.

199335766.review:
This is a perfect puzzle game. It begins by presenting the player with a simple set of rules, then lets them discover all kinds of ways to twist and bend those rules to solve some amazingly complex puzzles. 

Being a computer nerd, doing things like using recursion to hop through layers of infinity really scratched my brain. But as complex as these late-game concepts are, the game really eases the player into them with easier puzzles intended to simply showcase various possible ways to bend the rules. 

It really feels like the game wants you to succeed and move forward, which entices you further and further down the layers of recursion. I was always eager to discover what the next mechanic would be when completing one world and moving on to the next, and delighted to discover that this hole I was falling into ended right where it starts!

But the game also left a sort of Tetris effect in my head, where I kept seeing things recursively, seeing boxes inside of boxes, feeling recursion from my mouth to the back of my head. I can't explain it, this game just made me feel like I was going crazy, like solving all these puzzles was an obligation. Maybe it was the pretty graphics and lovely music? Maybe it's the promise of infinity, the feeling that there's a neverending hole of content to fall into and lose myself in, an infinite number of boxes that need moving and layers upon layers to discover...

Regardless, definitely a game worth playing. Completing it was one of the most satisfying experiences I've had this year lol.

作者的设计目标就是“让玩家丝滑地体验所有机制”，为此他甚至刻意简化和删除了许多难度较高的关卡，但同时也保留了一部分作为支线关或挑战关。[spoiler]不让你卡卡关你怎么知道你玩的是解谜(x)。[/spoiler]

本作围绕最质朴的玩法——推箱子，展现了创作者无与伦比的脑洞。整个游玩过程充满了不断的惊喜，虽然卡关很折磨，但是解开谜题，理清作者思路的那一刻真的有直冲天灵盖的爽感，实是解密爱好者不可错过的精品佳作。
下面我从一个新手解密玩家的角度来简单谈谈个人观点。
首先，游戏难度我觉得是循序渐进的，总体来看相比其他更硬核的解密，对于我这样新入门的玩家来说还是非常友好的。前面几个大关卡各自会介绍一种新规则，后面几关则会组合运用各种特性，用巧思而非堆步骤去逐渐加大难度。
游戏的几种规则是基于空间上的关系的，譬如进入，吞食，附身，循环等等，游戏中会打成无穷或者悖论的情况，这部分也是游戏设计的一环，这部分的运用相当精妙。
这种游戏的画面实际上无足轻重，但是本作里简洁的画面元素，泾渭分明的色块，干净的纯黑背景，灵动可爱的箱子和顺滑的动画转场，以及恰到好处的配乐，整天游玩体验在我看来还是相当舒服的，想来创作者在此方面也下了一些功夫的。
总的来说，这是一款解密爱好者们不可错过的佳作，新手玩家也可以借此入门，之后可以继续深入体验更多更难同意极富创意的游戏。

198858418.review:
Arguably the platonic ideal of a puzzle game.

This game starts off quite easy, but it introduces new mechanics at just the right pace to keep you engaged.  No singular idea overstays its welcome. You are being excitedly shown the consequences of each systemic axiom - yet the game also knows that oversharing would be counter productive, restraining itself to only the most meaningful nuggets.

The amount of content, however, is anything but restrained. There are 364 levels in the base game, and the vast majority of them have something unique to discover. I consider myself a fast puzzle solver, and it still took me ~22 hours to 100% the game. There are bonus puzzles and challenge puzzles and even alternate-reality puzzles, where the developer re-imagines one of those core axioms and shows you what puzzles might have looked like in that universe.

The OST is excellent. The artwork fulfills its primary purpose of being readable and leaving no ambiguities. The polish is generally just top-notch - for game that explores recursive and self-referential interactions, every possibility is seemingly accounted for. Creating paradoxes/infinities is actually embraced as a core mechanic, where in any other game it might have just been avoided to prevent crashes. It reflects the intentionality of the developer's approach to puzzle design.

It's the simple, genuine joyfulness of the presentation, and the generosity of the game's breadth, that really sold me on Patrick's Parabox. Pick it up for full price, or at a discount; It'll be a steal either way.

This is a rare example of a puzzle game that's beatable by puzzle novices but challenging for puzzle experts.

Despite the mind-bending nature of the game, the puzzles you need to clear to reach the credits are surprisingly doable if you spend a few minutes playing around. Sometimes it's worth skipping a puzzle and coming back to it after trying a couple later levels once you're more familiar with the mechanics it's showing you. I was able to reach the credits in about three hours, but I also still have about 200 puzzles left that weren't strictly required.

The challenge levels are aptly named; they range from tricky to brutally challenging. They also make up about half of the game's puzzle count. If you're a puzzle-loving completionist, you'll have a lot left to do as the game's mechanics are explored to their fullest.

19.帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇 Patrick's Parabox
循循善诱的套娃

简单说游戏的最核心玩法就是推箱子，但是本作自然也不可能仅仅是普通的推箱子，还加入了更多的机制。比方说他箱子可以推到箱子里、自己也可以是箱子、进出箱子可以左右/上下翻转、箱子套在箱子里等等。
本作的游戏机制很多，比方说常见的，进入箱子中的箱子时，会出现在内部箱子一侧的中间，但是出来时只有一个格子所以只有一个位置；将箱子挤压到另一个箱子上，如果有入口二者会触发吞并关系，但是谁吞谁则看具体形状等等。本作的机制虽然从数量上相当多，但是玩起来并不复杂，游戏的弱引导在解谜游戏里堪比天花板级别，每一个新机制的引入都会伴随大量的弱引导，从而让玩家全面地理解新机制的衍生机制。
本作在广度上如机制数量已经充足，在玩法深度上也相当出色。但问题或许也在这里，在解决前15个关卡后，进入最终的“无限”关卡时，游戏难度就会变得相当之高。一方面是作者的弱引导设计并不及前面那般出色，另一方面游戏的机制膨胀已经达到一个很夸张的水平，各种机制的组合应用是相当复杂的。与其说是玩法深度，更不如说是没活硬整的感觉，玩起来有些疲惫。

196179906.review:
This is one of my favourite puzzle games I've ever played. The concept of the nested or recursive levels could easily get too complex or out of hand but the game manages to present and teach it to you in such an accessible way that it never gets overwhelming. Yet it still keeps a solid level of difficulty throughout. 

Each world is usually based around some new core mechanic that's introduced, keeping fresh ideas showing throughout the game.

Each individual level keeps things simple - rather than overdoing the amount of stuff going on as some block-pushing puzzlers can do, each level ultimately boils down to one central obstacle that must be surpassed. This is exceptionally done in a way that keeps you constantly solving unique-feeling puzzles; almost every single level manages to make you feel like you've solved some new interaction of how the game's mechanics work. 

I particularly enjoy how often a puzzle is followed up with a puzzle that seems almost identical but with just a single aspect changed, and how often this results in a wildly new (yet still interesting) solution.

This really is a masterclass in puzzle design, one which feels particularly impressive with how often block-pushing puzzles can feel stale or like trial-and-error.

内容和扩展: 
  包含350+关卡. 我只打通主线和部分简单附加关,打了两三次共4.5小时. 主线主题就有18个,每个主题都有10+关卡. 后面还有挑战关和3个附加主题(游戏逻辑改变). 没有多周目要素.

  每个主题都要求打过一定关卡数才解锁下一主题,打完简单关卡后就能达到要求. 主题内还包含困难关卡和附加关卡可选. 若只打简单,每次开始游戏就可打通几个主题,难度并不高. 主线简单关卡约180个,若想一次打完会很烧脑. 如果打不过,设置里可以解锁全部关卡,直接跳到后面主题尝尝鲜也是不错的.
  主要驱动力就是见证新的关卡创意和主题创意. 主线打通关后估计不会再玩了.

I have mixed feelings about this game, let me just list pros and cons: 

+ nice puzzles
+ love the recursion motive
+ nice undo, reset and block of too fast input
+ good looking

- price: in my opinion this game should cost at most 50 PLN (or 10-12 EUR), because it's a puzzle game, i feel bad recommending this game to anyone, if it costs 92 PLN! i just don't get it what am i paying for? i bought it, i like it, but still, doesn't feel like money well spent
- GNU/Linux support: game works flawlessly on my Mac, but not on my Arch GNU/Linux, Factorio works out-of-the-box on those exact setups
- name: i just don't like it, it's not a big deal, but it feels... cheap? weird? i get why, but still, my opinion is that
- level designer: i don't know is it missing or just not unlocked, but i cannot find it anywhere, i believe there should be built-in editor for levels
- customization: it's nice to customize experience (by pressing 7), but the way of communicating that option is awful, i found it in description of some extra customizations, it's too much hidden for my taste
- saves and steam cloud: see edit below

EDIT: i finally found a way to run it under my Arch. The answer is Proton. Yes, only known way to run this game on GNU/Linux setup is NOT running it native, but through compatibility layer. I don't know is it Proton's fault (doubt it) or something is messed up inside the game (looks like it), but Steam Cloud doesn't work. Well, it works, but my saves aren't there. Steam says it's "actualizat", but inside the game there are no saves!

Do i recommend that game? I want to stay neutral, but Steam forces me to answer this question in yes/no manner. In that case: no, i cannot recommend this game with this price, if price doesn't concern You, fine, it is nice, but for Yall else decide for Yourself

Phenomenal puzzle game, one of the best I have ever played. It accomplishes so much with such a simple premise. Each mechanic is pushed to the limit without getting boring, constantly introducing new elements to the puzzles. 

Normally I find puzzle games have a steep, often frustrating, difficulty curve at some point- but this game is perfectly paced. The main puzzles you need to complete in order to progress get harder at a steady yet manageable pace. The optional puzzles do get pretty hard at times but the ability to leave them and come back later makes a huge difference. Such a joy to play, and even though the game has nothing else to it but a few hundred puzzles in a row it still managed to create a sense of awe and shock with how cool some of the mechanics introduced were. 

Easy recommendation for anyone who enjoys puzzle games.

192227167.review: Reminiscent of Baba Is You, Patrick's Parabox is a push-block puzzle with a twist. Sometimes, you can enter a block. Sometimes, you enter a clone of a block, Sometimes, a block enters itself. Sometimes, you are the block, or the wall. Each mechanic and puzzle solving aspect is introduced well, and there's enough variety and challenge to make this worth your while. I highly recommend this game to all avid puzzle solvers out there.

Patrick's Parabox is undoubtedly a good sokoban (block pushing puzzle game), but I didn't really enjoy it, which leaves me in a weird spot for a review. I picked it up after seeing YouTube videos and hearing how its the best puzzle game in ages, even though I don't really like sokoban's (they don't really work in my head for whatever reason). I ended up really liking the earlier levels, even though I struggled and raged at them for a while. The mechanics were interesting and the puzzles seemed to be designed fairly, and didn't waste your time with red herrings.

My main issue with the game didn't make itself apparent until I progressed further in; there are very few knowledge checks, especially early on, that you can't brute force. This allows you to make a whole lot of progress and experience most of the mechanics, before you are suddenly confronted with a knowledge check on some mechanic that used once and you haven't looked at in multiple play sessions. Particularly with the[spoiler]infinite and epsilon recursions, and their interactions with other mechanics[/spoiler], I desperately wished there was some more time spent explaining/showing how they worked (I still don't really get how the[spoiler]infinities[/spoiler] work). The part I struggle with is that throughout my time looking for hints on the later levels (I really didn't want to look up the solution), I constantly ran into people claiming that this is a very easy sokoban, so this could very well have been me accidentally skipping something important.

I honestly believe think that such an obviously intelligently and carefully designed game, regardless of my experiences and difficulties, deserves your time, even if you don't feel you have the mind for it. It took me about 7 hours to finish the base game, and another 9 to 100%, but the last two challenge levels I was stuck on took me over 4 hours so your time may differ significantly.

191121796.review:
This game was played in its entirety on a Steam Deck that was docked to a large television. All achievements were earned, and all puzzles were completed.

A Negative Review, with Huge Caveats!
Note: If you do not care about completing the game, AND if you have multiple input methods available to you (at least a controller AND a mouse), then this review is changed to a positive recommendation.

TL;DR - A good puzzle game that overstays its welcome. There are also some terrible control choices. 

Note on Reviews: I’ve checked many reviews for this game. It appears as though around 90-95% of them only have a small portion of the early game completed. This is also where the game is at its strongest. IF you plan to complete the game, then I urge you to seek out reviews from others that have also completed the game.

The Positives:
A) The concept is good. The execution is nearly flawless. The early game has a fantastic tempo to it.
B) Puzzles mostly follow a pattern of New Element Tutorial, Ease Into New Element, Difficult and Final Challenges with that Element. Each new puzzle element is explored thoroughly.
C) Zero crashes, zero issues with cloud saving.
D) Enjoyable graphics, animation, and music. Pleasant is a perfect word to describe all three.
E) One of the best undo and restart systems I’ve ever seen! You can even undo a restart!

The Negatives: (These will be longer and more descriptive. The game has overwhelmingly positive reviews. My positives largely echo many other reviews).

A) The game massively overstays its welcome. There are some games that leave you wanting more. This is not one of those games. By the time I had reached the archives and challenge stages, I just wanted the game to be over. Each element is explored so thoroughly that you are sick of it by the time you reach a new one. Much of it feels like repetition, because even though you might pick up one or two new skills during a new element’s “chapter”, there are so many puzzles in each that you will likely start to get bored. That’s not to say the game is too easy. In fact, the game gets downright mean in the post-game. I feel that this is the point where many reviewers (if they played to that point in the game) would change their review. It’s just not fun, these puzzles attempt to deceive you at many different points by using your previously learned skills against you. It also highlights the next two negatives more acutely than the rest of the game.

B) The game breaks its own rules. This can be done in clever ways. This game does not do it in a clever way. Instead, it takes the normal, set pattern of “new element introduced, puzzles get harder, possibly learn one or two new skills along the way, prove your mastery with the hardest puzzles at the end.” and uses it against you. This is broken by my count three times in the game. In all three cases, something changes in the middle of a “chapter” but only for one or two puzzles. But, the worst part is that these changes are not visible, and you simply will think you’ve done something wrong. The most likely way these will be solved is just by getting “the zoomies”, where you run around semi-randomly and bump into almost everything seeing if something different happens. This is, in my opinion, bad puzzle design.

C) The controls are just not great, particularly on the deck. This should be one of the easiest control schemes, you just move around! But, due to the recursive nature of the game, sometimes where you have to go, and what you have to do, might be really, really small, or so large you can’t even see it! That’s where the dreaded zoom function comes in! (I bet some reviewers have no idea what I’m talking about at this point) It’s not mentioned except in the options, and you don’t need to use it in the much easier, more pleasant early portion of the game. But, as things get much more complex, you will need to use this feature, and here is where the controls start to suck. You’re meant to use a controller to move yourself around. A keyboard is possible, but would be painful in my opinion. The problem is, even though you can set a button for zoom-in, you can’t actually USE the zoom-in feature, because something has to be SELECTED first. It doesn’t ever explain this. You cannot select anything with the controller. It is purely used for movement. You CAN use the mouse cursor to select an element, and THEN you can use the controller button to zoom in. Sound stupid? It is! The start button brings up the menu, You have a button for undo, restart, and zoom in. That leaves six buttons that do nothing. It would not have been difficult to have two buttons be “previous element” and “next element”. Sadly, without zooming in, some of these puzzles become nearly impossible to solve. The absolute last “challenge” puzzle in the game, I am convinced is NOT POSSIBLE to solve without using the zoom-in feature, as your character is actually completely off-screen and invisible for vast portions of the puzzle. A guide could be used, but otherwise, a person would be completely stuck!

Well, thank you for reading this far. I did enjoy the game, I just enjoyed the first part a LOT more than the last part.

Patrick's Parabox is the best puzzle game I have ever played. It's a clever twist on the Sokoban-style puzzle genre with a central focus on "boxes in boxes" and going inside the very boxes you push. The execution is perfect, with mechanics explored to their fullest potential but never overstaying their welcome.

My favorite thing about Patrick's Parabox is its welcoming approach to game design. No puzzle in the game felt like it was actively trying to stump me; rather, the trickier puzzles always had a clean solution that made sense and would feel obvious in retrospect. The calm lo-fi music by Priscilla Snow also helps to reinforce a more meditative vibe, gently encouraging the player to think about the puzzle at their own pace without stressing over scores or time limits.

Part of what makes the game feel so approachable is the pace at which it introduces new mechanics. The game starts very gently with a handful of introductory levels, and then gradually introduces new mechanics one batch of levels at a time. That way, you always feel equipped to take on the puzzles you are up against. Some of the late-game puzzles are pretty mind-bending—some may involve pushing a box out of itself, creating double/triple infinities, or even [i]entering yourself[/i]—but by the time you reach them, you will feel well prepared for any absurd complexities they may throw at you.

I also really appreciate the freedom each puzzle gave me to experiment with the mechanics. There were several instances where I was messing around with some mechanic or idea just to see what would happen, and I would somehow fumble my way into a solution. In these cases, I would immediately restart the puzzle to see if I could retrace my steps and make sense of why the solution worked, and that process was always so deeply rewarding.

All of this makes for a puzzle game that manages to be mind-bending, relaxing, fascinating, and incredibly satisfying to learn. Patrick Traynor, you have made a masterpiece!

Patrick's Parabox is one of the most clever puzzle games I've played. However, it's not the kind of game I can simply tell you is good, you have to experience it yourself. It has an indescribable quality, but if I had to compare, it's like the Inception of puzzle games. "A box within a box within a box..."

The game eases players into new mechanics, but every once in a while a level might introduce a tricky gimmick that stumps you. The game teaches the player through trial and error, encouraging experimentation. The best approach is to identify the winning state and then figure out how to get there. Then ask yourself, "What happens if I do this...?" It reminds me a lot of Baba Is You. However, Baba allows for more creativity, often allowing multiple solutions. Parabox usually only has one true solution. Also I think in Parabox, you can sometimes brute-force your way to the solution while not fully understanding how you got there, while in Baba you have to be more deliberate in your approach. That's why in terms of difficulty, this is probably easier than Baba Is You.

The game is divided into the "main campaign" and challenge levels. Minor spoiler: the main campaign might as well be called the tutorial, because the challenge levels is where the real game begins. I probably spent more than half my playtime in the challenge section alone.

There isn't much after you finish every level, which is a shame. I hope to see an in-game level creator for user-created levels. Custom levels exist, but you have to go download them from an external source then paste the files into the game folder. Wish there was an easier way to find custom levels. Overall, Patrick's Parabox is one of the best puzzle games on Steam and well worth a try.

Turns out, if you keep playing with that idea, you can make a whole game out of it, and the way each world introduces exactly one new concept (e.g. "What if the block you were pushing around actually is another copy of the level, with another copy of you and this block inside?") and then forces you to clear multiple levels built around various applications of that concept works really well to get you at least somewhat familiar with it before it introduces the next twist.

Generally, it didn't break my brain as much as Baba is You, and you have a decent chance to solve any given puzzle if you just start messing around to see what happens, so it was fun to play, yet easy enough to finish - albeit with many breaks in between, as is the case with any puzzle game.

玩家既可以 以缩略图的形式直观的看到当前房间中更内一层的房间的情况和在屏幕四周看到更外一层的房间颜色和周围一圈的情况，又可以使用鼠标切换查看更远的层。让玩家无需移动主角位置就可以获取更多的关卡结构信息，解决了玩家需要花额外精力来记忆各个关卡的布局和嵌套关系的问题。
但是我觉得作者其实还可以更进一步。为什么不能允许玩家在调整了视野的缩放和中心点之后，允许玩家保留调整后的视场进行推箱，而不是像现在这样一进行推箱就拉回镜头呢？我觉得如果允许这样做，或许可以更容易的理解一些同时在多个窗口发生的事或者更方便的在推箱的同时观察外一圈更大范围的情况。以便在陷入僵局的时候更好的找到出问题的原因。

最喜欢的关卡：挑战5
最喜欢的桥段：无限退出/无限进入（比无限更远的地方有什么 是我觉得最有特色的机制）

评分细则：
8.0值得一玩   9.0放心购入  9.5精神财富

9.5
tm怎么做得那么好？！
系统性解谜大体可以分解出几步
一是大致分析，确定必有步骤
二是头脑风暴，脑洞难点突破口
三是逻辑整理，确定主线顺序

该游戏的主要难点是在第二步，是最难设计，却做得最好的一步。而且每一关只有一个左右的难点，次顺序整理也相对简单，所以玩家可以集中精力于头脑风暴中。而可能性其实不多，进过逻辑推理后，大概可以猜出解法。
然后怀揣着激动的心情，完成关卡要求，无与伦比的成就感会将你淹没。
但等等！还有300多设计水平极高的关卡，玩家便上了瘾，深陷美妙的逻辑迷宫中。
当然，我不是说不能出现复杂的操作顺序要求，但是系统性解谜大多都有侧重点，当你又想要复杂逻辑，又想要意想不到的解法时，你最好不要放进一个关卡。或者，你要在逻辑上，给复杂逻辑的部分和核心难点之间留一点间隙，也就是说，可以让玩家把核心难点那一部分视作一个黑盒子，其后有着一些从谜题开始就可以确定的必经步骤！其他游戏的设计失误，大概就是把核心难点和其余逻辑顺序的难题杂糅在一起，尤其是指向一些之前从未出现过的解法。这当然可以增加难度！但是玩家即便可以攻破核心难点也无法确定做得就是对的，或者遍历复杂逻辑时，误把可以走的路当作死路。解谜游戏要上难度有时候很难避免这一点，但这个游戏确实做到了，即便玩家暂时无法攻克在“后面”逻辑难题，也可以解决在“前面”的突破点，然后认为“虽然不确定接下来要干什么，起码我比刚才确实更进一步了”。也是多亏于此我能不看攻略完成除了挑战世界中的7个关卡之外的所有关卡，其余极难的题目也会留下一些穷举的机会，而那七个关卡却也不在逻辑上给我额外的课题，结合游戏优秀的引导，可见作者确实非常想鼓励玩家进行思维上的突破。
此外游戏本身也非常有脑洞，对悖论的使用实在是令人叹为观止，兼具体量和质量，完成度极高，可以说是一款可以放心原价购入的游戏。

This is easily one of if not the best puzzle game I have ever played. It feels so overwhelming at times how recursive the game becomes, yet at the same time there were very few times were I was actually stumped. I almost always had ideas flowing just because of how the game is. It's built in such a way that even when you feel like you should have tried everything, you still haven't, and you know it. There are two levels though that had weird camera that kind of made me feel nauseous, but they weren't bad. There was only one level I feel like was actually bad, and that was Flip level 17. The level would be really easy, but the visual style obscures information in the same way a couple of Baba is You's worst levels did, by changing the visual style, and it is far worse in this game because as overwhelming as it can seem, information is VERY important, and much more difficult to get through trial and error. Most puzzles that do that are still fine, but Flip 17 includes a gimmick that doesn't mesh well at all with obscured information, as it gives too many and too few options all at once. I looked this level up, it was the only one where I got so stumped that I felt I had to, and by time I did, I was SURE I had already tried the solution I found, but I was incorrect. I get that the level was too simple to be a level with normal visuals, but it was too complex for the out there visuals. Every other puzzle in the entire game I solved without really even thinking of looking, which should speak to not only the quality of the game, but how much of an outlier this puzzle is.

My playtime was inflated by idling overnight, and a few times today, but I would guess that makes up roughly... 15 of the hours, maybe a little more. It's fairly short, but it is a brilliant game and I cannot possibly recommend it enough, just beware Flip 17. I give this game a 9.75/10 for what it is. Absolutely amazing.

《Patrick's Parabox》是一款高难度推箱子解谜游戏。

若是笔者来为游戏起名字，一定是叫做“悖论盒”，作为一款推箱子游戏，该作加入了无数创新机制，而相较于其他同类型游戏，该作的难度可以说是循序渐进，引导做的最出色的作品了，从选关界面的布局上讲。先是引入机制并通过多个简单关卡实际演示，分支作为难度挑战和对机制的侧面思考，连续关卡作为机制的深入，不会有超级难的关卡带来无穷的挫败感[strike]点名《baba is you》[/strike]。

游戏有两个相当出众的优点值得借鉴与学习。
第一，是游戏的每一章节对应一个独特机制，而机制直接反映到章节选关界面之中。例如从[居中]章节到[克隆]章节，有两个入口，笔者纠结半天选择一个，打完[克隆]后前往另一个却回到原地是恍然大悟，游戏将克隆的机制直接体现出来，又比如后续的[玩家]和[占据]，玩家进入关卡的动画也随机制进行了改变，可以说是更高维的设计了。当然，要是在这一层面更加深入，比如设计在选关界面利用机制才能得到的隐藏关卡等等就更好啦。

第二，游戏中有众多的Error，无穷大和无穷小的概念，是非常贴合游戏本身设计，且非常新颖合理的概念。玩家在前期惊喜的发现，并极力避免其出现。而此时，游戏又站在更高的维度进行了反向思考，将这些Error在后面的章节直接作为机制，让玩家去深入理解这一熟悉而陌生的机制，足以体现设计的水平之高。

非常推荐喜爱解密人士来体验这款佳作。游戏的流程难度因人而异，全成就需要通关全364个关卡，建议做好准备在挑战。

A very interesting and fun idea, great puzzle game for people who aren't that experienced with sokoban-ians. For people who play a lot of puzzle games this game should be smooth sailing, and you probably won't get stuck on a level for more than 5 minutes. I 100%'d the base game and haven't done the extra content yet, but so far I feel like the levels could be harder. Especially near the end, I didn't really need to dive into some mechanics in my mind and think about them until I understand them perfectly to beat the level. I could trust my intuition that "If I do X I will probably win" or "I don't know what X will do but that's probably what the level wants me to do" to beat a lot of levels (again, especially in the last 3 worlds) and that's a sign of the levels being either too limited in options or just too easy. In my opinion there should be at least a few hard levels (even optional levels) in the base game that require you to have a very good understanding of the mechanics at play in order to beat them. in any case, it was very fun to play and very fun to experiment with, now I'm gonna go 100% the extra content :)

Edit: With around 9.5 hours on my save I 100%'d the game. Definitely enjoyable, definitely creative, but still in terms of difficulty it's nothing special. When I played Baba Is You I had levels stumping me for weeks before I managed to solve them. And yeah, obviously Baba is an exception and is considered to be one of the if not the hardest puzzle game available, but when I could beat each level within a few minutes it's a bit disappointing. I was more challenged on the few SnakeBird levels I played at my friend's or on the demo of Maxwell's Puzzling Demon. The thing is, the concept here is great. This game deserves a more content update with harder levels.

Difficulty: ★★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆
Quality: ★★★★★★★★★★

It's funny how every YouTube playthrough of this game has episode breaks at the exact same points the whole way through. This is because the dev tries to reach into your brain and use it as a sockpuppet. None of the thoughts you are going to have in this game are going to be your own, all of them have been carefully planned out by the dev. Including puzzle solutions. Which means this is one of the easiest puzzle games I've ever played, despite the mechanics being so mind-bending. It's funny because the game is inspired by Recursed, which I'd describe as the exact opposite, where each solution feels like it's derived by you, and not the dev. That's great too, but the specific sequence of thoughts patrick has come up with and implanted directly into our brains is just beautiful. The mechanics are explored super deeply, and each puzzle explores a fun little trick (even though you may not be finding it yourself). Custom levels exist, and explore the mechanics even deeper, but none have the outright magical effect of the basegame, where it reads your mind by writing to it.

182972179.review:
个人评分：9.5/10
一句话评价：推箱子类解谜游戏中的登峰造极之作，对核心机制的挖掘深入透彻的同时又在新机制的引入上保持克制。恰到好处的难度曲线，克制的新机制引入都让大部分玩家能完整体验到本作的全部魅力。
游戏时长：全流程10小时左右，全成就15小时左右
购买建议：steam史低45.6元，cdk17元左右，建议直接购买散key

优点：
1.绝妙的核心机制。递归这一核心机制就像we will rock的前奏节拍一样，当它出现时既让人感觉本该如此，又让人感慨为什么前人没有发现。主线的18个大关中，有12个大关是从递归机制的应用方向设计谜题，3个无穷大关也是引入递归机制后自然而然会产生的结果，可以说本作就像一本展示递归在推箱子中应用方式的教学手册，将各种可能的方向都展示了一编；
2.克制的新机制引入。18个大关中只有第11关的翻转、第14关的夺舍和第15关的墙方块算是全新机制，与递归机制存在一定冲突或者其他可能性的新机制都放在了通关后的3个附录关卡里，可以说始终将游戏的基调定在了让绝大多数玩家感受递归与推箱子结合本身的魅力；
3.恰到好处的难度曲线。递归和推箱子都是具备极高难度上限的谜题类型，但本作并没有过多在难度上为难玩家，甚至于本作的主线关卡难度被限制在了大部分玩家进行适当的试错就能靠自己解决的程度，即便一时半会儿解不出来也能直观地想到解题思路。即便是通关后的挑战关卡也没有过多为难玩家，更多考察的是玩家对各个机制的理解而非通过试错逐渐摸索出唯一的答案。这一点对于解谜游戏来说很难得，近几年高分逻辑推理类解谜游戏或多或少都存在难度曲线过于陡峭的问题，以至于相当一部分玩家不借助攻略很难领会到游戏全部的魅力（点名批评轨道连结）

缺点：
1.不支持创意工坊。虽然本作可以通过某些方式游玩别人创作的社区关卡，但相较于创意工坊的一键式操作来说还是太过繁琐了。

Difficulty : 2/5 (Normal)
Global : 4.5/5 (Great)

Curator page : [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44695991-Anokturnus/]Anokturnus[/url]

Patrick's Parabox is a sokoban puzzle game that takes inspiration from the masterpiece Recursed to offer a different kind of recursion-based puzzles.  

The goal is to put a box or a cube on top of each mark in the level, you then need to place yourself on the player mark to end the level. The cube you control can push any box as long as there's no wall behind it. The boxes can contain a room, you can enter them if the middle of the box is open and the box can't be pushed further.
The rooms contained in the boxes can also be the very same room you're already in, recursion is at the center of this game... and it's such a good core mechanic, it really makes you think in very unconventional ways. 
Describing the other mechanics of Patrick's Parabox is nearly impossible as there are tons of them (each world introduces a new one and deepens it) and I don't want to spoil anything.
That creativity is really the strength of the game, it's astonishing how diverse the puzzles are and the more you progress, the better they become; it's very similar to Baba is You on this aspect (yes it's that good).

The game is not designed to be very challenging though, it consists of hundreds of small and pretty straightforward puzzles. It also takes inspiration from The Witness for its puzzle structure, the main puzzles in each world are a multi-step tutorial. You can hardly be stuck on those, they really are extremely basic and meant to efficiently teach you the new stuff.
The true puzzles are the "challenge" optional puzzles, or in other words the normal puzzles. They are not difficult either, but offer more challenge and explore the subtleties of the mechanics.
It's still a shame that there's not a lot of very challenging puzzles, otherwise the game would've been perfect to me. 

Patrick Parabox is a mind-bending gem, one of the most creative games I've played and a concentrate of fun.
A nearly perfect game and a must-play for any puzzle lover.

This is one of the best puzzle games I've played. There is a lot of depth in this game. There are so many puzzles, and every one of them has some interesting aspect of the mechanics to highlight. Some of the puzzles are pretty mind-bending, but once my mind bends around it and I have that realization of what I need to do, it feels so good.

Since you only have to complete a certain amount of puzzles in each area to advance to the next one, you never have to be stuck on a single puzzle that you're struggling with. And some that I was banging my head on and skipped for a while I was able to get pretty quickly when I came back to them later, so being able to set them aside for a time was very helpful.

There's also a pretty good pacing to the game. Each area introduces a new concept, and the puzzles start off pretty simple to let you get a feel for how it works. Then the difficulty ramps up and the later puzzles in the area can be pretty challenging. But once you clear those and move on, you get a nice break to be introduced to another fun aspect of the game.

The designer chose to focus on the mechanics and puzzles, so there's not a lot else going on in this game, and that's not necessarily a bad thing. The mechanics and puzzles are so unique and interesting that I wouldn't really want it muddied up and lost in a complex narrative or world. This game is an inch wide and a mile deep in that it keeps a pure focus on exploring all the facets of the mechanics. Really a joy to play.

One of the best puzzle games I've played in a long time. 

Admittedly I haven't played a lot in the puzzle genre recently. Friend put me on to this game, gifted it to me in fact, and it reminded me of how a good puzzle game should be. The rules range from simple logic to the esoteric, but there are always a handful of easier levels at the start of each new concept that not only show off said mechanic; it also shows you nearly the full extent of the mechanic as well. Moves, techniques, the works. The challenge comes of course from applying your knowledge in the optional side levels, which range from self explanatory to... well... you'll be shoving boxes around aimlessly for half an hour until it suddenly clicks.

There were some moments of frustration in this game. However, a distinct majority of times where you get stuck, the solution turns out to be something that you just overlooked. Thinking outside the box, one could say, haha. There are a couple hitches, and the challenge levels at the end are certainly headscratchers (I still haven't done them all as of writing this,) but overall it very rarely felt unfair, or pulled something out of the aether to trick you. It gave you room for error and time to experiment, and you could remedy any mistakes or misinputs with a back button and a restart button (back button also undoes your reset if you accidentally hit it like I did a dozen or so times, haha.)

Other than that, not much to say. The aesthetics are simple and cute, and the music is very pleasant, and fitting for the respective worlds they're in. Certainly a recommend from me.

[b]TLDR[/b] Abstract sokoban-style game with recursive mechanics, not as challenging as you’d expect. [17/20⭐, 17h🏅, 3/5💡]

[b]Context[/b] Patrick’s Parabox is an abstract sokoban-style game with recursive mechanics where obstacles are themselves navigable areas. The closest in mechanics would be [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/macwh/recommended/497780/]Recursed[/url], even though that was a platformer.

[b]Writing[/b] There is no plot, the setting is completely abstract.

[b]Aesthetics[/b] The visuals are simple and abstract, and the soundtrack calm and non-intrusive. In general everything is decent but not particularly memorable.

[b]Gameplay[/b] Patrick’s Parabox is a grid obstacle game where the obstacles are themselves navigable areas that can be entered. While this already introduces some interesting challenges, it gets mind bending (and paradoxical, hence the name) once levels start to be contained within themselves and have multiple occurrences. This leads to some impressive effects but without ever getting too challenging. In fact, even in more complex levels there are little paths to explore and solutions end up being rather simple (except for a few bonus levels). Granted, I felt not all introduced mechanics work, such as levels with areas with varying grid sizes that never felt natural.

As any game of the kind, you can hit deadends when solving a level, but can always undo indefinitely (including after restarts). Game progress is auto-saved but not the level progress.

[b]Value[/b] It took me about 10h to beat the ~300 main levels and additional 7h to beat the ~60 bonus levels. You can always revisit levels, and there are multiple progress slots. There are custom downloadable levels so you can further extend gameplay (although I haven’t tried them). Achievements are mostly related with progressing the game, except requiring certain actions that naturally happen throughout normal gameplay.

仕事終わりのヘロヘロの頭でトロトロやって全実績解除までいきました。
卵焼きでもひっくり返すように「無限」を裏返す感覚が味わえるのはこのゲームだけ。かなり高い次元のことを誰でも遊べるとっつきやすい形で表現しています。音楽がやさしくてかわいいのでキッズにもおすすめ。

As a consequence people who dislike Patrick's Parabox truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn't appreciate, for instance, the humour in Patrick's existencial catchphrase "It's Paraboxin' Time" which itself is a cryptic reference to Sega's Japanese epic Morbius. 167961732.review: Pretty good box pushing puzzle game that does some fun, trippy stuff with its recursion mechanic. It constantly plays with new gimmicks and twists to provide a varied experience. While it gets reasonably challenging and has some good head-scratchers, the game overall is on the easier side - I got stumped twice in total out of the 364 puzzles, and felt like a dunce when I looked up the solution for one of them. The overall design trends toward a clean minimalism, with little in the way of obfuscation, red herrings, or complex solutions. Most of the levels are so barebones you can usually figure out what to do simply by poking around and trying every option available. Some of the later stages of the game feel like they're more about highlighting unique gimmicks but don't manage to work the gimmick into a satisfying puzzle. Still, the best puzzles here hit the mark of being a satisfying challenge but not something that will cause most people to give up in frustration. The challenge puzzles after you beat the "normal" game are for the most part very rewarding. Points for creativity as well. I'd recommend this one a lot to anyone who likes puzzles but isn't a super hardcore expert solver.

Pretty much another puzzle game masterpiece, if you like being challenged. Generous amount of levels with a broad enough offering such that you'll rarely get hard-locked out of a path to progress. Definitely has a "rhetorical" approach to introducing concepts within the vast possibilities of its ruleset which steadily builds upon itself: 
"Okay you just successfully applied this concept, but how do you apply that with other things you've learned, or with this constraint?"
You have to think outside the box, you have to think inside the box, you have to BE the box.

 [h2] Fazit [/h2]

162862505.review:
Patrick's Parabox is a fantastic and delightful puzzle game, and ranks highly among my favorite puzzle games of all times.

Like many of the best puzzle games (-> footnote), the game sets up a small universe of game mechanics and interactions, and then explores them to the fullest extent. However, Patrick's Parabox has a couple of characteristics that elevate it even among this illustrious company: the basic game mechanic of recursive boxes is incredibly unique and delightfully interesting; the game's great UX makes this unique mechanic surprisingly approachable and intuitive; and the game's difficulty curve is comfortably flat, so the game actually feels finishable. (Compare that latter point with Baba is You, another puzzle game I love, but which I also found frankly exhausting by the end.)

The game has a fantastic progression system. You're never stuck at a single level but always have a bunch of options to proceed, e.g. you only need to solve 1/3 to 1/2 of the levels in each of the 18 main chapters to proceed to the next one. Plus individual levels are delightfully small and only consist of a small number of components, so while you might have to skip a few particularly challenging puzzles, it's unlikely that you'd get completely stuck. (In an interview, the dev mentioned that he made levels as simple as possible while still expressing the core idea, without any red herrings or superfluous elements.)

The flat difficulty curve feels perfect, too. I like completing challenging puzzle games, but I don't particularly like replaying them, because it's one thing to solve a difficult puzzle once and a different thing entirely to bash one's head against a difficult puzzle again after one had already solved it previously. And yet Patrick's Parabox is one of the few puzzle games I've replayed. Another point in favor of the flat difficulty curve is that it helps completionists like me complete the game without looking up too many levels. In my initial playthrough, I only looked up 5 of the 364 levels.

After playing many sokoban-style games with a par move mechanic, I also appreciated that Parabox doesn't have one. As a result, it feels like the game rewards playful experimentation: when you're stuck you can just goof around by moving around randomly, and sometimes something interesting happens that gives you an idea for how to solve the level.

Ultimately, I adore this game. About the only bad things I can say about it are a) that I didn't like some of the music tracks, and b) that there are a few levels (Challenge 19-21) with multiple player character boxes, and since I couldn't make intuitive sense of their priority order, I had to write it down instead.

Highly recommended.

Footnote: As inspirations, the dev mentioned Stephen's Sausage Roll, The Witness, Recursed, and sokosoko as explicit influences, plus Snakebird and Baba is You. Talk about good taste!

A recursive sokoban with tons of interesting mechanics. When combined, these mechanics provide an endless possibility of ingenious puzzles, 364 of which can be found in this game.

The puzzles are divided into 20 worlds (plus appendix and challenges) to smooth the difficulty curve. In addition, there is a main path to follow: the core puzzles on the main path gently introduce new mechanics and need to be finished in order to unlock the next world; other puzzles offer additional challenge and explore deeper unusual consequences of the mechanics. Thus, casual players can finish the game by completing only the 100 or so core puzzles, while more hardcore players may strive to solve the more difficult ones to their heart's content.

Accessible yet with incredible depth, Patrick's Parabox is a must-play for all puzzle lovers.

160428560.review:
Patrick's Parabox是一款关于无穷的推箱子游戏。推箱子游戏是什么想必大家都很熟悉，但是关于无穷的推箱子游戏是怎么回事呢？为此，首先我们要了解什么是推箱子游戏。推箱子游戏是什么想必大家都很熟悉了，但……

是在范围有界、相等尺寸下推动箱子到指定地点的游戏，玩家要在狭小范围内运转移换来完成目标。parabox在目标上继承了这一点，但在其他方面都做出了创新。本作的章节题目颇有点题意味，现录于下：入门、进入、空白、吞食、参照、调换、居中、克隆、转移、开放、翻转、循环、玩家、占据、墙、无限退出、无限进入、多重无限。

谜题的设计大约有几个不同的体验阶段。前面的几章，主要玩法是在更小的箱子或世界中进出，到达平常无法到达的地方，完成操作，如蝴蝶穿花，狡兔入窟。中间的章节，则侧重于嵌套和传送机制，需要玩家对于无穷嵌套有一定的理解，在漫长的嵌套之中合理进入退出，调转顺序，如蚂蚁上树，羊亡歧路。至于后面部分，机制则更为放胆跳脱，在玩家身份上、无穷概念上大做文章，令人拍案叫绝，如凤凰窥湖，蛟龙衔尾。

该游戏难度适中，卡关情况很少，不得不说是作者的刻意善良，让即使是解密新手也能进入心流，享受乐趣。另外每一章机制新鲜度也是节节攀升，才过一峰，又见一峰，展开相当紧凑，乐趣始终围绕在线，而不似有些解密游戏，一鼓作气，再衰三竭了。

可以说，作者确实并不以难倒玩家为喜乐，有相当一部分的“关卡”，几乎没有任何难度，唤作“表演”都更为恰当。这也说到游戏的音画表现。画面虽然简单，但是质地很好，主角也很可爱，扭动挤压特效也不错，关于无穷嵌套的演出效果也从容规矩，使人目不暇接，在循环一章中尤其可见。音乐也轻松自在，而当你创造进入悖论时，音乐一刹变得诡异虚寂，心里难免打鼓一下。

古人之观于天地山川草木，往往得焉。至于今人，则未免太过矫情，玩游戏也不必发出玄远幽虚的感叹。但parabox确实带给了我某种程度上的哲思体验，主要来自于其中的无穷极限和自我指涉。即使是在数学上，无穷也引入了相当多反直觉的结论（如条件收敛级数可以通过调换顺序收敛到任意值），这本身就是一个拓展思维边界的概念。当你操作时，你能否意识到你并非在操作一个角色，而是无穷个角色同时在被移动？挤入子世界，角色从当前世界外面进来了，他们是同一个角色吗？这重要吗？此外的嵌套顺序，无穷边界的出口入口，也相当精妙。自我指涉的说法倒并不严格，只是表现上比较仿佛（也许叫递归更好），在克隆、翻转、玩家等章节多有体现，我进入我，我推动我，虚世界进入实世界，即属此类，这也是悖论中的经典议题。所以在游戏性之外，parabox给人以或数学、或宇宙上的遐思。

总的来说，parabox是一款在谜题设计、节奏把控、音画演出上都无穷趋于完美的游戏，瞻之在前，忽焉在后，令玩家深陷其中，欲罢不能！分01，疑置可无

I can not recommend this game enough if you want a truly head scratching puzzle game. I played the demo a while back and let me tell you it's been a few years since a demo made me want a game bad enough to... practically immediately buy it.

Speaking of buying it. Is it worth the price? Yes. If you can get it on sale it's a bonus. I don't think I paid full price? But I can say that if I had I wouldn't regret it.

I'm 2.7 hours in (probably a bit more since I've played some on steam deck while not connected to wifi) and I don't know how many puzzles I've gone through but I know without a doubt that I'm NOWHERE near the 350 puzzles in this game. On top of that, even when I do beat it I know I will be able to replay this game. The puzzles are enough of an "out of the box" thinking *buh dum tis* kind of situation that I promise you won't beat this game and go back and remember the solution to everything. So you'll definitely be able to go back and play it more if you liked it the first time you played it.

The puzzles in this game ARE difficult, and it takes the kind of thinking of games like Baba Is You. Difficult puzzles, but never difficult in a way that doesn't make sense or that seem unfair. You just have to try to look at things a bit differently. This game is hard but I fucking love it.

When I want to wake up the skull organ this is the game I've been picking up.

I've also not used a guide yet. I refuse. I get a kind of competitive with games like this one and Baba is You. Where I REFUSE to use guides because damn it that would mean the game wins. I can't let the game win! I'm the one playing a game! So I have to be the winner! And I won't let that win be tainted by guides!!!

So sometimes I've been sitting there beating my head against the wall that is this game and then I figure it out and I'm so damn proud of myself!

Enough of me raving about the puzzles though. Let's talk other more technical stuff.

The art design and sound design are also simple, but still wonderful in their simplicity. It's nice to look at and the music is nice to listen to.

The puzzle design if you don't know what the puzzles actually are is brilliant. You will have several places you need to move boxes and yourself into in order to beat a puzzle. This will generally require moving boxes in and out of each other in a paradoxical way. It's really... REALLY cool. Just pushing boxes into more boxes sometimes almost in a russian nesting doll kind of situation with a box inside a box inside a box as you try to get everything arranged the way you need to.

I mentioned briefly that I've played this on steam deck. It does play REALLY well and I have zero complaints about playing it on the steam deck.

Controls are really simple. Just use WASD to move around.

All in all. Patrick's Parabox is one of the best puzzles games I've played since finding Baba Is You (I keep comparing it because the kind of difficulty they both are makes me compare them). And I've played a lot of puzzles games and many have felt like they fell short in either length or puzzle difficulty (looking at you A Little to the Left).

Patrick's Parabox presents a lot of puzzles, feels like I will get a lot of time with it, and really really good difficulty for the price you pay and I can't recommend it enough. It's not aesthetic. It's not quick. It's not easy.

But it does manage to be chill, simple, yet really difficult in a way that is still REALLY enjoyable.

Fun and mind-bendy, but not hyper-difficult (at least for me). It's a similar feel to games like Stephen's Sausage Roll or Baba Is You or Monster's Expedition, but I didn't find it nearly as difficult as any of them. The meta trick of a box inside itself is used well in many puzzles, although I was just a tiny bit dissatisfied with how they handled some of the edge cases. 

(Some little side thoughts about this last point. In a game like this, once the creators set up the general rules of the universe, there's an obvious way that most things should behave. But there are always those strange little exceptions where the mechanics seem to conflict with themselves, and the creators have to have the game do *something*, even if it's going to seem completely arbitrary. Some games make it so that those exceptions are rare or that no puzzles depend on the arbitrary mechanics they implemented. Some relegate those mechanics to only bonus puzzles or only a few of the hardest end-game puzzles. Parabox just embraces them completely, relatively early in the game, building entire sequences of levels around those arbitrary edge case behaviors, thus creating even more edgy edge cases, and the end result is that those puzzles just don't feel as natural as the others. Don't get me wrong; they're still fun to solve. They're just not quite as satisfying to understand.)

Anyway, I enjoyed Patrick's Parabox quite a bit. The puzzles were just difficult enough to force me to bend my brain around them, but not so hard that I couldn't relax while playing.

Play as a squishy, lil' box named Patrick as he pushes a box into another box to move a box somewhere else while meeting yourself that's in a box along the way in this recursive, Sokoban-style game. This logic, puzzle game is absolutely brilliant!

The game respects players' time by offering bite-sized puzzles with clearly defined concepts. It allows for players to gradually ease themselves into the game by introducing new rules and integrating those mechanics into new puzzles in extraordinarily interesting ways. It even allows for players to jump into the deep end by giving them the option to unlock all the puzzles immediately from the get-go if they're so inclined to do so. Puzzles are cleverly made, and reaching the solutions to the puzzles will always make sense.

The minimalistic art-style and the accompanying cutesy, mellow tunes work well together. They lend themselves to the mood and flavor of the puzzles quite well to deliver a nice, relaxing ambiance. Players shouldn't feel rushed or stressed while they contemplate over their next move(s), and the game does a marvelous job to encourage a stress-free environment until players reach their eureka moment over a particularly elusive solution to a puzzle they may encounter.

This game is excellent for puzzle lovers! Thought and care were put in for the construction of the recursive puzzles, and they are superbly built. 157654215.review:
[h1]脑子快要长出来了，你没见过的套娃推箱子[/h1]

[h1]前言[/h1]
《Patrick's Parabox》又名《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》作为款套娃推箱解密游戏，画面非常可爱，上手非常简单.玩家只需要将笑脸箱子和其他一些箱子推到指定地点，即可通关.但上手游玩后并不像看上去那么简单。

[h1]体验[/h1]
游戏机制内容巧妙程度真的震撼到我，它拥有了经典“推箱子”游戏的一切要素以及不小心把箱子推到墙角陷入死局的普通规则。游戏采用大章节-小关卡制，每个章节内包含多个关卡。在进入章节时会出现章节名称。未解锁的关卡位熄灭状态，解锁后将被点亮.解锁但未完成的会有白色方块在左上角，提示玩家此关卡需要通关.

游戏中有许多操作引导，第一章会在关卡中教会玩家对应的按键提示操作，让玩家学习基础的按键操作。第二章会出现金色独立区域，进入区域可以获取开发者给的解题指导。

游戏中引入了通过探索箱子套着箱子的独特循环系统.将箱子推到彼此内部以及再从内部推出。箱子还可以通过缩放、映射等机制，通过非常意想不到的方式到达其他地方。各种镂空的箱子和嵌套机制，把原本的地图扩展了好几倍，让经典推箱子游戏解法变得更加复杂有趣，不断深入探索过程中，思考当箱子装下它自己会出现什么情况，一路探索更多的机制带来的精彩乐趣。

[h1]总结[/h1]
总体来说，这款属于献给喜欢推箱子玩家的一种智性的浪漫，不需要变得专业或聪明也能体验到它背后更深层的东西，瞥见其中的奥秘。它某种意义上它属于对于40年推箱子类型游戏的完美形态展现出自己的魅力.

156136394.review:
[b]10/10[/b]

To infinity, and double infinity, and triple infinity, and beyond!

[b]What is it:[/b] A recursive sokoban with mind-bending mechanics. Unlike a normal game restricted to what is physically possible, this game breaks reality by allowing you to do things only abstract theoretical math allows.

The game starts simple, with basic boxes you can push, and then gets more and more complicated with new abilities you have to master. First, the boxes you can push are not just simple boxes, but they can be mazes you can enter and exit, with their own puzzles inside, and there are boxes within boxes within boxes. Then you get boxes containing themselves, where going out of the box still puts you inside the box, or can form cycles with box A inside box B inside box C inside box A again. Then you get clone boxes, and flipped clones, and you become the whole level itself, and find out what happens when you push a box out of itself or into itself. What lies beyond infinity? Can you push yourself into yourself? Who shaves the barber who shaves those and only those who don't shave themselves?

The mechanics of the game are incredible and wonderful, yet the game does an excellent job at making you discover them. There are 18 main chapters, each focusing on one aspect of the game, and each containing some easy levels that are there to guide you towards discovering what can be done, a few hard levels that require you to show you really understand what's going on, and a few very hard levels that require a lot of thinking. You don't have to finish all of them to progress, most chapters will let you go to the next chapter if you just finish the basic levels. At the end there is a challenge chapter with really hard levels, this time combining different aspects, plus a few extra puzzles with different mechanics.

[b]How hard is it:[/b] A great variety from easy to very hard.

[b]How long is it:[/b] 364 levels, for more than 10-20 hours of playing.

[b]Level design:[/b] Superb. Very well done "discovery" levels, very hard levels that can be beaten with logic, with non-obvious solutions, and although there are hundreds of levels, most of them are unique. Some levels are quite similar on purpose, to show what a difference a little change makes.

[b]Quality:[/b] Very good. Unlimited undo, reconfigurable controls, clean and pleasant graphics, lots of settings, decent progress achievements, cloud saving, fast and responsive.

[b]Worth the price:[/b] Yes! It's expensive, but it's a very well made game, and a unique experience that must be tried.

[b]Most positive aspect for me:[/b] Mindbending mechanics.

[b]Most negative aspect for me:[/b] Nothing, this game is perfect.

这个游戏，无论从创意、机制引入、关卡设计、玩法深度、完成度方面都非常令人惊艳，我认为是能写进解谜游戏教科书的水平。

游戏的基础是简单的推箱子，再加上嵌套机制，乍看之下平平无奇。但是，游戏层层递进地引入了新奇又合理的机制，比如自指、克隆、无穷大、无穷小乃至多重无穷，使得游戏瞬间变得有趣又烧脑了起来。

本作相对于其他大多解谜游戏做得最出色的，是机制的引入和难度梯度设置，可以算作教科书式的典范。引导性关卡设置非常巧妙，直指机制核心，且每关都引入略有不同的机制，层层递进，值得反复品味；难度设置合理，可能会暂时卡住思考但几乎不会卡关。这是不少其他解谜游戏做不到的。

154507344.review:
今年有个叫cocoon的游戏名声大噪，新奇的套娃机制使其问鼎2023年tga最佳首发独立游戏。但其实论起“套娃”，patrick's parabox能算得上是它的大师兄（而recursed，则更是这个概念的祖师爷）。patrick作为recursed的首席大弟子，有着丝毫不逊色祖师爷的设计，除了赏心悦目的素材、空灵的音乐等优秀的外在，最令人眼前一亮的改变，是把“悖论”这个在recursed中通向隐藏关卡的钥匙进行具象化，使得“创造悖论”本身成为了一种非常普遍的解谜思路（甚至在后期关卡，你能看到许多需要在一种悖论中继续创造另外一种悖论的谜题）……此外，还增加了多重身、镜像反转、夺舍、吞噬等诸多新机制……实在是将师门发扬光大，自成一派。

当然，对于没有玩过recursed或者任何套娃游戏的玩家，我说上面的这些话你肯定会一头雾水。什么叫套娃游戏呢？就好像，你坐在一个水晶球当中，观摩着手上的一个小水晶球；你的视线通过你手上的水晶球，可以看到里面有一个缩小版的你、手里捧着一个更小的水晶球观摩着——不用说，这个更小的水晶球里面，还有一个超级小的你、在观摩一个超级小的水晶球；而你当前所在的水晶球外面，也有一个超级大的你，在观测着当前的你的一举一动，在无穷多个世界中，所有的你的一举一动都是相同的……有一天，你当前所在的这个水晶球出现了裂缝，你想和外面那个超级大的你打个招呼，猜猜看，走出这个裂缝会看到什么？如果你把手中的水晶球丢出缝隙之外，又会发生什么？

这里我就不剧透了（虽然聪明的人联系上下文已经能猜到了答案了）。我非常喜欢patrick的另外一点，是它有一个辅助功能，你只要按键盘7号键，它就展示该关卡的实际组成，告诉你这些神奇的关卡是怎么运作的，包括悖论的产生。ASCII模式十分有利于你在令你眼花缭乱、无穷无尽的视觉冲击下发现事物最简单的本质。这个功能教会了我很多东西。如果你担心一个无限套娃的游戏会吃爆你的内存，不妨看看这个世界的真相，相信你很快就会打消疑虑。

对我而言，这个游戏没有不足之处，只有一些小遗憾，那就是它舍弃了recursed中其他几种有意思的箱子：递归箱（游戏一开始就出现的红箱）、快照箱（从temple开始出现的罐子）、分支箱（从the last tapestry开始出现的大锅）。所以你要问我recursed和patrick哪个的造诣更高明？我会说recursed更高明，因为patrick里的箱子本质上是recursed里的静态箱（也就是冒着绿烟的箱子）的一种特例，而recursed的宝藏依然很多，我们依然可以期待更多类recursed游戏的问世。但patrick的确是个十分优秀的模仿者，我和爱recursed一样爱它。


以下是一些杂乱无章的个人笔记，有关部分游戏机制的探究或者可能的编程原理，涉及到recursed和patrick两个游戏的中度剧透，不建议未玩过两个游戏的玩家观看。


---------------------------------

1、无穷的本质。
[spoiler]如果按了7号键，会发现patrick里的无穷本质就是传送。但你首先必须得把“箱子”和“场景”区分开来。你一开始就处于某个场景中，场景里有不同的箱子，你进入不同的箱子就切换到不同的场景；造成无穷套娃的关键，就是场景中出现一种能传送到当前场景的箱子，我一般把这种箱子称为“缩影”。你从当前场景边缘离开，则会从缩影对应的方向传出来。当你在缩影附近晃悠时，你可以清晰地看到当前场景之外有一个放大版的你也在围绕着当前场景晃悠。[/spoiler]

 1.1、和recursed的绿箱有什么不同？
[spoiler]我在一开始没有认出来缩影其实就是recursed里的绿箱，因为绿箱只代表它不会被刷新湮灭，不代表它内部的场景不会刷新——你从绿箱里面取东西出来、下次再进去会发现绿箱里面的东西刷新了；那你在patrick里有看到过刷新吗？在patrick里你把一个箱子推到另一个箱子里再出来，那个推进去的箱子会消失吗？但是后来我意识到，如果patrick里所有箱子都等同于绿箱呢？就可以解释得通了。

但在编程上，patrick和recursed对于这种箱子的处理肯定是不同的。patrick里的很简单，就是每次离开场景都要储存当前场景里的所有信息，进入场景时再则加载这些信息即可，无论你进入了一堆自相似的场景多少次，你对该场景的存档永远都是同一个；而在recursed里就不能这么做，因为recursed里所有箱子本质都是递归箱（绿箱严格来说不是一种单独类型的箱子）：你进入一个绿箱（该绿箱就指向当前的场景），挪动了场景里一把（非绿色）钥匙位置到左下角，然后进入了下一层绿箱，又把钥匙挪到右下角；然后再进一次绿箱，把钥匙摆回中间……你一共进入了同一个场景3次，你为同一个场景创建了2个ID不同、储存内容不同的存档，这样，当你返回第二、第一层时，就能依次载入这两个存档，就能看到钥匙分别处于右下角、左下角，而不是处于默认的位置。这只是我个人对recursed递归箱的原理猜测，不确定是否有更简洁的办法。[/spoiler]

2、悖论是如何产生的？

 2.1、∞悖论
[spoiler]把缩影推出边缘，则造成∞悖论。因为从地图之外推出去的箱子会从缩影里传出来，可如果那个推出去的箱子是缩影本身，那么就会造成缩影要从缩影里传出来——自己从自己肚子里传出来，这就是∞悖论的由来。[/spoiler]

 2.2、ε悖论
[spoiler]ε悖论也是相似的形成过程。我们知道有一种特殊的箱子最先出现在“clone”关卡（所以我们把这种箱子称为“克隆”）。克隆箱本质上是一种单向传送门，你进入克隆，则你被传送到克隆所指向的场景。有意思的地方来了：如果把一个普通箱子推入它的克隆，然后跟着进入克隆，会发生什么？你就会发现，当你围绕着那个普通箱子转悠时，一个放大版的你在也在围绕着当前场景转悠——这，不就是“缩影”吗？！！为什么会这样？

是的，这就是缩影的本质。你打开ASCII模式能很清晰地观察到这点。你进入一个箱子，你本质上是传送到了另外一个场景；而你进入一个克隆，你同样是传送到了那个场景，区别在于当你从场景中退出时，你只会从箱子出来、而不会从克隆出来。每个箱子一定对应一个场景，进入这个箱子，就进入了箱子所指向的场景；如果这个箱子处于其他场景，那它就是一个普通箱子；而当这个箱子本身处于场景内部的时候，那这个普通的箱子就成为了一个缩影。这就是这个游戏的真相——说到底，一个箱子本来就不可能处于它自身的内部，悖论的根源就在于此。

要造成ε悖论，你可以想象有这样一个箱子：它除了入口，其余的位置都是实体。那么把该箱的克隆推入该箱子（或反过来，把该箱子推入它的克隆），你再从那唯一入口进入，你就造成了ε悖论（infinite enter有很多关卡可供实验）。其实无论是本体推入克隆还是克隆推入本体，你在ASCII模式下观察都没什么区别，因为克隆和本体本质都是传送门，这个过程无非就是把某种传送门推入它们所指向的场景罢了——如果场景内的空间宽裕就不会发生悖论，因为当patrick进入场景时，会自动把前方的箱子推走然后占领原本箱子的位置；可如果箱子后方都是障碍，推不动，则patrick就会缩小自身被迫进入这个箱子——然而这个箱子传送的位置也是当前场景的同一位置，所以就会无限传送，造成了悖论。[/spoiler]

 2.3、多阶∞悖论是怎么实现的？
[spoiler]我对这个机制比较感兴趣。当你把缩影和一阶悖论同时放置于场景边缘的时候，你踏出场景就会从二阶∞箱（如果有）传送出来，更多阶的∞悖论以此类推。不仅如此，若此时你在二阶∞箱附近转悠，你同样可以看到放大版的patrick也在当前场景之外转悠。如果是我写代码的话，我会这样实现：首先，如果当前场景存在缩影，那么就把缩影附近的格子（用额外的摄像机）映射到当前场景周围，这个不难；可如果缩影附近的格子超出了边界（即：缩影处于场景边缘），则①、若场景中找不到下一阶∞箱，则映射虚空；②、若场景能找到下一阶∞箱，且下一阶∞箱对应方向的格子处于场景内，则映射该格的内容；③、若场景能找到下一阶∞箱，但下一阶∞箱对应方向的格子依然处于界外，则回到上一步的判断。[/spoiler]

152903244.review:
"Patrick's Parabox" fait partie des nombreuses variantes "à gimmick" de "[b]Sokoban[/b]", le fameux jeu de puzzles de 1982 où l'on pousse des caisses dans un hangar sans pouvoir les tirer. Ici, le gimmick est spectaculaire et bouleverse la formule en profondeur: les caisses que l'on doit pousser sont aussi des [i]salles[/i] dans lesquelles on peut entrer, et on peut même pousser la salle [i]dans laquelle on se trouve[/i] en une boucle récursive (idée reprise du jeu PICO-8 "[b]Sokosoko[/b]")!

Le jeu est propre, lisible, il tire toutes les conséquences de son idée de base et l'enrichit de diverses mécaniques logiques bien exploitées. Les puzzles sont très nombreux, plus de 350.

Le problème, hélas, est que l'on n'a pas vraiment l'impression de résoudre des puzzles, on se trouve plutôt dans un tutoriel sans fin: chaque puzzle repose en effet sur une seule idée, un seul mouvement clef à effectuer, et si on le trouve tout de suite, le puzzle dure littéralement quelques secondes! On se dit d'abord que c'est temporaire, mais la difficulté ne grimpe jamais jusqu'au générique de fin (!), les puzzles ne deviennent pas plus riches ou plus longs ou plus complexes, on passe simplement à une autre mécanique illustrée par un "puzzle" toujours très court et simpliste.

Pour moi, un bon problème de jeu de puzzles est comme un tour de magie, avec des règles claires et bien assimilées et un level design à l'apparence dépouillée mais qui paraît pourtant insoluble. On y passe du temps, on expérimente, on se demande s'il n'y a pas un bug ou une mécanique qui nous aurait échappé, puis soudain on trouve le "truc" (de préférence élégant), on progresse, on résout finalement le puzzle, et on éprouve alors une immense satisfaction.

Ici, il n'y a qu'une poignée de (courts) puzzles bonus qui correspondent à cette description... "Patrick's Parabox" est comme se rendre à un restaurant prestigieux dans l'espoir d'un bon repas mais n'y recevoir que des apéritifs: de [i]bons[/i] apéritifs, mais qui s'avalent en une bouchée et ne laissent aucune impression durable. Quand on constate qu'un jeu comme "[b]Yugo Puzzle[/b]" (ou tous ses prédécesseurs signés Qrostar) réussit à nous bloquer pendant des heures sur des puzzles incroyablement épurés avec des règles élémentaires, on est bien forcé d'admettre que "Patrick's Parabox" loupe le coche de son potentiel prometteur, avec 90% de mini-puzzles basiques qui donnent une impression de remplissage, 8% de puzzles dont la difficulté repose sur leur extrême abstraction, et 2% de puzzles vraiment satisfaisants.

Le jeu reste bon et peut vous plaire selon ce que vous recherchez, mais pour ma part c'est une déception, et je recommanderais beaucoup d'autres jeux du genre avant lui, surtout à ce prix: "[b]Stephen's Sausage Roll[/b]" bien sûr, "Yugo Puzzle", "[b]Puddle Knights[/b]", "[b]Pipe Push Paradise[/b]", "[b]Sokobond[/b]", "[b]Room to Grow[/b]", "[b]A Good Snowman Is Hard To Build[/b]", "[b]Bonfire Peaks[/b]", ou, sur un concept voisin de salles que l'on manipule comme des objets avec des effets récursifs, le grandiose "[b]Recursed[/b]".

152098853.review:
Patrick's Parabox is quite a beautiful puzzle game to train your brain with. With a simple, elegant design, this Sokoban-style game takes the task of organizing boxes to new heights, or rather, dimensions.

As a kid, I used to love playing Sokoban-style games, there was something so interesting about figuring out how to place each box in its place. When I learned about Patrick's Parabox, I couldn't help but be intrigued by its concept: a Sokoban game where not only can you move boxes around, but sometimes you can fit those boxes inside smaller boxes, or even fit those boxes inside themselves? Sign me right up! After all, there's something that fills me with wonder when dealing with impossible geometry, recursion, and the like, and this game has it in spades.

Now, I've given a general idea of the main gameplay loop: each level is a box, filled with boxes that you have to fit in specific places. The game starts out simple: the first levels are basically your standard Sokoban puzzle. As you progress through each chapter, however, new concepts get introduced, in a very intuitive way, I'd say. The game seems to follow the principle of teaching the player a new mechanic, getting them used to it by putting some spin on it, before moving on to the next mechanic, while still incorporating those previously used.

The lenght of the game is pretty decent, if I recall correctly, there's something like 200+ different levels, including challenges that really make your brain work. Still, it's pretty manageable, I only had to look up a single puzzle, I'll admit, and when I saw the solution, I was facepalming at how simple it was and I couldn't figure it out. So, my advice to you, future player of this game, is to really try to think outside the box, or inside it, or besides it. You'll figure it out eventually.

Artistically speaking, as I mentioned above, the game has a rather simple, yet elegant design, with colours that really pop, so to speak. The soundtrack is also very soothing, perfect for some mental exercise. All in all, I truly enjoyed this game, and I'm a bit ashamed it took me so long to finally sit down and write a proper review for it, as I think everyone should give it a chance. So, go ahead, get this game, and let your brain start working!

无需多言，神作。

这是我的第二款解密作品，也是我的第一个好评。当年阅历低，观点表达偏激。不过在玩了不少解密作品后，我仍愿意称其为神作。或许他的机制没有别的游戏多，或许他缺少关卡编辑器，好点子没能被深挖。但它是一款完美的“游戏”！

简评：别出心裁的创意，恰到好处的引导和难度曲线，无处不在的尤里卡时刻，量大管饱的谜题数量，背后引人深思的逻辑，以及舒适简约的画风和音乐。

游戏玩法&创意
以推箱子为核心，总计18种机制主题，每种主题在一个核心机制下手工设计谜题。由于章节的划分界限，不仅能完全体验一个机制的妙处，同时也是核心解题方法，辅助玩家思考，达到降低逻辑难度的效果。解密过程中不乏尤里卡时刻。

引导&难度
机制简单易懂，难度恰到好处。过关方式并非疑难杂，可能只是跳出常规思维方法进行尝试，这样的思考方式，不失通关的乐趣，也不会因太难，负反馈强烈而劝退。主线采用递进式的解题方式，原有基础上扩充新的思考点，此为引导的妙处，游戏中的凸起等小异常也是对思考的提示，简直是教科书般的引导。同时还有红线标注的较难支线，给予不同玩家自己需要的游戏体验。

深度
在通关主线后，还有30+的挑战关卡。杂糅之前所有学到的机制进行综合解密。更有一些跳出主线运行逻辑的章节。量大管饱，享受思考带来的快乐。

美术&额外
基于逻辑解密的本质，核心创造力当然是机制，但是没有一个好看的皮囊怎么能吸引他人发现美妙的内在呢？好在此款游戏的美术音乐都非常不错，支线内容中也有未经包装的计算机编程内容的实质，通关后还有作者制作游戏的过程和解读。正是这样的细心打磨，让我们看到了可爱有活力的小箱子，在轻松的氛围中解题。

这个游戏从刚出来的时候就知道了，但是一直没舍得买。为什么呢，因为太贵了，原价70，最低也就56。前不久才咬咬牙买了。

现在基本上是打的差不多了，这游戏给我感觉就是非常惊艳，虽然看宣传就知道很惊艳，但是自己上手玩感觉更是别有一番滋味在其中。

游戏性上，差不多是考虑穷尽了所有能够挖掘到的游戏机制，我想不到的他也给我做了，而且难度曲线非常合理，循序渐进的感觉很不错。每一章重点引入一个新机制，十分有趣。解谜有难有容易的，大部分按照一定规律思考和摸索是能够解出来的。当然玩不出来的也可以在b站看攻略。而且难度设计还是很有意思的，前期一些直观的机制可以做的难，后期一些抽象的机制（比如无穷，循环）就反而很容易，估计是特意做关把难度做的均匀一些。毕竟抽象的机制我觉得完全可以设计很复杂很逆天的关出来，可是没有。总之，是一款非常棒的解谜游戏，玩下来你会觉得完全值得这56或者70块钱。（老守财奴了）

最后，游戏的画风和音乐也很不错，画面很简约可爱，音乐也很休闲轻快悦耳，配合或简单或难的休闲解密是很配的。所以，我对这款游戏非常满意！

不过，嗯，对大家推荐的话，我还是建议大家看看自己对解密游戏的喜好和擅长程度。虽然画风可爱关卡设计友好，但是还是有硬核的烧脑解密的，是解谜的菜的那绝对值得入，但是不善于解密的恐怕会体验不佳。

145513669.review:
入れ子構造というコンセプトとちょっとずつある小さなギミックだけでものすごく奥深いパズルゲームになってる。
箱の中の箱が永久に続く「∞」という概念が自分にとっては非常に興味深く、直感だけでは解けないが、論理的に考えても混乱し出して、最終的にはなんとなく、無限とはこういうものだから、みたいな感覚で溶けるようになっていた。
ゲームはクリアしたが、まだ、全てのステージをクリアしたわけではないためまだまだ遊ぶつもりだが、クリアするだけならそこまで時間はかからないと思う。パズルが好きな人には非常におすすめのゲーム。
パズルが好きでなくとも、「∞」の概念や最後の方に出てくる「多重無限」の概念は非常に面白いのでぜひ遊んでみてほしい。

ステージの構成も非常によくできており、徐々に徐々にギミックが足されていって気がつけばとても難解なパズルに挑戦している自分がいて心地よい。
パズルゲームあるあるだが、解けないステージに直面したら飛ばしてどんどん先に行ってあとで戻ってくると簡単に解けたりする、絶妙な難易度だと私は感じた。
グラフィックはシンプルでサウンドも各ステージごとに個性はあるが落ち着いていて、ゆったりと遊べるゲームだった。残りのやり込み要素も楽しみだ。

2023/10/3追記：クリア後のチャレンジステージ、かなり骨があった。解き方を見つけるまでがかなりキツイが、解法を発見した時の達成感は素晴らしい。22時間もかかったが全ステージ自力で頭を捻って答えに辿り着けてよかった。

141532713.review:
Bon, bien avancé (pas fini, mais ne risque pas d'arrivé de fait) et je ne suis pas si émerveillé que ça.

Le concept est sympa et bien exploité, rien à dire là-dessus. Après, même si chaque puzzle a sa petite idée nouvelle (et chaque chapitre sa grosse idée nouvelle), je trouve une certaine lassitude qui s’installe, une sensation de redondance malgré tout. Chaque nouvelle idée me parait pas incroyable en fait, même si « bien vue » dans l’absolue, ne renouvelle pas les enjeux (à part la récursivité, mais ça c’est le tout début), voire est parfois un peu parachutée. Et puis le jeu se montre assez fermé / obtus par moment, interdisant des choses sans raison autre que « nan mais j’ai pas prévu/envie que tu fasses ça alors je te bloque dans une zone vide sortie de nulle part ; réessaye autrement ». C’est quand même là qu’il trouve pour moi ça plus grosse limite, surtout quand les puzzles se la jouent « suffit de rester cohérent et rationnel et tu vas trouver » mais à certains moment « ah oué mais nan, ah ah, ça oublie, j’y avais pas pensé / c’est pas ça que je voulais ».

Au final autant de points où des puzzle-games autrement plus recommandables comme Baba is You brillent à des niveaux bien supérieur.

La progression reste plutôt exemplaire, n’imposant que les puzzles introduisant les nouvelles mécaniques et approches, et laissant toutes les exploitations avancées comme optionnelles, pour des digressions qui vont parfois assez loin (mais ne constituent donc jamais d’obstacles bloquant, juste là pour qui veut approfondir).

________

Mais arrivé au puzzle 141, je ne trouve pas que le jeu bouleverse trop son concept à qqs moments que ce soit. Aucun puzzle ne m’as semblé franchement difficile jusque là, et aucun m’a mis le cerveau à l’envers et m’a bluffé comme a pu le faire Baba is You à de multiples reprises.

Y’a que l’idée rapidement introduite de récursivité qui me parait bien cool, mais finalement très superficiellement exploitée à mon sens (voire mal exploitée assez régulièrement, quand le jeu te pose des interdits injustifiés … :|).

Il n’en reste pas moins sympa, et s’avère hautement accessible ne serait-ce que du fait que seuls les puzzles basiques sont nécessaires pour avancer, toutes les utilisations un peu évoluées rentrent dans les puzzles optionnels. Mais plutôt du genre dispensable, tellement mieux existe ailleurs.

139675409.review:
总评：解谜玩家可以试试的优秀作品。

我最想赞美的不是作者的创意，而是作者的关卡编排：
1.每个章节有确定的主题，前几关算是这一章的教学关卡，思维比较套路化。
2.每一章的关卡都被编排成了树状结构，在树上排布的关卡有连续的也有分离的。连续的关卡有思维上的关联，游玩时也是无缝衔接，难度阶梯式上升，玩得非常过瘾。
3.作者在一些章节放置了字符形式的关卡，基本上解答了“这样的创意是怎么编程实现的？”这个问题。有点想要写一个阉割版的Parabox作为程序设计大作业（）

说完优点，聊聊缺点：
1.连续关卡难度上升是没错，但一个章节关卡还是太多了，当离开一个章节时，通常会感觉厌倦。
2.尤其批评后面的“多重无穷小”和“多重无穷大”的关卡，刚刚见到概念时感觉是新奇的，但是玩几关之后会发现游戏实际上没有什么变化，很无聊。作者在这里没能给我比较好的游戏体验，感觉作者才尽了。
3.有不少关卡的难度上升不是由于思维上的创新，而是由于步骤的繁琐，这或许是很多解谜游戏的通病？
4.性价比问题：你自己看着办，这玩意儿卖得还挺贵的。


一周目实际用时大约11小时全部通关，最近正在刷二周目。
