おまけ含め全クリ済み。良ゲーです。子どもにもおすすめできます。無料Demo版あり。

12のステージ（+おまけ）で構成されており、各ステージはそれぞれ異なるルールをもっています。次のステージに行く為には全てパズルを解く必要はなく、ステージ中の６～８割を解けばＯＫです。
多くのレビューで触れられている通り、このゲームの良さは「易しくはないが、複雑ではない」ということ。全てのパズルにおいて、解に向かうためのプロセスは決して長くありません。解に必要なのは、その手段の適切な順序です。わかれば30秒で解けます。パズルにありがちな「プレイヤー置いてけぼりで問題の難易度が急に跳ね上がる」が、このゲームにはありません。

プレイヤーが新しいルールに触れたときの驚きと発見、（ほんの少しの忍耐を要するかもしれない）試行錯誤の末にパズルを解いたときの嬉しさや喜びに重きを置いていることがよくわかります。詰まったら今できること、やりたいこと、実行した結果等を紙に書き出してみたり、あるいは思い切ってゲームをやめて寝てしまえば、次の機会には解けていることでしょう。または、パートナーやフレンドと一緒に解いてみたり、お子さんと悩んでみるのも良いと思います。

頭の回転が早い人であれば10時間かからずクリアできそうなので、人によっては時間対費用が見合わないかもしれません。しかし、このゲームでしか体感できないであろうこともあります…私はパズルゲームで「ここはどこ？」ではなく、「何ここ？」と恐怖や次元を感じたのはこのゲームが初めてです。レビューの少なさに悲しみを覚えて、初めてレビューを書きました。多くの人におすすめできる、丁寧にデザインされた良いゲームです。

As the levels progress, new mechanics are introduced such as pushing a box outside of itself, going inside of boxes, and even possessing them! This game really tests your problem-solving skills and each new level really tests your brain. And while it may take a while to solve a level (or even days), you'll eventually get that "aha" moment and know how to solve it instantly. It's a very rewarding game and gives you the sense that "you did that all by yourself with no hints whatsoever!" The soundtrack also fits the mood of the game as well, whether it be taking your time with puzzles to hardcore "thinking" music for moments like "How do I solve this," and "So if I move this block here..." and other moments like that. If you're looking for a very casual puzzle game with a relaxing soundtrack to get by the day, I would definitely try Patrick's Parabox! Each level will cure your boredom right from the start!

136137008.review:
I am not a fan of Sokoban puzzle games. I think too many in this subgenre rely on irritatingly specific solutions and end up being more about positioning yourself rather than working with a game's mechanics to understand a solution. Add in elements of spatial uncertainty and Patrick's Parabox sounds nightmarish by construction. But after checking out his previous game (Linelith, which I highly recommend), I needed to give this title a fair shake, and it is easily the best Sokoban game you can play right now.

Right off the bat, Patrick's Parabox doesn't restrict you as a player. You frequently have free reign to solve puzzles in whatever order you want, and you only need to solve the bare minimum of puzzles in one area to move onto the next. Even when I was hopelessly stuck, I never felt trapped since I had many other conundrums to work out instead. There are also options if needed to unlock all puzzles and solve as you wish, but I personally felt content with the pace of the game's natural process.

Patrick's Parabox maintains the Sokoban standards of pushing blocks into a desired position, but the main gimmick is that many boxes are collapsable on themselves or can create infinite loops, allowing you to bend space and push blocks and access corners you normally couldn't. I was consistently surprised at the depth some boxes could provide mechanically, and with over 300 puzzles, there are tons of extremely clever ideas that are gradually and intellectually expanded upon. An early idea teaches you that boxes will move into the center when pushed, and soon you will be exiting one looping paradox to use this center idea to shove a box into an impossible pathway. The simple presentation is always a misdirect from the complex, but never unfair thought process you must have to find a way to a correct solve. I was floored by how little a puzzle gave you to finish it and how much you could actually do with the tools you're handed, but I was equally stumped as often, finding myself toying with directions and boxes in any way I could. 

Patrick's Parabox is a marvelous title. There is no story; this is a pure puzzler. And while some of the late and post game puzzles are borderline neuroticly difficult, I really enjoyed reaching the credits on PP and hope to play more innovative games from Patrick Traynor in the future.

This game is a serious master piece in game design.  I know that's a bold statement for a game that on the surface is about pushing blocks around.

The thing is, this game shares a design style similar to one of my other favorite designed games -- The Witness.

See, there's no tutorials.  No hand overt hand holding.  But it's not a brutal "screw you, figure it out" motif.  They game TEACHES you subtly.  Every new level is comprised of a dozen or more individual puzzles.  Each level builds on a theme and new mechanic, and the mechanics are CLEVER.

Each puzzle within a level are roughly sequential, and they are well designed such that they gradually get harder, but teach you more about what you can do with the new mechnic.  But you can also usually skip a few if you get stuck.  There are also optional ones outside the main solution path where you can really go for the brain twisting.

All in all, it's a very good pick up and play game, and is constantly delighting you in new ways of solving the puzzles.  Just when you think "what else could they do with boxes?" they come up with some other mind warping mechanic that makes you glad AND sorry you asked.

Definitely worth its price.

这是我迄今为止见过最nb的游戏创意。作者在推箱子这一经典玩法上引入了“嵌套”的概念。但是，作者的天才之处在于，游戏仅仅依靠引入这一个如此简洁的概念，就做出了12个类别，364个关卡，而且关卡各具创意，毫无重复之感。论玩法的深度，游戏从“嵌套”开始，发展为“多重嵌套”、“自我嵌套”，再到“无穷大”、“无穷小”，甚至“多重无穷”。再说玩法的广度，游戏在“嵌套”概念这一主干的基础上，又引出了“透明箱子”“不同长宽比的箱子”“克隆”“反向穿越”等多种分支玩法。可以说，作者不仅发现了这一游戏创意，而且几乎穷尽了这一创意所能开发出的玩法。

在我的游玩过程中，我玩得越深入，就越能感受到我和作者的差距。因为每当我自以为发现了一个新机制或者bug，就会发现作者不仅考虑到了它，甚至基于它开发了新玩法！我在游戏中所有的“灵光一闪”，作者都比我想得深远得多。等到游戏后期开始引入“无穷”的概念，我的心中已经只剩下了对作者的敬意。能开发出这种游戏的人，必然有着深厚的数学功底。

等到我真正通关，随着通关动画回顾整个游戏，我才蓦然感受到，作者以极其和缓的难度梯度，让我在十几个小时的游玩时间内由浅入深地学习（是的，学习）了大量集合论、范畴论的数学知识。

一个箱子夺舍了另一个箱子。

一群箱子玩起了吃豆人。
一群箱子玩起了拼图游戏。

空间、步数、方向、嵌套关系……
每一个要素都如齿轮般严丝合缝，组装出了350多件各具特点的艺术品。
在这个箱子里，我见过了万千宇宙，览遍了无数风景，跨过了最远的距离。
而这一切，都发生在一个箱子里。
顺便，这么神奇的箱子，比平平无奇的拉杆箱还便宜。

认真说一句，作为一个解谜游戏，几乎每一个关卡都有一个中心思想，并且能带动玩家去理解关卡的设计思路，真的很不错。这样的关卡让我觉得我是清醒的带着脑子去玩的，而不是不知所云只能胡乱尝试最后精疲力竭。每次理解了关卡的核心思想时，都有一种顿悟的惊喜和掌控的满足，虽然全程挑战不断，但总体来说难度曲线很合适，成就感和挑战性并存。

另外画面和音乐也很不错，简约而可爱，动画流畅，表达直观，很好地缓解了解谜时的疲劳，也成功地化抽象为具体，降低了游戏的难度。

132113865.review:
不用看，解谜游戏玩家无脑入手就对了。

《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》是由Patrick Traynor制作发行的一款以推箱子玩法的解谜游戏。对于推箱子解谜游戏，相信大部分玩家小学时候有在学习机上面玩过，虽然操作上简单不过依旧可以玩得很入迷。若你也跟我一样有沉迷过推箱子解谜游戏的话，那么本作绝对能够给你带来更加有意思、同时也更加烧脑的推箱子解谜。

制作者在游戏商店页面中提到本作在2020年独立游戏节中获得设计卓越奖项，就游戏体验来说个人认为本作确实也值得这个奖。一般的推箱子游戏都是设定在一个固定的场景中，玩家只要把箱子推到对应的位置就OK了，而本作就如其游戏名字一般，毕竟是箱子无穷奇遇嘛，其箱子是一层套一层，箱子套着箱子、箱子套着箱子多重箱子的循环式套娃解谜。

其套娃的特性体现在，从最开始只有普通的实心方块变成了有内置通道的方块，玩家需要利用好内置通道的特性，将实心方块先推进至内置通道的方块，在将含有实心方块的内置通道方块移动的正确前置位，最后再进入导内置通道的方块中将实心方块推出，放置到标记好的位置上。这还是最基础的套娃，后续的关卡中还会有更多的新机制给玩家进行思考挑战，比如放大场景跟缩小场景的结合，玩家在方块内部的行动，场景内的方块也会体现出来，如何利用好方块的出入口来完成解谜则是玩家需要考虑的因素。

《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》提供了超过350多个关卡，玩家需要完成每个关卡中规定的关卡数量后才能解锁进入到新的关卡，就游戏的耐玩性来说是相当充足的。不过考虑到本作的烧脑程度不低，为了让玩家也能够体验到后续关卡，制作组在设置中加入了解锁全关卡游玩的选项，虽说每个大关卡中的小关卡都是对应着本关卡的主题，但个人建议还是循序渐进。前面的关卡都完成不了了，对于机制不熟悉的话，后面的话就更加折磨了。

游戏性方面表现优秀，音画体验的话也同样让人满意，极简画风观感清新，音乐部分则是如制作组所说一般令人心旷神怡，如果有单独的原声集推出一定要入一份，很适合工作学习时听。总的来说作为一款解谜游戏《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》的游戏质量在线，充足的挑战性也能够满足解谜游戏爱好者的游玩需求，强烈推荐解谜游戏玩家入手游玩。

132098224.review:
What a great puzzle game! The premise is pretty ingenious: if boxes can contain boxes, what if a box contains itself? This self-referential aspect of the puzzles is interesting from the start, but it's even more amazing to see the consequences developed through the course of the game. Seeing new, unexpected behavior emerge from rules I thought I had grasped frequently made me smile.
Several other reviews mention the pleasant difficulty curve - I wholeheartedly agree! It's great how the game manages never to ask too much, yet to stay engaging at the same time.
One detail I quite enjoyed is the option to select between different graphical styles (in most levels). I'm particularly fond of the ASCII option. Although it's not the most beautiful, it makes it easy to appreciate what's going on behind the scenes.
All in all, it's among the best puzzle games I've played, and I had a wonderful time with it. Now to figure out how to create custom levels...

131513580.review:
这款独立游戏可以说把创新和想象力发挥到了极致，把推箱子的故事演绎到了极致，推到后面就是箱子推我，我推箱子，我与箱子合二为一，甚至可以从一个空间穿越到另一个空间，非常考验想象能力和思维连贯。
先说优点吧画面精简可爱非常Q弹，不显草率也没有故作纷繁，转场和过度自然，没有贴图塑料感。音乐节奏较好。关卡数量和模块设计够多，由简到难，就算不会附加关卡也可以只通过主线关进入下一大关。设计合理耐人寻味。
缺点几乎没有，但是也有些建议和给未购买玩家的参考，建议有以下几点，游戏音乐方面曲目数量有点少，配不上这三百多关卡。其次游戏定价略高，并且较少打折。最后是希望作者可以给出内置的解谜答案，或者教学视频，有些较难的关卡实在不好通过。
给玩家的建议是游戏因为题材设定主要为推箱子，所以游戏性较为单一，通关所有主线以后挑战和附录关容易让人丧失耐心，如果没有耐心可以再做斟酌，毕竟游戏价位不低。如果对思考谜题很感兴趣并且乐于挑战，可以放心购买。

131415893.review:
太好玩啦
个人观点：传统推箱子可以视为箱子和推箱人所有可能位置构成的集合，推箱人的单步推动构成该集合到自身的一个映射；悖论箱是一个不同的映射，将原来某些会碰到墙壁从而使元素映射到自身的情形更改为了映射到另一个不同的元素，具体映射规则采用了递归来构造。此外，对于无穷递归（出口和入口）的情形，特别定义了inf和epsilon。这些无穷元素本来是不属于传统推箱子的位置集合的。因此，悖论箱实际上可看作对传统推箱子位置集合和映射的延拓，采用同样的描述方式甚至可能构建出更加扭曲和抽象的非递归类型的推箱子。不过找到和递归一样自然和纯粹的表现形式恐怕也很难了；等全成就的时候，再回顾一下看看有没有新的理解。
--
完成所有谜题了，递归之外定义的特殊映射规则确实存在，比较典型的是吞食主题的谜题，因为不熟悉机制在挑战里的几个谜题上卡了好久，一个是推动箱子A带动B这种情形，是A吃B还是B吃A；另一个是当箱子的缺口不在正中间、而是在侧边时，和另一个箱子互吃的交互方式。这类情形必须要专门指定规则，而且显然存在多种合理的映射。
感觉吞食和非均匀格子间转移的谜题反而更难一些，也许就是因为对规则不够熟悉吧，递归的表现形式相比起来直观很多，反而容易理解。

[i]Patrick's Parabox[/i] is an extremely well-designed puzzler with a great learning curve, and puzzles that intrigue and delight instead of stumping and frustrating. It has super audio design and cute aesthetics. But most importantly...

[h1]...it's friendly to people with bad spatial imagination![/h1]

Problem with puzzle games deriving from [i]Sokoban[/i] is that way too often turn up the difficult at latter puzzles by just making the space intricate. For example, [i]Baba Is You[/i] eventually turns from a delightful game about manipulating rules (where the main difficulty is figuring out the sequence of rule changes) into a boring game of complicated box pushing (where the main difficulty is distinguishing zigzagzagzagzigzagzigzagzagzagzagzig from zigzigzagzagzigzagzigzigzagzagzagzig).

[i]Patrick's Parabox[/i] [b]avoids this completely[/b]. It always gives you enough room to focus on the high-level stuff, has an Undo and Redo[b](!)[/b] buttons, and its levels have a grokkable size.

If your spatial imagination is bad enough that [i]Antichamber[/i] is intuitive to walk through but you keep getting lost in [i]Half-Life 2[/i], this game is for you.

(Also, I bought the game [i]immediately after[/i] finishing the demo. Demos work!)

Patrick's Parabox is a pure puzzle game. The controls are simple, the graphics minimal, and the concepts bend your brain in a way it has never been done before. There is no story or platforming or mechanics to really speak of, only puzzles.
The difficulty progression is near perfect. Nothing ever seems too easy or too difficult (until perhaps you reach the post-endgame challenges), but almost everything requires you to think through the puzzle and work through it logically. The additions of complicating ideas such as recursion and infinities all feel natural and logical conclusions of the world this game lives in. Nonetheless, this game has bent my brain in more ways than one and I was left speechless a number of times upon figuring out the solution to a given puzzle.

Playing Patrick's Parabox, I am continually reminded of Baba Is You. Both games feel very similar, have similar logical puzzles with no story to speak of, with similar levels of polish and difficulty. If you've played and enjoyed Baba is You, you will certainly enjoy Patrick's Parabox, and vice versa. If you've not played either game, and enjoy puzzles, I would certainly recommend playing both.

A [b]very[/b] quick puzzle game if you know what you're doing - ~100 minutes is all it took me to finish it. Yet there's no way I'm going to refund this, it was thoroughly worth every penny!

The basic premise: It's Sokoban, except you can enter the boxes you push. Boxes can also contain themselves. Shenanigans ensue.

There's a few gimmicks, like turning the player into other blocks (fun), pushing blocks into the player (great), turning into walls (a gimmick that I hope to never see again in my life), and shunting around subworlds in weird and wacky ways. I played the demo of this a year or so ago, and was disappointed that something I stumbled upon early seemed to just be coded out for convenience... I was really glad that it got expanded upon literally tenfold!

There's a few iffy worlds: Center is just fiddly, Clone feels like a gimmick that was just invented to make some worlds possible. Cycle is also mediocre and feels like a totally different game. But that's 3 "misses" out of 15 worlds, the rest of which are great.

Overall, this is a fun concept that thoroughly explores the design space of "what if reality was Sokoban, crossed that one scene from Futurama where they end up with a box that contains their own universe". Definitely recommend!

A fun little puzzle game. You start out just the bare basics of pushing blocks around, and with every world a new mechanic is introduced and focused on, with a few simple levels to demonstrate the new gimmick and let you get a feel for how it works. 

If you're more of a casual puzzler then just stick to the middle path and go to the next world once you've beaten the required amount of levels. But if you feel like challenging yourself then there are red and blue levels which usually force more thought and difficulty. 

There is no story to miss, so you can take the game at your leisure. 100% each world before moving on, or only do the bare minimum to get to the next world and see what else the game has to offer. 

Once you beat the final world you unlock some bonus areas, which involve some puzzles with unique mechanics which solely work in those mini-worlds, as well as more difficult challenge puzzles. 

I 100% the game, and some puzzles can really throw you for a loop learning how to make the solution work. While sometimes I'd get stuck, come back to it later on, and see that the solution was much simpler than I thought and I just needed to work backwards from how I thought the final solution should be.

This was a real fun experience that I'd heavily recommend for either a casual or an experienced puzzler.

125565674.review:
Let's be honest: nobody likes looking up solutions to puzzles, and nobody likes leaving puzzles unfinished, and nobody likes staring at a puzzle for hours, having your brain operate on 42069 teraflops. But if a puzzle game is too easy, then it becomes boring and there's no satisfaction.

Patrick's Parabox solves this conundrum by having excellent puzzle design, a very fine learning curve with lots of teachable moments, and deciding to err on the side of being too easy rather than too hard. Don't worry; it'll still make your brain hurt in that good way... okay, I think I'd better explain myself.

[h1]Difficulty[/h1]
I don't consider myself particularly good at puzzle games; I managed to "beat" Baba is You (got to the credits) with only looking up solutions maybe 2-3 times, but every late game puzzle took me ... a pretty long time. Sometimes hours. At some point it stops being fun. 

Parabox, on the other hand... I managed to 100% of the main game (all puzzles, minus the post-game challenges) in 12 hours. The longest I was stuck on a puzzle was 15-20 minutes, tops, and most I've solved in around 2. I mean, I have around 260 puzzles solved, so that'd make it around 3 mins per puzzle on average?

Point is, it's much easier. Once you hit the "aha" moment, setting everything up to work the way you want to is quick and pleasant. Still, no puzzle was so easy that I'd instantly know the answer just by looking at it. If I had to describe my "brain flow" here, it'd be something like this:

Look -> Hmm -> Messing around -> Ok -> Sherlock Mode -> Elementary, my dear Patrick -> Solve

I hope that makes sense. Let's talk about the learning curve, since that's what makes the difficulty so pleasant.

[h1]Learning Curve[/h1]
The game's split into thematic worlds, which all use a central mechanic as a foundation. Of course, latter worlds include mechanics from previous worlds to keep things interesting - but they don't overuse them, and many optional side puzzles have mechanics that are unique to this particular set.

Every world has the "main" path - easy puzzles which mostly just show you how a new mechanic works. Sometimes two puzzles have essentially the same solution, just are flipped around a bit; but that ensures that you really get it. Once you're done with those, you can try the "red" or even "blue" puzzles which are, in my opinion, where the real meat of the game is - they test your understanding of the mechanics, and are rather  non-trivial. But the good news is that you don't need to do them if you don't want to.

So: do you want a brain workout, or would you like to just be taken on a magic [strike]carpet[/strike] box ride through a theme park of guided "aha" moments? The game's got you covered either way. No shame.

[h1]Puzzle Design[/h1]
You might think that the trailer showcases this part quite well. You'd be wrong; because it gets so, so much [i]crazier[/i] than that. What happens if you put a box inside itself, and then leave it? That's simple, you reappear inside, at the edge of where the "inner" box is. But what if you tweaked that situation and put the inner box's edge so that it lines up with the outer edge... and then try to leave? You'd be stuck in an infinite loop of leaving into something that doesn't exist. 

The game just shrugs at that paradox and calls it "infinity". It usually breaks the puzzle, but not always. The game's called "Parabox" because it's all about using and abusing such paradoxes... with boxes. And that infinity thing is arguably the simplest weird thing you'll encounter here, by the way.

And the best part? The puzzle design not only explains those weird concepts very well, it also twists them around and puts them in such insane configurations that you can't help but be amazed at the sheer [i]genius[/i] required to craft this insane concoction. A prime example of the divine creativity only a solodev can wield.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Flaws... there really isn't much to complain here. The biggest "problem" I can think of is that there doesn't seem to be a way to zoom on a controller, you have to use the mouse. Also, if you're smarter than me (or just good at puzzle games), you'll probably find the game too easy - but I still think you'd have fun.

In a nutshell, I'd say that this game has the mechanical depth of Baba is You but the difficulty and pacing of Portal. In other words - if you even remotely enjoy puzzle games, this is an absolute must play.

One of the few puzzle games I've played lately that I really enjoyed.

(legend: o; neutral, -; negative, +; positive)

What it does do:

+ relatively simple mechanics that are easy to pick up and hard to master
+ allows for 100%ing without breaking an arm and a leg (as far as I've seen at least, I'm not quite there yet)
+ epsilon and infinity are nice math jokes that are actually correctly applied, but I figure that's a plus just for me
+ it has five or so hints that basically amount to "Don't Panic", which is nice despite not being written in large red friendly letters
+ proper recursion, no time travel, y'know, it just behaves as I expect it to (as a programmer)
+ hard puzzles
+ funky retro levels that feel like a CLI version of the game which I find very attractive <3

What it doesn't do:

+ does not hold your hand every step of the way
o it actually doesn't hold your hand at all, it just kicks you into free fall and lets you figure out what to do (which works *most* of the time, but not always)
- some mechanics remain entirely unexplained (mostly precedence for some actions) which is hard to get right
- it's not very long
o there is no story whatsoever
+ it is not a Portal spin-off (yes, this deserves its own point in this genre)
+ most puzzles that melt your brain are not the required main puzzles so you can skip them

A few levels are really awkward to the point of feeling like IEEE 754 floating point rounding errors, but hey, it makes for a nice change of pace for a dozen levels.

Overall I liked it and I think it's worth the ~20 bucks, albeit a bit expensive it is nice to see a game excel in this genre without going over board, being a portal spin-off, or being incomprehensible, YMMV.
If in doubt wait for a 50% discount, 10 bucks would be absolutely worth the buy IMHO.

제작자의 센스가 돋보이는 게임 설계와 제목 선정. 솔직히 게임 플레이하는 동안에는 모순이 그리 주요한 주제가 아니다. 많은 플레이어들이 리뷰를 남겼듯이, 모순보다는 "재귀"가 핵심적인 게임 플레이의 주축이 된다. 그렇다면 이 게임의 제목은 왜 "Parabox"인가? 

 이렇게 잘 빚어진 퍼즐게임을 플레이할 때 우리는 제작자가 만든 세계에 흠뻑 빠지는 경험을 하게 된다. 우리가 물리법칙 하에서 걷고 뛰는 것처럼, 플레이어는 제작자가 만든 규칙 안에서 캐릭터를 조작해야만 한다. 좋은 퍼즐 게임일수록 그 규칙은 참신하면서도, 직관적이다. 처음엔 낯설지만 몇 번의 시행착오를 통해 익숙해지게 된다. 그렇게 제작자의 규칙을 학습한 채로 제작자가 만든 놀이터에서 뛰노는 것이 게임의 본질이라고 할 수 있을 것이다.

 허나 그러한 규칙을 만드는 것은 정말 어렵다. 참신한 규칙은 플레이어를 끌어당기지만, 그만큼 참신한 오류들을 야기한다. 그러기에 제작자는 섬세하게 규칙을 다듬으며 그러한 오류들을 다듬어야만 한다. 이는 단순히 버그를 잡는 것과는 아주 다른 이야기이다. 규칙과 규칙이 맞닿으며 부딪히는, "모순"이 생기는 부분들이 존재하며, 제작자는 그러한 모순이 생기지 않게 규칙을 수정하거나 새로운 규칙을 도입한다.

 Baba is you라는 게임으로 예시를 들면, BABA IS WIN과 BABA IS NOT WIN이라는 두 문장은 통념상 공존할 수 없는 문장이다. 즉, NOT이라는 규칙을 도입하려다가 모순이 생겨버린 것이다. 이러한 경우 제작자는 NOT이라는 규칙을 도입하는 것을 포기할 수도 있으며, 맵 디자인 상에서 두 문장이 동시에 만들어지는 경우가 생기지 않게끔 할 수도 있다. 허나 만일 그랬다면 Baba is you는 지금의 명성만큼 훌륭한 게임이 되지 못했을 것이다. 우선 너무나 당연하게도 제작자가 전자와 같이 대처했다면 (NOT 규칙 포기) 현 Baba is you에 존재하는 수많은 레벨디자인들이 존재할 수 없었을 것이다. 그리고 후자와 같이 대처했다면? 할 수 있는 무엇이든지 전부 다 시도해보고싶은 것이 플레이어의 심리인 법인데 , 이를 못하게 하면 얼마나 답답하겠는가! 이러한 경우 좋은 게임이라고 보기 어려울 것이다. 자유롭게 뛰놀 수 있는 직관적인 규칙이 몰입감을 형성하기 때문이다. Baba is you에서는 아주 간단한 규칙을 추가함으로써 이러한 모순을 극복했다. 이는 아래와 같다. 

 "NOT을 제외하고는 주어와 서술어가 모두 일치하는 두 명제가 있을 경우, NOT이 포함된 명제가 우선적으로 적용된다 (즉 NOT이 없는 명제는 무효처리된다.)"

 Baba is you를 플레이해보지 않은 사람이라면 뭐이리 지저분해.. 라고 생각할 수도 있겠지만, 실제로 플레이해보면 한 두번의 시행착오만으로도 거부감없이 체화가 되는 규칙이다. 모순을 극복하기 위해 Baba is you만의 새로운 규칙을 만들었으며, 머리가 (과할 정도로) 비상한 제작자는 이 규칙이 빛을 발하는 수많은 레벨 디자인을 선보였다. 

 그렇다면 우리의 Parabox는? 박스 안에 박스가 들어가는 "재귀"라는 개념을 정말이지 맛깔나게 차용했지만, 그 과정에서 치명적인 오류(모순)가 생겨버리는데...  바로 재귀박스가 직접 재귀박스 밖으로 나가는 그 순간, 재귀박스는 재귀박스 밖으로 나가는 과정(연산)을 무한히 반복하게 된다. 재귀박스는 재귀박스의 밖으로 나가고 이 액션으로 인해 재귀박스 다시 재귀박스의 밖으로 나가고....... 고등학교 수학 극한에서 배웠듯이 무한이라는건 수가 아닌 현상이자 과정이다. 허나 그렇다고 해서 무한히 반복되는 연산과정에 의해 과부하되어 게임이 꺼져버렸거나, R을 눌러 게임을 다시 시작하라는 오류메세지가 화면에 나타났다면 이 게임은 지금과 같이 훌륭한 평가를 받지 못했을 것이다. 다시 말하지만 짓궂은 플레이어는 그게 무엇이 됐든 간에 씹고 뜯고 맛보고 즐기고 싶어하는 법이고, 훌륭한 개발자는 자신도 그러한 플에이어임을 알기에 이러한 욕구를 해소시키고 싶어하는 법. Parabox의 개발자 Patrick 역시 훌륭한 개발자였고, 그는 호기롭게 이 난관을 넘는다.

 "무한마저 박스로 표현하는 것". 그는 플레이어가 게임에 오롯이 집중할 수 있게 lim x->infinity을 어디 한 구석에 숨겨둔 채, 과감히 무한을 x(박스)로 표현한 것이다. 개발자는 여기에 한 술을 더 떠서, x를 거듭제곱하기에 이른다. 그로 인해 x의 지수는 차원이라는 개념으로 표현되어 게임에 메타적인 재미를 더하였고, 나아가 무한소(입실론)라는 개념까지도 과감하게 선보일 수 있었다. 무한이라는 개념에 반항하는 듯 하면서도 수학적으로 그 논리가 타당해보이기까지 하니, 이 얼마나 과감하고 멋진 해결책인가! 실제 플레이 과정에서도 게임의 이러한 paradox(어찌보면 '이 게임만의 제멋대로인 규칙')는 아주 직관적으로 우리의 뇌에 받아들여진다. 너무 직관적이여서, "왜 이 게임의 제목에 Paradox가 들어갔을까" 라고 리뷰를 남길만큼..

 필자가 언급한 것들 이외에도 Patrick's parabox라는 놀이터 안에는 그대만 준비되었다면 얼마든지 갖고 놀 수 있는 장난감들이 가득하다. "이렇게 하면 어떻게 될까?" 하는 기대감을 실망시키지 않을 훌륭한 게임이니, 망설이지 말고 도전해보는 것을 추천한다.

One of the most mind-bending things I've ever played—maybe [i]the[/i] most ever. Though this game doesn't get extremely complex with its puzzle solutions, the puzzles themselves are so abstract and fun to learn and mess around with that it doesn't really need to. Plus, the collection of challenge levels at the end do provide some high difficulty. But what really makes this game shine so tremendously well is how it grounds theoretical physics into reality, represented clearly. I won't go into detail for spoilers, but the game gets much stranger and crazier, especially near the end, with mechanics that take some serious thinking to wrap your head around and which are mind-blowing to attempt to do so. Yet despite that, the game is able to ease players into these mechanics so smoothly with tutorial puzzles throughout the game that I think just about anyone can do it. Some of the areas' BGM is really nice as well.

121691810.review:
[b]A really innovative, fun, and brain-melting puzzle game.[/b]

Positives:
- The whole experience can be described as "I can't tell you how exactly this works or why I'm doing this ... but when I do these steps, I will solve the puzzle because that's exactly how the puzzle works (even tho I'm just using muscle memory and educated guesses)".
- Lots of puzzles, lots of different mechanics, lots of interactions, lots of aha-moments.
- There are some really nice twists to the regular puzzles, like when you have to solve one using the string representation. There are lots of these small sets with 3-4 levels that completely change the puzzle formula, and it really shows how creative the devs got with such seemingly simple mechanics.
- Paradoxes are used in a clever way. First they are just an edge case you have to avoid, but later they actually become part of the puzzles.
- The level hubs give a preview of the mechanic/theme of the puzzles, which is very clever.

Neural:
- I can recommend playing the game in multiple long sessions so you don't lose the muscle memory of how the mechanics work. It worked well for me: by the 8th or 10th level hub (out of [spoiler]23[/spoiler] total), I was still breezing through the puzzles, but the game didn't give me any sort of indicator of how much more there is, so it became a little monotonous and exhausting.
- There's puzzles and that's it. (For me it's a positive, but some may prefer puzzles wrapped in a story or some form of progression.)

Negatives:
- It can be pretty difficult to distinguish the block "states", especially if the only difference is a change in brightness of the block's color. This makes it difficult to immediately start thinking about the puzzle solution when you first need to figure out what everything is. Same with when you don't start at the "outermost layer" of the puzzle or when some blocks are burrowed 2 "layers" deep inside other blocks.

119493645.review:
A delightful take on Sokoban-style puzzles, polished to within an inch of its life. Every level feels like it's there for a reason, and nothing feels wasted or overdone. Patrick's Parabox adds many new mechanics to Sokoban, but strangely they all seem to fit together extremely well. Each mechanic is introduced in a logical and straightforward manner, and its consequences are then explored. The result is a rich series of "aha" moments and clever insights. It's clear the author spent a great deal of time thinking carefully about how the player would engage with the game and its systems, rather than just slapping together a few dozen levels and calling it a day, as is so common with puzzle games these days.

Less interesting tidbits:
[list]
[*]There's no story. But it doesn't need a story.
[*]The graphics look more or less the same as you can see in the trailer (i.e. stylized, flat, and mildly cartoonish). They provide good feedback in response to player actions, including unsuccessful actions (e.g. pushing against a wall).
[*]The music's style is nicely matched to each mechanic, and helps to make each set of levels feel cohesive and unique.
[*]The game supports infinite undo, and also lets you undo the reset button. All puzzle games ought to have that functionality.
[*]If you really hate puzzle games, Patrick's Parabox isn't likely to change your mind. But if you like puzzle games, I strongly recommend it.
[/list]

119376630.review:
已经是我的解谜GOTY了（akurra？那是啥），不得不吹一下。
解谜设计师把递归玩法掏出来的那一刻就已经赢了大半。递归有两层美，先是逻辑美：像recursed、baba这样的硬核前辈们，再加上各路编程解谜，对玩家来说递归思考很坚固强硬，却始终有迹可循。再是结构美：像manifold garden、antichamber，再有今年的recursive ruin，无不将空间的可能性推向极致。

而《派箱》既有逻辑美也有结构美，在某种程度上是集大成者，这就强得可怕了。但我更欣赏的是关卡设计对概念的玩弄和发散。无限性到底是什么？无限性可以被捕捉和把握么？在这个小小的派“箱”里，在游戏规则的条条框框下，无限性变成了孤单的符号，我们用视听的语言丰富它，用关卡的空间陈列它。而游戏最后的几个大关让我发散联想到范畴论中的米田引理（Yoneda lemma）：如果无限能被表达，那我们也可以有无限的无限，有无限的无限的无限，我们可以在空间的层次间遨游，在递归的缝隙里狂奔；但最后，一切的一切都会回到那个小箱子里。在《派箱》里，无限性的技术就是派箱本身，我们能看到游戏设计对机制的规训和超越。我不由得这样想：人类的思想发源于自对于无限的凝视，但却因为有限性而伟大。

Patrick's Parabox is an incredible puzzle game, with an incredible premise and concept. This game's 300+ levels are sorted into 18 worlds, with each of these worlds introducing a new mechanic. There are also optional challenge levels, which are harder, and optional side levels that change the basic game formula a bit.

The difficuly curve is really good - hard enough to be interesting but not to the point of frustration. The game is easier than some other games of this genre (Baba Is You is considerbly more difficult), but I don't see that as a downside. The artstyle and music fit the game really well. The postgame content could be better, but it's pretty good anyway.

I have 100%ed this game, and I just want more of it. There is custom level support, but it isn't all that accessible so I have never used it. I really hope for a sequel or an in-game level editor in a future update, because I just want more of this game.

This is probably the best puzzle box type game made yet. You heard about The Witness and Stephen's Sausage Roll, and those are all difficult games that make you think and unfortunately also do stuff. Often time you can figure out the solution far before you can actually solve it and then have to go through the actual tedium of solving the dang thing. Patrick's Parabox on the other hand goes the opposite direction where your exploration of how the rules function and your progress through a particular level tend to coincide, where you figure out how you got to the solution just moments before you actually get to the solution. Sometimes this strays too far and you get to the solution without really realizing why you got there, but those are often the introductory puzzles that show you how a mechanic works. 

My only complaint, I need more. The game as it stands introduces a number of concepts and rules that all layer on top of each other, but aside from my first "paradox" I have not hit the "it goes one meta layer deeper" that the others (Baba is You, Stephen's Sausage Roll, The Witness, etc) get to, though I will admit that I am not quite done with all the levels. 

I honestly think that this is the freshest take on sokoban style mind bending puzzles I have ever seen. Most go too far and are far past the point where I am smart or patient enough to complete them, but this hits the absolute sweet spot and really is the best for anyone, even if you do not normally like these sorts of puzzlers.

Another great entry in the genre of "box-pushing game with more to offer than you'd think." If you enjoy the kind of game that Baba Is You is, with all of its puzzling yet fun-to-overcome mechanics, this game feels like you're playing it all over again. Just when I thought I had seen every possible way the game could explore its main gimmick of recursion, there was yet another set of levels that twisted the rules even further. This is definitely the type of game where the less you know going into it, the more fun your experience will be.

The music is fairly simplistic and there is no story, but this type of puzzle game does not need a narrative to be enjoyable. You're here for the head-scratchers, and that's what you get. It's an easy game to pick up, but finishing every last puzzle requires more than just thinking outside the box -- you must come to a complete understanding of the layers of "infinity."

The concept is refreshingly original, and I would love to see this game expanded upon with more puzzles or a level editor (I know that one exists, but I mean one with something like workshop support for easier sharing.) Very fun if you like to feel smart, then helplessly stuck, then smart again.

117848491.review:
This game has a friendly sort of charm that only grows more appealing as you progress. The difficulty ramps very gently, beginning with an extremely basic introduction of fundamental sokoban mechanics, escalating through a series of level groups which are each named for the concept they introduce. People who play a lot of puzzle games may find the early game a bit easier and less exciting than they'd like, but as the game starts iterating on combinations of mechanics the boards start becoming intensely clever. It is absolutely fantastic at presenting a situation that immediately looks impossible yet contains all the subtle tells needed to back out what [i]must[/i] happen to reach the goal. There are many excellent "wow" moments where you can barely comprehend what you're seeing, yet the game is always admirably legible and easy to read.

Just truly excellent craft on display in every area. I was a bit soft on the soundtrack from my impression of the demo, but after listening to all the tracks through the full game (they change for each named area) I am much more positive, with several standout tracks that I really enjoy. The inclusion of some otherwise unused mechanics as 'appendices' was really great to see--Patrick clearly has a lot of good ideas but is also willing to make thoughtful decisions about editing and scope discipline. Having them as a small post-game bonus is a great way to handle this; they don't get very much time but some of it is just excruciatingly clever. In any case, there seem to be a fair number of user levels exploring these concepts, so I think it works out beautifully.

In short, perhaps the most amiable game I've ever played, with some of the sharpest and smartest puzzles this side of The Talos Principle.

The reward for solving ALL the puzzles is a very small thing, but it made me smile :)

Le jeu est très satisfaisant à jouer.
Premièrement, 80% du jeu fonctionne comme un tutoriel, mais en laissant les joueurs découvrir les fonctionnalités par eux-mêmes, car les mécaniques du jeu sont introduites comme des moyens naturels de résoudre les niveaux. C'est un peu pour le même genre de raison que les jeux de Nintendo sont si naturels à jouer, donc si populaires.
Ensuite, le jeu est minimaliste, se base sur quelques concepts fondamentaux, et se contente de les pousser progressivement à l'extrême. Il n'y a littéralement pas besoin de réfléchir pour comprendre le jeu, car il s'agit juste de boîtes que l'on pousse vers des buts. Pourtant, il arriver à introduire, en les faisant jouer aux joueurs, des variantes liées à la récursion, l'infini, l'orientation ou les mathématiques de la grille, qui sont toutes simplement des généralisation des concepts de base. Les niveaux challenges que l'on débloque après avoir terminé les dix-huit mondes vont jusqu'au bout du concept en combinant tout ce qui a été appris.
En somme, ses principales qualités sont que les joueurs ont la sensation de comprendre le jeu par eux-même, que le jeu relativise un concept simple, que la courbe de difficulté soit bien dosée, que le jeu n'ait pas de redondance par l'apport de nouveauté sans cesse, ainsi que l'esthétisme audio et graphique du jeu que je n'ai pas mentionné mais qui fait toute la différence sur le ressenti.
Je l'ai déjà recommandé à plusieurs reprises. Pas de l'acheter sur Steam, car ça ne vaut le coup qu'en étant fan des qualités que j'ai décrites, mais au moins d'essayer le jeu que j'ai (je suis d'ailleurs ravi de la possibilité de plusieurs sauvegardes).

117418161.review:
Peak puzzle design. One of the best puzzle games out there. Underrated, and honestly could beat one of its greatest rivals: Baba is you. If there's anything Patrick's Parabox splendidly outdoes Baba is You at, it's elegant simplicity. 

The difficulty isn't too hard for most puzzles. This might turn off people who want a serious brain scratcher, but other than that, if you enjoy puzzles, get it. If you really want to be cautious, the demo will give you only a tiny yet fun peak at the easier puzzles. The difficulty is well balanced imo. Neither too easy, nor too hard. You will still have to pause for a moment and have to rethink, retry and reconsider your approach for almost every solution. The pace is good too, a little on the slow side, but you will never get overwhelmed.

The level design is genius, and the game manages to be so incredibly simple, contained within tiny spaces, yet have dozens and dozens of different mechanics derived from a couple core mechanics, with many fascinating applications. There are many levels (read: areas/chapters), each with a theme and a few puzzles, and they all introduce a new mechanic everytime, while never changing any rule, and almost never adding a new one. The consistency of the rules deserves credit. The depth is shockingly endless. More than a hundred puzzles is also a very fair ammount of puzzles for a puzzle game, especially since the price is reasonable.

It nails the satisfaction good puzzles should provide, the Ah Hah! moment. On top of that, it also nails the "wow" factor, surprising you in new ways every puzzle and new introduced mechanic.

My only gripe is that this game's potential is infinite, and it isn't fully exploited as there isn't a lot of levels that try to combine a lot of mechanics at once, which means it would benefit so, so much from an editor. There IS one, but it's just not something the average player will be able to use, unlike an editor like mario maker. It's not THAT complicated either, but still demanding more than most will have.

EDIT: Small correction about the editor. The way the level creation is implemented also has some significant advantages, the biggest being the following: The ability to create new mechanics.

As for other aspects including technical, i have no complaint.

Bu yılın beyin yakan bulmaca harikası.

Her sene bir yandan bizi eğlendirip hayrete düşürürken diğer yandan da zorluğuyla bol bol kafa kaşıtan en az bir tane bulmaca oyunu çıkıyor. Baba Is You, Superliminal ve Manifold Garden ilk aklıma gelenlerden... Patrick's Parabox da işte bu oyunların yanına ismini rahatça yazabileceğiniz, çok başarılı ve yaratıcı bir bulmaca oyunu.

Oyun Sokoban'ın kutuları itip haritadaki belirli yerlere yerleştirme mantığını alıyor ve bunu durmadan değişen kurallarla, akla hayale gelmeyecek şekillerde geliştirip sizi sürekli şaşırtmayı başarıyor.

Kutuları kutuların içine itmek, o kutuların içine kendimiz girmek, kutuların kenarlarındaki boşlukları giriş çıkış olarak kullanıp ekranın sağından solundan çıkmak gibi yazarak anlatılması da anlaşılması da zor olan bir sürü atraksiyona giriyoruz oyunda.

Pratik olarak bir kutu içindeki kutu içindeki kutuda dolaştığımızdan oyun sırasında ekranın ortasındaki küçük kutularda kendi minik hâlimizi hareket hâlinde görüyoruz. Bazen de ekranın dış kenarında kendi devasa hâlimizin hareketleri çarpıyor gözümüze. 

Patrick's Parabox'ta toplam 350 bölüm bulunuyor ve bunların hiç biri laf olsun diye konulmamış. Hiçbir zaman daha önce yaptığınız bir şeyi tekrarlamıyor, aynı çözüm yolunu uygulamıyorsunuz. Normal bölümlerin yanı sıra etrafları kırmızı çerçeveyle işaretlenmiş daha zor bulmacalar da var. Müzikleri, sevimli baş karakteri ve minimalist grafikleri de gayet yeterli.

Oyun bana yer yer Baba Is You'yu hatırlattı. Ama ona göre önemli bir avantajı var, o da kafanızı çok fazla karıştırmaması. Baba Is You'da ne yapmanız gerektiğini anlamak çoğu zaman çok zordu. Patrick's Parabox'ta ise sizden ne istendiğini daha çabuk anlıyorsunuz. Bu da başınızı çok ağrıtmamasını, çok çabuk bunalmamanızı sağlıyor.

Artılar:
+ Orijinal oynanış mekanikleri
+ Kutu içinde kutu içinde kutu paradoksları yaratmak eğlenceli
+ Bulmacalar zor ama yıldırıcı değil. Diğer bulmaca oyunlarına göre daha kolay anlaşılıyor
+ Geri alma ve baştan başlatma seçenekleri

Eksiler:
- Yok

Oyunun ücretsiz demosunu mutlaka deneyin derim. Böylece az çok fikir sahibi olabilir ve sevip sevmeyeceğinizi hemen anlarsınız. Çünkü dediğim gibi yazarak anlatması zor bir oyun Patrick's Parabox. Kendiniz tecrübe etmelisiniz. 8/10

116123945.review: This game... where to begin?  I'm a longtime puzzle game fan, I love puzzle games, and I try to play all the best ones.  Patrick's Parabox is definitely at the top of the heap; it's one of the finest puzzle games ever made.  The only games I can think of that are in the same league are Stephen's Sausage Roll (which this game's name is an obvious homage to) and Baba Is You.  And though I love those games, I love this one more.  It's curious, because visually, this game isn't much to look at.  It's basically just colored squares over and over.  But the gameplay is so weird, so mind-bending, and so [i]different[/i] from anything I've ever played before that I'm totally hooked.  Patrick gets a tremendous amount of mileage out of the recursive boxes-within-boxes theme, and he finds an endless number of variations on this theme. I find I can't play this for more than a few minutes at a time before my mind starts going numb (but in a good way, honestly!).  I like that the levels have a path that has to be completed to get to the next level, but there are also a few optional challenge puzzles on each level.  This avoids the syndrome where you get stuck on the one impossible puzzle which makes you rage quit the game.  Also, the puzzles themselves aren't difficult in a typical finding-the-needle-in-the-haystack way that many puzzle games are; instead, you just need to learn to think about the puzzle in the right way, and then it's (usually) easy.  Maybe this means that this game is easier than Stephen's Sausage Roll, but it's still plenty hard and, more importantly, plenty of fun.  This developer has real talent, and I'll be watching his future work closely.  If you like puzzle games even a little, you should buy this immediately!

I absolutely love this game. Enough that I'm even writing a review for it! As far as puzzles go, it's phenomenal - it keeps adding new mechanics at a nice and steady clip, and a lot of the puzzles have that really head-scratchy difficulty that makes you feel like an utter genius once you finally have that "Aha!" moment. What really sets Patrick's Parabox apart, though, is how much this game respects the player. There's the little, simple stuff - the UI is nice and clean, the animations are pleasing without being disorienting (important, given this game in particular), you can undo _and_ redo, and one touch I really like is that you can undo past a level-restart, useful when you want to remember how the puzzle was originally laid out but not lose all the progress you made.

But the much bigger part of that comes from the puzzle design itself. The easy puzzles that introduce mechanics do so cleanly, giving you all the info you need about how this new weird thing works, so that once you get to the hard puzzles, you aren't left wondering what in the world is going on. And the hard puzzles _are_ hard, but each is based around a clever but logical twist that, once you get it, you don't have to spend a long time shoving blocks all over the place before you solve it. It's a really wonderful and refreshing feeling, and the only thing I wish is that there were more of it!

115908417.review:
[b]Patrick's Parabox[/b] is a sokoban-type puzzle game where blocks can be entered and house puzzles within puzzles. The game is heavily inspired by [b]Sokosoko[/b] by juner.

This game is an idea taken to its logical conclusion, with the idea being "blocks are also rooms that can be entered".

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
If you've played Sokoban, you know what to expect. You need to push blocks onto specified marked squares, then go and stand your character on the goal square to win a level. The twist put on it, as previously mentioned, is that the blocks you push can sometimes be entered and house a puzzle within them.

Perhaps a level requires two blocks to win, but theres only one block in the level. You can enter the block that exists however, and inside it you find the second block you need. You can extract it from this block and suddenly you have all the blocks you need to finish the level.

This quickly get more complicated as you come across blocks that [i]are[/i] the level you're currently playing, and exiting the level border makes you exit the level block inside the level you're in.

Or maybe you try to enter a block as you enter the same block as you enter the same block as you enter the same block as you-

Well, you get the picture. The game has paradoxes [i]more than accounted for[/i] however, and it will not let you forget that.

[h2]Impressions[/h2]
This game is very elegant. It has a few clearly defined rules, and does a lot with them.
It pushes its idea beyond what you expect as a player, which reminds me of [b]Baba is You[/b].
It's mildly challenging, nowhere near the hair-tearing difficulty that for example Baba is You can throw your way. Patrick's Parabox also knows when to stop, which is something I can respect in the current gaming landscape where things seem to be designed to grab ahold of you and do nothing but waste your time.

There are of course some puzzles I did not like. Most of them were puzzles that didn't make use of the main gimmick at all, or in a way that was plain uninteresting. A few ideas were recycled several times, the small tweaks were not enough to make them interesting.

The puzzles I didn't like were a clear minority though!

[h2]Closing thoughts[/h2]
My playtime as of this review is the time it took to do everything. I completed this game in two sittings.
Might seem short, but if you like block-pushing games, you're doing yourself a disservice if you skip Patrick's Parabox.

It's one of the best in the genre.

115852776.review:
I don't usually recommend games due to the amount of time required to write such a review. Games like these are the exception because of either how well made or horrible the game is. In this case, its the former.

I'm going to compare this game to Baba is You because I feel like where Baba failed to uphold, Patrick comes in with a solid gold plate that reads 'No Excuses'.

In Baba, each level teaches you a new physic mechanic, allowing you to alter the physics of the puzzle. Each level afterward becomes increasingly difficult, which is exactly how it's suppose to be done. HOWEVER, what it failed to do is when it introduces these new mechanics, it doesn't bring those mechanics back to newer levels. 

Spoiler Ex: There was a level in Baba where Flag is Stop and you had a treadmill is move. How you would go about solving it is that you use the treadmill to Push you on to the Flag. I thought that was a neat mechanic but when playing the game, I have yet to see that mechanic ever being reintroduced. 

This is where Patrick comes in. This game will teach you core mechanics of the game, while making each one harder than the last level. Not only that, but when you are no longer in the world with that mechanic, it still reuses the past core mechanics in the future levels.

Spoiler: Let's say you learn about Center. Where you can only enter the area if the Center is not blocked. You can also push blocks that are in the Center by entering said area with the block. In the next worlds, they have constantly use that mechanic, not by a lot but enough of them use it to reward you on learning about the center.

I guess that's the other thing about this game, every time you clear a level it feels like a sense of accomplishment and rewards you by giving you levels that uses the mechanics you learn beforehand. And this barely covers the amount of content it provides. There are challenge levels that are optional in each world, not to mention several extra worlds that are full of challenges and surprises. 

This game is the best example of a perfect puzzle game. From the level design, to the simple mechanics, to all the extra stuff, all puzzle games should use this game as a blueprint for any puzzle game that they want to create.

Amazing game, I can't wait to see what other games this company will put out.

いわゆる倉庫番ライクなゲームだが、倉庫番の難しいテクニックは出てこない。
代わりにチャプターごとに特有のルールが用意されていて、そのルールを使ったテクニックを各ステージで一つずつ発見していけるようなデザインになっている。
このテクニックの発見こそがこのゲームの醍醐味だと思っている。

また、通常のステージ（白）で学んだテクニックは、そのあとの発展的ステージ（赤）でより深く使いこなすことを要求される。

13小时全成就，讲讲体验。
这个游戏确实是一款极其优秀的解谜游戏。推箱子游戏，但远不止是推箱子游戏。
游戏一共360关（加上Gallery的三关为363关），核心玩法的297关分为18个大章节，以及38个挑战关，还有3篇附录中的变体玩法共25关，无论是难度梯度还是引入的新机制，能真正做到由浅入深，循循善诱，玩下来让人感到酣畅淋漓，痛快至极。

115056130.review:
[h1]概要[/h1]
昨今その亜種を増やしつつ有るアドバンス倉庫番の一種であり、本作はステージ内にステージを持つ構造が特徴。
最も原始的な倉庫番のルール（箱を押して目的地に置く）を踏襲しつつ、輸送対象物である箱へ出入りする事ができる。この一見単純だが革新的なルールのお陰で、パズルを解く（または間違えてしまう）ための選択肢が一層増えており、問題を複雑且つ面白く仕立てている。
そして本作最大の目玉とも言える要素は、自己回帰性を有する点である。一体どういうことだろうか？
即ち、ステージ内の箱自体がステージと同義であり、小さな自分の入った箱を自分で押すと、大きな自分に押される事になる。その箱に入れば、より微小だが先程まで居たステージと同じステージへ無限に入り続ける事が出来るという訳だ。
これを聞いた貴方は恐らくシェルピンスキーのギャスケットやメンガーのスポンジなどを代表とするフラクタル図形について考え、その難解且つ奇妙な性質に関する知識を開陳したくなったかもしれないが、フラクタルに詳しくなくてもパズルをクリアすることが出来るので安心して欲しい。

[h1]考察[/h1]
箱の中に入るためには箱を壁に押し付けなければならない為、本来は倉庫番に於いて”詰み”とされる、箱が壁際に寄った状態がパズル解決に利用される。
レガシーな倉庫番では失敗の為に用意されていた手順が、本作では成功への道程と化しており、新規性は寧ろここにあるのだと思う。微小領域へアクセスするギミックもこの発明に依存した枝葉の1本に過ぎない（プレイヤーと箱を入れ替えるギミック等もあり、これも壁に押し付けることで成立する）。

[h1]総評[/h1]
発売前から下馬評が高く、その評価に違わぬ面白くて斬新な、こめかみを指で抑え続ける事ができるパズルゲームである。
特にステージ6（スワップ）は本作のギミックを遺憾無く発揮した異次元の構造をしており、カバンの中で複雑に絡まったイヤホンをほどく事にワクワクを感じている人は絶対に愉快になること間違いなしである。
惜しむらくは、自己回帰の斬新さを前半で体験してしまい、プレイヤーと箱を入れ替える後半のギミックが少し味気なく感じる事か。但しこれはメインパスの話なので、難しい赤枠のステージでは以前のギミックと複合され、事態をよりカオスにしている。
難易度については青天井という訳でもなく、しかし簡単とは言えない絶妙な塩梅である。クリアした状態を想像し易いパズルが多いので、過程の絞り込みは速やかであり、気持ちのいいテンポで次の問題のために頭を悩ますことが出来る。
何故解けたのか分からないってのは皆思ってます。貴方だけではないのでご心配なく。

this is definitely my favourite puzzle game. it's extremely accessible in its puzzles and takes the time to emphasise every single game mechanic from the absolute simplest to the most complex, to the point that no other game I've seen has managed to do well

like, the initial premise is already weird (what if I could have levels inside levels, with nested recursion), but it somehow manages to get even weirder to the point that I was somehow even more surprised as the game progressed until the very end as new mechanics were introduced and explored

that said, the puzzles are hard, and most of the optional puzzles really push the boundaries of what you can do. even when I hadn't finished them all, I never felt like I didn't have the tools to solve them, but I definitely took a while to figure out how.

the game is definitely on par with the magnificence of games like Stephen's Sausage Roll and Baba Is You but way more accessible IMHO. if you liked but had trouble with those types of games, you may like Patrick's Parabox even better.

extremely small nitpick is the puzzles which move the camera around, which does affect the accessibility. there is a way to change the camera (press 7 to cycle between display modes, including the text mode), but I feel like this could have been advertised a little better.

overall: I absolutely love it. play this game and enjoy.

I really enjoyed this one and played it to 100% completion. Not only are the puzzles fun to solve in a puzzley way, but simply moving around in these recursive spaces is very fun in and of itself. It explores the concept thoroughly and comes up with more gimmicks than you're probably expecting, each new one is really cool to discover. There is a nice length to the game as well, not too short not too long. To my tastes the length is just right, nothing ever felt like a slog.

I'd also like to point out that the game structure is likely to appeal to a wide spectrum of gamers:

Want to experience all the different gimmicks but afraid you'll get stuck? Don't worry, every world has a path of relatively easy puzzles to unlock the next world, so you have the option of moving forward if you're stuck or simply aren't vibing with a particular gimmick.

Want a good challenge? Actually solving everything is HARD and will really force you to master the power of recursion. The hardest puzzles are roughly of a similar difficulty (maybe slightly easier) to the hardest in other popular puzzle games.

114516613.review:
[h1] Patrick’s Parabox是一款递归类推箱解谜游戏。 [/h1]
在游戏的过程中，一个箱子可以进入另一个箱子，乃至层层嵌套和循环。
[b]机制特色：[/b]

l 深入探索过的嵌套机制。箱子里可以装箱子是嵌套；自己装自己是递归，作者对嵌套的条件、递归玩法的深度都做出了有趣的探索。多个箱子一起被推动会如何，推者与被推者谁进入谁，乃至后期的无穷大循环和无穷小循环，附录中的规则反转……通过不断引入新的主题机制给玩家带来耳目一新的感觉，而非一味地通过提升关卡规模来增加难度。
机制得分：9.0/10.0
 
[b]内容特色：[/b]

l 合理的难度设置。难度曲线大致分为主线，支线和挑战3档，完成较少数量关卡即可前往下一章节。主线的难度相当之低而又足以让玩家体会章节的核心机制是如何实现的。而支线和挑战则进一步考验着对于核心机制的理解与运用。总体来说本作的难度拉得比较低，主旨在于让玩家享受机制产生的奇妙变化而不是刁难玩家。
l 优秀的“演出效果”。一些支线关卡会附带小型的主题：画面不断缩放、拥有和主角同步以动的方块、方块的网格被“压扁”等等，通过此种方式引入的小主题是优秀的调味剂，为闯关增添了趣味性。还有我推我自己，无限分型等名场面。
内容得分：8.5/10.0
 
[b]艺术特色：[/b]

l 明亮色调与富有动态感的效果。高对比度的配色和每章节特有的主题颜色十分养眼，箱子推动时一跳一跳的动画效果使得游戏氛围轻松明快。
l 较为一般的配乐。本作的BGM听着使得笔者没有觉得放松轻快，有时甚至会干扰解题。
艺术得分：7.5/10.0
 
[b]综合评价：[/b]

l Patrick’s Paradox在前人的基础上做到了机制和内容的创新和突破，是值得尝试的优秀作品。尤其推荐想入解谜游戏坑的新人尝试。

综合得分：8.5/10.0
通关时间：3h(15h)
游戏难度：4/10

114320734.review:
This game implements recursion in a meaningful, consistent, comprehensible way. But recursion isn't the only draw here; it's implemented as part of a more general system of levels and sublevels. And in that system lies the beauty of Patrick's Parabox.

The pacing in this game is really, really good so far. I always have time to get used to and internalize a concept before a new mechanic is dropped on me to melt my brain all over again. Each new world brings a concept that fundamentally changes how a sokoban style game works, and in an entirely different way than the concept before it.

If you liked Baba Is You, you'll probably like Patrick's Parabox. The base interactions at play are simpler, yet the consequences are somehow even more insane. It doesn't take Turing completeness to produce beautiful insanity.

[h1]《Patrick’s Parabox》:箱子里的解密，属于自己的无穷冒险[/h1]
[h1]前言[/h1]
《Patrick’s Parabox》是一款以“推箱子”为主题的逻辑解密游戏，游戏中玩家需要将各种各样的箱子推到指定的位置来实现通关，每一个“大关”都会有相同的主题，而这些“大关”中的小关卡都会有“异曲同工”的妙处，玩法简单易懂，通关乐趣无穷，不论是上班摸鱼还是下班放松都是不错的选择。
[h1]玩法独特别具一格[/h1]
相信玩家们在小时候就已经接触过《推箱子》这一游戏了，那时的我们会随着地图的变换不断更换自己的思考方式，从而实现不同关卡的通过，这些箱子们给我们带来了无限的乐趣。如今，它以不一样的方式又出现在了我们的眼前，这一次，又是一场全新的体验。
游戏的玩法与一般的推箱子不同，这一次，玩家们不仅需要将箱子推到指定的位置，还需要自己走到指定地点才能可以，值得一提的还有，这次你终于可以实现“一次推多个箱子”的梦想了，限制你的不再是箱子的数量，而是多种多样的其它玩法，这包括了“无限宇宙”、“多维空间”等等，你想象得到的想象不到的这里都有。
玩家们大可不必担心由于游戏过难而导致很难有代入感，相反，你可能因为由于游戏简单易懂的规则和玩法而沉浸其中，导致在卡关时会有些既无奈又生气，其实就跟做题一样，许多时候遇到无法解决的问题时不妨换种思路，或者是多走走其他的路，往往会给自己打开一个新的思路，从而解决问题。
[h1]画面简单明了[/h1]
游戏将简约的风格贯彻的从头到尾，不论是玩法还是画面，都十分明了，作为解密游戏这是非常难能可贵的一点，玩家会因此更专注的将焦点放在“解密”上，其它的反而都是一些细枝末节的装饰了。
不过由于画面的简单，通过图文的方式反而很难表现出游戏的有趣性，只有“动静结合”才能更好地展现出游戏的可玩性和乐趣，一进一出、一张一弛、一静一动，游戏像是进化般由简到繁的蜕变着，玩家也乐在其中。
我认为游戏在可玩性方面可以类比《赛博之钩》、《Hexologic》、《极简地牢》这几款游戏，至少我认为这几个游戏在某些方面确实有着“异曲同工”之妙，都是以极其简单的玩法和画面带给了玩家极大的乐趣。
[h1]音乐悠扬放松[/h1]
作为一款十分简约的游戏，音乐也确实给游戏加了不少分，并不单纯是说背景音乐，游戏中的互动音效也十分可爱，总是能让人联想到一些像是水滴声、雨声这样的声音，悠扬且舒缓，让人能够放松的解密。
许多玩家留言说解密无脑入就可以，其实并不是夸张，由于游戏的核心玩法十分独特，解密的思路也在这一点上和同类型的解密游戏十分不同，如果说你也喜欢解密，我也很建议你尝试一下本作。
游戏虽然没有什么剧情，但就在个人感觉上来说，每一次通关都像是一次旅程，而你上下左右的操作、一次又一次的撤回、一次又一次的重开便是旅途上的冒险和经历，盯着屏幕认真思考的你真的很可爱。
[h1]购买指南[/h1]
总结来看，《Patrick’s Parabox》是一款十分优秀的逻辑解密作品，甚至是每一关都有不一样的特点，当你过完某一关，睡醒了再来看一下，似乎又不会了，可以说很好的预防了老年痴呆。游戏支持键鼠和手柄，这里提一嘴，说回游戏价格，我个人认为原价可以接受，毕竟游戏的内容还是多的，完全通关的时长可能还是说因人而异，由于我也还没通关所以不是很好判断，猜测应该在15小时以上？9.0/10

1982年にパズルゲーム「倉庫番」が誕生してから40年。パズルゲームとして数々の亜種を生み出しながら進化を続けて来た。そしてついに、倉庫番は新たな地平に到達した。それがこの「Patrick's Parabox」だ。通常の倉庫番では、箱はただの箱で、ただ運ばれるだけの存在。しかし本作においては、プレイヤーは箱の中に入ることができる。箱の中に入って、通り抜けたりできる。しかしそれは序の口で、箱の中に箱があったり、スタート地点がすでに箱の中だったりする。さらには箱の中と倉庫の外がつながっていたり、うかつに箱を運ぶと無限の宇宙に放り出されたり、微小な世界に迷い込んだりする。もう倉庫と箱という物理概念をを超えた、形而上学的な何かを運ぶゲームに仕上がっている。とはいえ難易度は適切で、理解しがたい概念も間欠明瞭なインターフェースと丁寧なレベルデザインによって段階的にクリアできるようになっている。パズルゲームが好きな方、無限の宇宙に放り出される刺激が足りない方に是非お勧めしたい。

It has been 40 years since the puzzle game "Sokoban" was created in 1982. The game has continued to evolve as a puzzle game, creating numerous variants. Finally, Sokoban has reached a new horizon. This is "Patrick's Parabox”. In the usual Sokoban game, a box is just a box, and it is simply transported. In this work, however, the player can enter the box. They can get into the box and go through it. But that is just the beginning; there are boxes within boxes, and the starting point is already inside a box. Furthermore, there is a connection between the inside of the box and the outside of the warehouse, and if the box is carried carelessly, the player may be thrown out into an infinite universe or lost in a microscopic world. This is a game that transcends the physical concept of a warehouse and a box, and is a game about transporting something metaphysical. Nevertheless, the difficulty level is appropriate, and even difficult-to-understand concepts can be completed step-by-step thanks to the clear and concise interface and careful level design. I highly recommend this game to those who enjoy puzzle games and are missing the stimulation of being thrown out into an infinite universe.

不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]
[h1] 《Patrick's Parabox》：又是一款别样的推箱子游戏 [/h1]
[h1] 前言 [/h1]
想必大家或多或少都接触过推箱子游戏，小时候在爸妈的手机上玩。后来在steam上也玩了推箱子游戏，第一款是免费游戏《Helltaker》，在地狱里邂逅魅魔，接着又玩了seek girl系列，但是这两款游戏并没有太多的革新玩法，无非加了点狼人以及难度更高。首次让我感到新颖的是《ba ba is you》，这款游戏所带的meta元素是真有意思，然后就是今天所要介绍的这款游戏了，翻译名叫《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》。
[h1] 简单介绍下游戏 [/h1]
这是一款循环解谜套娃推箱子游戏，递归套娃推箱，由独立制作人Patrick Traynor 制作并发行。该游戏，在2019年获得了IndieCade开发者选择奖，也在2020年独立游戏节上获得了优秀设计奖。整体游戏画面比较清新可爱，小方块的形象也非常有趣，音乐也比较轻快带感。难度偏烧脑，前期比较休闲，后期就越来越难，所以游戏流程看个人，我是玩了几个小时才过了几关，真的菜。
游戏操作也很简单，只需要传统的wsad键或方向键就可以移动，鼠标可以用来放大缩小界面，因为有套娃机制存在嘛，大多数时候只会用到键盘。
最让我感到意外的是，每一关的设计都别出心裁，以至于自己每过一小关，都感到很开心，不会有丝毫倦意。
[h1] 怎么玩？只需要进入和退出就行 [/h1]
开始游戏时，画面会进入游戏名中的那个场景，刚开局就把俺惊艳到了。
游玩时，玩家所操控的红方块需要把箱子推到指定地方，自己也要到规定位置。但是那个位置非常刁钻，有时在一个方块的内部，或者在一个犄角旮旯的地方。咱们就需要利用这关的机制，将方块推进另一个方块的内部，再推出去，能推进去的前提是那个特殊方块已经是被固定好了（无法再推动，后面有方块或墙壁啥的）。所以有些方块是起着辅助的作用（作为障碍物），并不需要将其移动到指定地方。 
在游玩过程中，让自己有种在玩哆啦A梦的道具的奇妙感觉，就是那个能放大和缩小生物的隧道，真的很有意思，彷佛一瞬间回到了童年。
在操作失误的时候，可以按Z键取消操作（返回上一步），按X键重新操作（这个貌似没多大用），还是按R键重置谜题好了，也就是重新操作。 
游玩每一个大关卡时，只需要完成指定的小关卡数，就可以进入下一个大关卡。 
 顺便说一下，在起初的关卡右上角有一个特殊的黄方块，进去后会有五个游戏提示。
[h1] 让人感到有趣又烧脑的地方：递归套娃机制  [/h1]
这个游戏的特色之一就是递归套娃，需要玩家进入方块内部，然后外面的世界会随内部世界变化而变化，你在推你自己。可以理解成是一个多重世界，内部的方块移动，外部也有个相同的方块也在移动，虽然有趣但有时也会让人感到有点晕（特别多的时候）。而且一些方块的入口是有方向的，并不是四面八方都可以进入，这时候需要玩家像列文虎克一样细致入微，提前了解方块的构造及其入口朝向，再针对性地做下一
步决策。
当你成功后，你会觉得十分高兴，没想到这样也行，真的太棒了。
[h1]不会让人感到无聊，激发玩家的好奇欲 [/h1]
前文也说了，每一关卡的设计都别出心裁，准确地来说是每一个大关卡。只不过那些小关卡都会用到所处大关卡的主题，目前来说会有18个大关卡。依照顺序来介绍，入门、进入、空白、吞食、参照、调换、居中、克隆、转移、开放、翻转、循环、玩家、占据、墙、无限退出、无限进入、多重无限。 
游戏里有一个自制关卡的选项，等时间久了，肯定会不不少大佬的自制关卡，或许因为这一点，所以暂时还没有创意工坊。个人也希望制作者能开放创意工坊，这样能游戏的可玩性大大提高，虽说目前游戏已经很好玩了，但自己有点贪心，想必大多数玩家也是这么想的吧。
[h1]寓教于乐，不学习，你连游戏都玩不明白，开个玩笑 [/h1]
Paradox是悖论的意思，与游戏名中的parabox仅相差一个字母。看到B站up主打算用集合论的知识来玩这一款游戏，个人觉得稍微有点道理，但也不是完全有道理。在无限退出关卡，会遇到无穷大∞；在无限进入关卡，会遇到无穷小ε。一些大佬还能在同一个关卡，推出两个悖论。说实话，游戏中文名完全可以叫《帕特里克的悖论箱》，确实很悖论。笔者稍微提了下，感兴趣的朋友一定要去试一试，真的很有意思。
[h1] 总结 [/h1]
这款推箱子游戏确实好玩，简单的操作方法，舒适轻快的音乐，巧妙的关卡设计，不得不佩服制作者能设计一款游戏。
这款游戏原价70元，说实话不是很贵，游戏内容还是很足的，并不是一味地重复，还会越玩越带劲。当然个人建议，对这类游戏感兴趣的朋友但又比较菜，可以等打折入，相信以后肯定会有创意工坊，以及更多的大佬自制关卡。
顺带提一句，这款游戏还有附录关卡。当你玩完多重无限关卡，或许会感受到一个别样的宇宙，十分奇妙，渐渐进入贤者时间，啊不，进入超神的状态，十分宁静祥和。

This is pretty good game. Here are the pros and cons

Cons:
- I found it strangely enough, too easy. Maybe I'm just better than average at weird recursive sokoban (I did have an easier time with Baba is You than most of my friends and family who played it), or maybe something about the levels makes it too quick to reverse engineer the solution. I managed to solve the levels in under a minute on average, and only got stuck on two or three of the post-game extra levels.

Pros:
- Despite how easy it was, I still found it fun and interesting to explore what this kind of meta-sokoban would entail, and, for that reason, I don't regret buying it.
- The level-design is (barring difficulty) excellent. There aren't annoying red-herrings and the puzzles had varied solutions. Some levels build on each other, but it never felt like I was playing the exact same thing.
- This game has fantastic communication! The "tutorials" (if it's even right to call them that, they're really just introductory levels) made every new mechanic intuitive without feeling like the game was questioning your intelligence. For a game that introduces a fair number of new mechanics, it did not feel overwhelming. Also, everything is well-telegraphed and consistent.
- The polish is amazing! Accessibility options are great, didn't encounter a single bug, everything about the way the levels look and the characters move was quite charming.

So, I would recommend this game, but make sure to savor it because otherwise, it might feel underwhelming.

113742559.review:
[h1] Pros[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Excellent tutorial levels! This game is about recursion, a concept that is notoriously difficult to wrap your head around in maths and programming. Despite that however, the visuals and the tutorial levels teach the player without words how everything works together.
   [*]The game is quite easy. If you are new to puzzle games, or if you want something you can complete in a single sitting, this game might be for you.
   [*] [b]Some[/b] interesting concepts. Some concepts like the recursion feel very well planned out and stay with you the entire game. And when these concepts work together it creates some amazingly clever puzzles.
[/list]

[h1] Cons[/h1]
[list]
    [*] Actually, the game is too easy. Now this is a bit up to personal preference, but for me the game is just too easy. In the first two hours of playing I saw that i had 150 puzzles completed. Which meant that I was burning through levels at a rate of around one level per minute. And that is not for me.
[*] Way too many mechanics that just feel gimmicky. Some worlds feel like they just revolve around a single gimmick, and every level in those worlds just feel like rehashes of the previous ones. Very rarely do we get some brilliant level that connects all these loose, poorly explored parts and brings them together into a beautiful artisitc masterpiece of a level, but those levels are few and far between. I have not finished every level in this game because I got bored, but I did play through at least parts of every world (so i reached the end credits and saw all mechanics), and what i've seen so far just feels lacking.
[*] Levels where you can accidentaly stumble into the solution. There are levels in this game, where due to the limited options at your disposal, you are almost forced into a solution by the movement constraints without thinking at all. This is a big no no for me.
[*] Too many levels that just feel samey. Too many levels right after another just feel like remixes of each other. You can often use almost the same solution as you've done previously without much thought.
[/list]

Overall, the game is not bad. And it might be for you. But for me the mechanics and puzzles presented were just not interesting enough. 

6/10 - average

113672320.review:
Patrick's Parabox is exquisite. It's immediately one of the greatest puzzle games of all time - I'd argue top 3. For those who didn't read the blurb, it's a sokoban puzzle game whose gimmick is based around the programming concept of recursion; each block you push around can be a map unto itself that you are able to go into, and the game builds on these ideas of recursion in extremely clever ways.

I was wary going into this game because it's not the first puzzle game playing with the concept of recursion. Recursed has attempted this before, and I found it to be a case test in how not to design a puzzle game; The recursive puzzles very quickly became too tangled and hard to follow, and it failed to offer any satisfying a-ha moments that you expect from a puzzle game.

Thankfully, Patrick's Parabox is the complete opposite experience. It's rich with brilliant puzzles that are minimal and elegant and expose interesting idea upon interesting idea. And they don't feel needlessly hard, which I appreciate. It's not like a Baba level where you might get stuck on it for hours. In the over 350 levels I never got stuck for more than like 25 minutes. It's like the quality of a qrostar game, but more accessible (while still being plenty mind bending). 

If you enjoy puzzle games, you must play this. It's a treat.

113671705.review:
I've 100% completed Patrick's Parabox, along with many other puzzlers. 
TL;DR: This one is an overall 7/10 (Very good). If you are new to puzzlers, this is a perfect start.

DIFFICULTY: 5/10. Compared to some other tile based puzzlers, this is one of the easiest out there. Once you wrap your head around the concept of things being multi-layered, most levels come with either trying the only thing possible, or learning a new mechanic.
MAIN CONTENT: 9/10. Each level has a small section dedicated to simply teaching the mechanics of the game, and most sections add completely new mechanics into the mix. The mechanics are never overly complicated nor out-blown (except in cases where the solution is presented to you instantly, as more of a fun experiment rather than an actual level). Additionally, the tutorials don't overlay previous mechanics too much, allowing you to properly learn the concept before throwing it into the pot.
SIDE/POST CONTENT: 7/10. Most of the side content is either: 1. Some new mechanic not presented in a previous level, or 2: a combo of old and current mechanics. Perfect Parabox取得(=全ステージクリア)しました。
「常識をひっくり返す」の説明の通り、パズル内パズル、再帰構造、無限といった怪しげなシステムを楽しめるパズルゲームです。

自機である箱を上下左右に動かしてステージ上の箱を押して指定された位置に運び、最後に自機を指定された位置に動かせばクリアとなる、「倉庫番」のシステムを下地にしたパズルです。
また、「The Witness」「Baba Is You」といった著名パズルゲームに採用されている、「ルールの詳細がゲーム中で説明されず、ステージを進める度に新たなギミックが登場する」性質も持っています。
ステージ毎に1つのギミックがテーマとして据えられており、問題を通してギミックの仕様を理解してパズルを解き、次のステージに挑んでいくことになります。

ステージ中に登場する箱には、出入り可能な性質をもつものが登場します。
箱の中に入る、箱から違う箱に出る、箱の中にもパズルがある、箱を動かしてパズルを組む、etc.
参照構造・再帰構造をもった箱は極めて理解しがたい謎めいた挙動を見せ、プレイヤーを混乱させます。
これを理解・利用してゴールへの箱の運び方、自機の動かし方を考えるのがパズルの趣旨となります。

操作は方向のみであり、アンドゥ・リセット等の機能も充実しておりパズルを解くことに集中できます。
パズル数は300を超える充実仕様。素直に解けるものからインチキじみたものまで多種多様なパズルが待ち受けます。
箱に出入りするエフェクトは若干酔うかもしれないので、動きを見て「設定→移動設定」を調整することをオススメします。

この手の固有ギミックを擁するパズルゲームはえてして高難易度でありPatrick's Paraboxもその例にもれませんが、ギミックを理解すれば閃きを要さずとも解けるパズルが多い、パズル自体がコンパクトである等の理由により全体を通して比較的解きやすい部類であると感じました。導入も丁寧なので、PVを見て挙動をある程度理解できるならエンディングに辿り着くことは十分に可能でしょう。
(ゲーム内Tipsにも記載されている通り、考えずに解けるものではなく相応の思考は求められますが)
十分なパズル力があれば、現実を汚染したり夢にまで現れるといったほどの苦戦はしないと思います。これを親切設計と見るか、物足りないと見るかは人それぞれでしょうか。

箱のキャラクターを動かしてギミックのぶっ飛んだ挙動を見ているだけでも楽しいゲームです。
パズルの質も高く、簡単なものからチャレンジングなものまで、解き応えがしっかり感じられる良作だと思います。
全ステージが正方形、箱も正方形(ごく一部例外あり)、エフェクトも正方形と見た目のこだわりも面白いです。
話題作りとして、頭の運動として、難関パズルゲームの入門として、いかがでしょうか。

作为一款以推箱子为核心玩法的游戏，作者无疑是用硕大的脑洞将我狠狠震惊到，作者将套娃与推箱子相结合，并且融入了无限空间的玩法，这种创意让原本难度就颇高的玩法从难度和趣味性上都更上一层楼，喜欢解密游戏的玩家一定不要错过。

万万没想到一款推箱子游戏我却玩的这么津津有味，不得不说作者对于推箱子的玩法的创新是十分成功的，随着要素的逐渐增多，这样一款操作简单的小游戏也展现出无限的可能性，游戏中玩家要通过重叠的套娃空间，借助空间的不同来解决谜题，虽然听起来十分简单，但在真正操作起来却会发现其独特的魅力，玩家在本游戏中所推的箱子也变成了一个小世界或是一模一样的套娃世界，随着游戏关卡的递进，玩家可能要面对越来越多层数的套娃，并通过不同的顺序，将箱子和玩家本身放到指定的位置上，几乎不变的玩法，却带来完全不同的体验。

而作者在难度的把握上也有着十分不错的火候，游戏被作者分为数十个大的关卡，而每个关卡的主题也不相同，随着关卡的递进，游戏中会出现新的玩法机制，并且每个关卡的难度也是逐渐升高，但是游戏的整体难度并不是很高，但是在这样的创意下总能带给玩家惊喜。

这无疑是对推箱子游戏的一场创新，简单却吸引人，如果你喜欢过推箱子游戏，那么本作一定能带给你惊喜。所以创意工坊什么时候开。
评分9/10

This is the first time in a while that I've felt compelled and capable to 100% a puzzle game on my own. It's a complex and difficult game, but also very fair and forgiving in ways that make it a joy to play. Puzzles are difficult because of how they re-use and re-contextualize their mechanics, rather than adding additional layers of complexity for the sake of difficulty. Solutions tend not to be particularly long. I think of the 364 puzzles, there was a total of [i]one[/i] that I did not understand and had to brute force. That's pretty remarkable!

In addition to all that, I think there's a lot of value in playing this game for the first time blind. Every time a new mechanic is introduced, it was a surprise to me - and yet, the mechanic was simple enough that I almost instantly understood it.

I do not know if you'll enjoy this game to the end if you're not a puzzle game enjoyer. However, if you are, I cannot recommend it enough.

[u][b]특히 패러박스에서 가장 두드러지는 기믹인 "재귀"는 이 게임의 핵심을 관통한다.[/b][/u]

[h1] 前言 [/h1]

《Patrick's Parabox》，又一款类推箱子的神作。解谜多神作，我们总是惊叹作者天马行空的脑洞，总是感慨自己生了锈的脑子。不过玩家大可不必妄自菲薄，十几二十个小时就解决作者动辄一两年积累的奇思妙想，已经很强了好吧。

[h1] “嵌入”为核，递进为辅 [/h1]

类推箱子的玩法不胜枚举，本作的核心则在于功能不同的箱子以及可以互相“嵌入”的特殊机制。

古早的推箱子就是一个小人，将箱子推到指定的位置，相当简单的核心玩法与并不普通的策略性，结合较低得到门槛与极高的可玩性，推箱子玩法长久不衰。本作在此基础上做了微创新，并且深入挖掘了可能性，呈现出的可玩性相当不错。比如将小人替换成箱子，也需要移动到指定位置；比如箱子变成可以互相嵌入，以此带来全新的移动方式；再比如多个箱子相互嵌套，形成循环的效果，挖掘出现有机制下的全新玩法，让人大开眼界。

本作虽然是微创新，但是深入挖掘出的玩法，让“微”不再微，而是变成了一个个惊人的脑洞，颠覆常规的解题思路同时给予玩家强烈的满足感。最让人惊喜的是游戏整体的难度设计十分友好。游戏分为多个区域，每个区域都有不同的机制，并且有一条主线贯穿所有区域，同时解释新机制。主线的难度极低，作用就相当于新手教程。挑战的难度在于支线，不但有对机制的全新解读，还有多个机制结合的难题，烧脑程度upup。难能可贵的是支线难度也依次递增，看起来类似的关卡，实际上还需要新思路。

[h1] 明确的解题思路 [/h1]

游戏的逻辑性相当强，它不同于其它解谜神作，需要跳出当前环境。这不禁让我想起来《witness》的环境谜题，核心也是简单的一笔画，但是空间跨度如此大的解题思路，说惊艳的确惊艳，说不当人也真的不当人。本作就十分友好，目标明确，无论正推还是逆推，效果都不错，给予玩家的正反馈也相当足。

[h1] 总结 [/h1]

解谜类游戏一般都以创造新机制和深入挖掘为主要手段，《Patrick's Parabox》在这两方面都做的相当优秀。虽然全程几乎无文字教程，但是循序渐进的主线关卡很容易教会玩家规则。唯一的缺点（不是）怕是挑战性没那么高，期待社区的不当人关卡。

113558919.review:
The game is a Sokoban block puzzle clone. Push the blocks into the right spaces and then get to the exit. The mandatory twist is that blocks can contain mini-levels inside of themselves. So you can push a block inside another one, then shrink down inside the mini-level to retrieve the block later. This opens up a whole lot of possibilities for getting blocks off walls and navigated around corners.

That's the mandatory twist. The real twist is that blocks often contain recursive copies of the level. This gets nutty.

You can push a block off the edge of the level, and then it reappears inside of the level next to the recursive copy. You can push the copy to a hard-to-reach location, then walk off the edge of the level later to teleport next to the block - or enter the block to get back the to the edge. Some levels have recursive copies inside of recursive copies, requiring you to turn them inside-out to have the right number of blocks in the right copy or move them around each other to keep blocks from getting stuck on walls.

One thing you'll inevitably stumble upon by accident is that you'll push a level up next to its own edge and then step outside. This drops you into a void you can never return from, a mathematical dead-end marked by an infinity symbol. And then you think about it. Each time you step out of the level, you go up one stage of recursion. So if the level is up against its own edge, then when you exit the level, you're outside the edge of the next stage already. So you go up another stage, but you're still outside the edge, so that means... Oh dear.

It's a very cute little joke, handled cheekily and easy to undo.

It's also foreshadowing - and far from the most mind-bending idea the game requires you to wrap your head around...

The puzzles hit this fantastic sweet spot where every single level gets you to wrap your head around another way of looking at the same mechanics, but there aren't so many mechanics that you get overwhelmed with options. And the puzzles are generally only a few steps long with a lot of generous space to navigate the mazes - there's no tedium about figuring out the exact right way to navigate a claustrophobic mess.

And the final levels in the game are impressive for just how hard they run circles around dizzying existential ideas of infinity, treating the incomprehensible endless with the same casual indifference that Mario treats coins. Honestly, they're not hard puzzles. The last puzzle in the game in particular is also probably the easiest. But that's fine. The point isn't to challenge you. The point is that over a couple hundred puzzles, the game has taught you how to conquer the very boundaries of existence, and you deserve to have some fun with that knowledge before you're sent off.

113473320.review:
Patrick's Parabox is a masterpiece in puzzle design elegance. It is the ultimate result of:

[list]
    [*]taking a simple concept: Sokoban, but levels can have levels within them that you can enter and exit,
    [*]reducing the rules to be as simple as possible:
    [list]
        [*][spoiler]there are only two objects: boxes and walls[/spoiler]
        [*][spoiler]you control a box[/spoiler]
        [*][spoiler]if a box moves out of bounds, it exits the box it's in[/spoiler]
        [*][spoiler]box-to-box movement can either push, enter or (area 4 mechanic - try spotting it in the trailer!), which may result in more box movements[/spoiler]
    [/list]
    [*]and exploring every single emergent behaviour that results from those simple rules.
[/list]

In fact, the simplicity of the rules is arguably a spoiler - if you think hard enough, you can figure out many of the concepts explored in the game!

Just those mechanics would be enough to make a solid, small game... but Patrick's Parabox takes it to the next level with additional mechanics. It's very easy to make a game convoluted and overwhelming by introducing additional mechanics, either by having too many mechanics or each mechanic being too complicated. Patrick's Parabox does not fall for this trap - there are just enough new mechanics to keep things interesting but not overwhelming, and each mechanic is so natural that it only takes a single introduction level to fully understand it.

The puzzles themselves are also excellent. The negative reviews I've seen contradict my own experiences - to quote the Steam description:

[quote=About this game]Each puzzle contains a new idea; there is no filler.[/quote]

The overall difficulty of the game [i]is[/i] indeed easier than other games like Baba Is You. If you're a puzzle game master, Patrick's Parabox overall difficulty might be a bit on the easier side, and each "new idea" might be so simple for you that they don't seem like new ideas. On the other hand, this makes Patrick's Parabox's excellent ideas much more accessible to a wide variety of people without the need to enable the "Unlock all puzzles" option in the settings.

I personally found the difficulty pacing to be excellent - the main puzzles are indeed on the easier side, but there are harder optional puzzles marked with a red border, extra-hard post-game puzzles and a level editor for user-made levels.

If Baba Is You is like a fine dining restaurant, Patrick's Parabox is like a brunch cafe: sometimes, you're just not in the mood for something deep and complex, but aren't willing to go as low as junk food.

113433834.review:
This game gets a lot of things right, that make a puzzle game good:
[list]
[*]The artwork and animations are clean and clear, so you challenge is figuring out the puzzles, rather than figuring out what you're seeing, in addition to the puzzles. (There's a few levels that are intentionally visually challenging; those are optional and relatively easy - the puzzle there is being able to interpret what you're seeing)
[*]The challenge on each level is figuring out how the mechanics interact, not arbitrary conditions like "Solve this within a time limit" or "Solve this with a limited number of moves" - it encourages you to experiment and think, and not just charge blindly into solving the experiment.
[*]The game allows you to undo and redo your actions - including resetting the stage.  It means that for stages with multiple lynchpins, you can freely experiment after each step, and not worry about remembering the exact steps (or going the wrong direction, or undoing too far)
[*]Each stage focuses on a single mechanic (while reusing mechanics from earlier stages), and each level in a stage focuses on a single idea.  Each level is quick to solve, and while there are oftentimes variants of each idea, each puzzle has a unique core idea.  It rarely feels like, "Here's a new trick, now repeat it five times to pad the level count."  (And when it does, it's because I found the 'advanced' variant of an idea before finding the basic solution).
[/list]

But most importantly, the game nails what I'm looking for in a puzzle game.  Specifically:
I want to feel clever for solving a puzzle, and I want to feel like the designer is clever for creating the puzzle.  I don't want to feel like I lucked into a solution, or brute-forced it - I want to feel like I understand the idea the level is centered on.  And that, the game does in spades.

Patrick's Parabox is a polygonal puzzling masterpiece. Parsing the pieces of each puzzle is perplexing and yet rewarding. It starts off simple, allowing you to enter and exit boxes, but quickly escalates to mastering [spoiler] Multiple Infinities[/spoiler].

Each puzzle contains a new concept, even if some are variations of previous puzzles-- note down what you learn from each of the main series puzzles (you'll know when you hit the bottom) so you'll have an easier time tackling the extra Appendix and Challenge puzzles at the end- wherein the Appendix Puzzles contain [spoiler] new mechanics [/spoiler] and the Challenge puzzles simply being brutally difficult even if you've made it that far.

It took me approximately 19 hours to conquer all 364 puzzles this game had to offer, and there were countless moments that I felt like a goddamn idiot when I solved a puzzle-- having repeatedly come within a step or two of solving the puzzle but not quite getting it.

I would STRONGLY recommend you pick this up even if you are a fan of puzzle games-- even if it's to the smallest extent. Parabox is very beginner friendly with how approachable and understandable the puzzles are-- every time a new mechanic is introduced, it eases you into it softly.

This game is EASILY in my top 10 for 2022.

There's something that really fascinates me about Patrick's Parabox: it makes WAY too much sense.

It's a puzzle game about boxes within boxes, where the levels are boxes and the boxes are levels. Put a level inside itself and voila! recursion. You can enter it over and over and over and over. After that, every world adds a brand new mechanic.

Understanding what's going on gets progressively more difficult as you progress, but once you get past that mental barrier, the levels themselves aren't as difficult to solve. Most are a simple showcase of that world's mechanic or an interesting consequence of it. Optional challenge levels on the sides then build on those ideas, and that's where you'll spend most of your time.

The music is fitting for the genre, being present but never getting in the way. Each world has a different song that plays through it, and the title theme is in fact incredibly catchy.

As you "enter" deeper into the worlds you realize something interesting: most of their so-called "new mechanics" are just a core part of how the game has always worked - or perhaps a natural edge case -, that were cleverly withheld in the previous worlds, being brought into light only when they were needed to increase complexity. So much so, that after you see them, you can't help but think "of COURSE that's how that works! it's the only logical thing!"
This way, by the end, everything you thought you knew about the game at the beginning is recontextualized. However... true to its own recursive nature, it's not recontextualized into something different, but into itself: it's still a relatively simple game about boxes within boxes, where the levels are boxes and the boxes are levels.

The post-game has some small worlds that playfully tweak some of the interactions, radically changing how the game plays out; and a big world full of the toughest challenges the game has to offer. This was the point of the game where I finally found some puzzles where I simply cannot explain how they work. Thankfully, a fully complete understanding of the "why" isn't necessary to figure out the "how" of beating them, so I was still able to beat 100% of the game.

This will not be the hardest puzzle game you ever play, but damn if it isn't one of the smartest. I recommend it to anyone who is even vaguely interested in the genre. 10/10
