Every third spring, a solo indie developer reinvents Sokoban.

Okay, well, this certainly isn't as hard as Baba or Stephen's Sausage Roll but it's just as inventive and creative, and it's also, importantly, incredibly funny. I don't think puzzle design has ever made me laugh as hard as this game. The concepts are introduced and toyed with then integrated into future concepts smoothly, rarely do ideas feel repeated, there's a -ton- of puzzles and the challenge puzzles can get quite tricky, the aesthetic is polished and pleasant to look at, it's just an overall really clever and enjoyable puzzle game with.... no real downside to speak of, other than that it's not going to wreck your brain or stump you in the same ways as similar games, and that [spoiler]there's no real meta-puzzle aspect to the game, it is just a long sequence of levels with no real twist[/spoiler] but that second one is... well, really a nitpick, the game is compelling enough as-is that it didn't necessarily -need- that extra push to be awesome.

This is a puzzle game, a Sokoban game, but honestly you don't have to be a Sokoban aficionado to enjoy it. There are plenty of tough Sokoban sorts of challenges, but if you're stuck on a puzzle there's almost always a way to progress deeper in the game without having to solve it. 

Honestly, as solid as the puzzle-solving is, it's not the core experience. Instead, the core experience of this game is in wrapping your mind around the really trippy mechanics at play. 113320682.review:
[h1] 패트릭의 상자는 역설과 재귀로 가득해 [/h1]

차원과 공간의 왜곡이라는 컨셉을 내세운 게임으로, 상자를 다른 상자 속에 집어넣거나 밖으로 빼내 모든 상자들을 알맞은 위치에 배치해야 하는 소코반 스타일의 퍼즐 게임이다. 미니멀리즘의 미덕을 준수한 산뜻하고 깔끔한 비주얼과 느린 박자, 낮은 음색의 편안한 사운드트랙으로 퍼즐의 매력을 한껏 살린다. 참고로 헷갈릴까봐 노파심에 굳이 언급하자면, 게임의 제목은 '패트릭의 패러독스'가 아니고, [b] '패트릭의 패러박스' [/b]다. 이는 공간의 역설을 극대화한 게임의 핵심을 담은 제목이라 할 수 있을 것이다.

굉장히 기묘한 양상을 보여주는 퍼즐 게임이다. 구석에 박힌 상자 속에 들어가 퍼즐을 풀고 다른 방향으로 상자에서 나오기도 하고, 상자를 바깥으로 밀었더니 안에 있는 상자에서 밀어낸 상자가 다시 튀어나오기도 한다. 조건만 맞으면 같은 상자가 끝없이 들어가고 나오는 반복이 발생하기도 하고, 아예 퍼즐 자체를 벗어나는 역설이 발생하기까지 한다. 처음 게임을 접하면 도대체 이게 무슨 세상 요지경인가 싶을 정도다.

그래도 게임의 규칙 자체는 생각보다 단순하고 직관적이다. 상자의 열린 방향과 공간의 특성만 잘 파악해도 무난히 퍼즐을 해결할 수 있고, 매 챕터마다 새로 나타나는 매커니즘은 별다른 설명이 없어도 한두번의 시도만으로 그 특징을 쉽게 이해할 수 있다. 사실 퍼즐을 가만히 들여다보면 논리나 규칙이 모순되는 역설의 개념보다는 일정한 논리에 따라 상자의 출입이 반복되는 재귀의 개념에 좀 더 가깝다는 걸 알 수 있다. 그래서 상자의 안팎과 위치만 잘 따져도 퍼즐이 술술 풀릴 때가 많은 것이다.

더군다나 대부분의 퍼즐은 크기가 생각보다 작고 그만큼 퍼즐의 디자인 역시 단순하게 구성돼있다. 이를테면 후반부의 난해한 매커니즘을 제대로 이해하지 못해도 행동의 경우의 수를 좁히다보면 해결에 가까워지는 퍼즐이 더러 존재한다. 발상을 전환하는 게 힘들어서 그렇지, 무턱대고 이것저것 시도하다보면 의외로 뭔가 되는 것 같은 상황이 발생하는 것이다. 따라서 뭔가 혼란스러운 첫인상에 비해 실질적인 게임의 난이도는 그렇게까지 어렵진 않은 편이라 할 수 있다. (물론 이건 1차 엔딩을 위한 필수 퍼즐에 해당되는 말이고, 엔딩 이후 해금되는 챌린지 퍼즐은 모든 매커니즘의 특성을 총동원해야 겨우 풀릴 만큼 결코 만만치 않다.)

무려 364개의 퍼즐이 준비돼있어 컨텐츠 볼륨도 상당히 알찬 퍼즐 게임이다. 각 챕터마다 챕터의 핵심 매커니즘을 살린 퍼즐이 열몇개씩 배치돼있고, 주어진 선로에 배치된 기본 퍼즐과 선로 바깥의 확장 퍼즐이 분리돼있는 식이다. 특히 확장 퍼즐의 경우 화면이 이리저리 움직이거나 아스키 아트를 활용하는 등의 차별화를 보여주고 있어 퍼즐의 양상이 한결 풍부하게 느껴진다. 한편 한 챕터 안의 퍼즐들이 자가 복제에 가깝다는 의견이 종종 보이는데, 이걸 다르게 해석하자면 유사한 퍼즐 디자인에 약간의 변주를 입혀 난이도를 조금씩 올리고 퍼즐의 다양성을 늘린 좋은 시도라고도 볼 수 있을 것이다.

참 바바 이즈 유(Baba Is You)도 그렇고 이렇게 논리 구조를 치밀하면서도 절묘하게 활용하는 퍼즐 게임은 소수의 변태적인 천재가 좋은 게임을 만들어내는 것 같다. 개인적으로는 역대 다섯 손가락 안에 꼽을 수 있을 만큼 뛰어난 완성도를 자랑하는 퍼즐 게임이라고 본다. 그만큼 두뇌를 빠릿하게 굴려야 하는 퍼즐 게임을 원하는 이들이라면 무조건 만족할 수 밖에 없을 게임이다.

Ce jeu est fou. On pourrait penser que le concept, aussi intéressant soit-il, s'essouffle vite. Et ben pas du tout.

Il s'agit d'un "simple" jeu de réflexion construit autour d'un concept très simple : votre personnage (un carré rouge… au début) peut se déplacer de boîtes en boîtes. Et ces boîtes peuvent elle-même être poussées pour créer des chemins afin de résoudre chaque niveau.

Simple, on a dit.

Et pourtant. Je ne vais pas spoiler (car oui, ce jeu peut être spoilé) mais ces boîtes peuvent aussi être poussées dans d'autres. Et des fois, une boîte peut en contenir une deuxième, qui contient… la première. Vous voyez le genre ?

Le jeu va saupoudrer de nouvelles mécaniques au fil des (très nombreux) niveaux. Mais attention, on n'est pas ici face à un jeu d'énigme qui vous attire avec une carotte de premiers niveaux ultra simple, et vous met à mi-chemin face à un mur infranchissable. Chaque nouvelle mécanique est introduite organiquement de façon très claire, et est mise à contribution pour les niveaux suivants de façon très progressive.

La difficulté du jeu évolue raisonnablement, et même si certains niveaux sur le chemin principal finiront par demander pas mal de réflexion, les défis apparemment "impossibles" sont relégués à des niveaux bonus, non obligatoire pour la progression (mais fortement recommandé pour le challenge !). Ce jeu peut donc être pris en main par des joueurs de tout niveaux sans s'inquiéter d'arriver face à un mur infranchissable.

Et pourtant, vu les mécaniques en fin de partie, il aurait été très facile de faire des niveaux "n'importe quoi". Mais non, jusqu'au bout c'est super soigné.

On ajoute à tout ça une petite ambiance sonore sympathique qui colle parfaitement à ce qu'on a à l'écran, et une maniabilité évidemment aisée : quatre direction (plus un bouton pour valider dans les menus…).

En bref, un jeu d'énigme bien pensé, bien conçu, qui sait comment amener la difficulté sans jamais dégoûter le joueur.

This is a phenomenal puzzle game -- there's simply no other way to put it. So much care was put into the development of this game, and it really shows. This game introduces you to its mind-boggling mechanics in ways that make them feel intuitive, and the difficulty curve is a smooth and steady climb the whole way through. The game is structured in such a way that you don't have to solve all the puzzles in order to continue to the next "batch" of levels -- and on the other hand, if you found a section to be fairly easy, there's an abundance of much more challenging & completely optional puzzles that you can take a crack at along the way. And if you get through all of those (or even if you don't), once the game has introduced all of its mechanics, it opens up yet another huge area with dozens more of the game's hardest levels, which combine any and all of the crazy tricks you've learned along the way.
I can't stress enough just how incredible the level design of this game is. I can be pretty nitpicky when it comes to game design -- and I'm definitely prone to getting stuck on puzzles every now and then -- and I truly have nothing bad to say about the level design in Patrick's Parabox. It was a joyride from start to finish, and it never got boring for me; not even once.
If you like puzzle games, you'll love Patrick's Parabox -- whether you're new to the puzzle genre or an experienced puzzle master.

-Some puzzles are easy, little confidence boosters but not especially challenging
-Some puzzles are tough, making you stop and think carefully about what exactly has to happen to find the solution

Кривая сложности в игре выстроена очень грамотно – за всё прохождение ни разу не ловил себя на мысли, что текущие уровни стали сильно сложнее предыдущих. Возможно, однако, что перечисленное выше работает и в минус игре, так как за все основные уровни, включая испытания, не было таких, которые бы заставили посидеть над решением дольше 20 минут. 상자 속에 상자, 공간 안에 공간, 심지어 패러독스 안에 패러독스까지 차원을 농락하는 퍼즐게임

일반적인 소코반 계열의 퍼즐 풀이방식 (정해진 위치에 박스 및 캐릭터를 위치시켜야 레벨이 클리어되는 방식) 에 신박한 퍼즐 메커니즘을 섞은 게임으로, 반복성 / 재귀함수의 맛 + 공간 안에 공간을 집어넣는다는 발상이 섞여 재미있는 퍼즐 풀이법들을 볼 수 있는 작품이다. 스팀 페이지의 스크린샷만 봐도 혼란스러움이 느껴지지만 실제로 퍼즐들을 풀다 보면 이보다도 정신이 아득해지는 해답들 및 현상들을 마주할 수 있는데, 캐릭터가 움직이는 공간을 빈 공간에 집어넣은 뒤 이를 밀어서 원래 캐릭터가 움직이는 공간으로 다시 옮겨버린다던가, 캐릭터가 윗 차원의 캐릭터에게 밀려서 움직일 수 없다던가, 캐릭터 자체가 하나의 차원이여서 캐릭터 안에 캐릭터가 들어간다던가 등등 퍼즐들을 풀다보면 감탄하는 순간들이 나온다. 모든 퍼즐게임들이 그렇듯이 퍼즐들을 풀면 풀수록 새로운 메커니즘 - 예를 들면 다른 물체에 빙의를 한다던가, 무간지옥에 갇혀버린 상자들을 밀어야 한다던가, 심지어는 차원과 차원을 고의적으로 엮이게 만들어 패러독스를 일으킨다던가 등등의 요소들이 나오면서 퍼즐을 푸는 과정이 지루하지 않게 만드는 역할을 한다. 여기에 더해 게임 내 메인 퍼즐들 말고도 빨간 테두리의 퍼즐들과 파란 테두리의 퍼즐들이 있는데, 빨간 테두리는 메인보다 난이도가 높은 챌린지 퍼즐들이고, 파란 테두리는 난이도는 (빨간색보다는) 낮을 수는 있어도 메인 퍼즐들에서는 소개해주지 않는 메커니즘 및 비주얼을 자랑하는 퍼즐들이다. 이 파란 테두리의 퍼즐들이 생각보다 푸는 재미가 쏠쏠하고, 본편 퍼즐들로 이미 게임의 모든 것을 파악했다고 생각했던 두뇌에 다시 한번 자극을 주는 퍼즐들이다. 심지어는 게임의 엔딩을 보고 나면 (30+ 개의 챌린지 레벨들과 함께) 본편 퍼즐들과 비슷해 보이지만 퍼즐들의 규칙이 살짝 다른 부록 퍼즐들을 풀 수 있는데, 이 부록 퍼즐들은 본편의 퍼즐 규칙을 그대로 쓰면 당연히 안 풀리기 때문에 새로운 사고방식으로 퍼즐들을 푸는 재미가 있었다.

다만, Patrick's Parabox 의 퍼즐들은 은근히 난이도가 어렵지는 않다. 과거에 했었던 Baba is You 나 A Monster's Expedition 이 퍼즐 하나를 풀 때마다 햄버거 정식을 먹는 것처럼 뇌가 쪼개지는 기분이었다면, 이 게임은 퍼즐 하나당 치킨 너겟 하나를 먹는 기분으로 퍼즐 하나하나를 비교적 가볍게 풀 수 있는 퍼즐 게임이다. 대부분의 퍼즐들이 아이디어 하나만 잘 잡으면 "유레카 !" 하고 술술 풀리기 때문에, 퍼즐을 푸는 메인 열쇠를 제외한 실제 소코반 자체 (즉, 상자들을 배치해서 알맞은 방향으로 자리 잡게 하는 과정) 은 직관적이고 단순하다. 하드코어 퍼즐 매니아들은 이런 가벼운 퍼즐 게임을 별로 안 좋아할 수도 있으나, 개인적으로 나같이 소코반 계열 퍼즐 게임에 쥐약인 사람들에게는 이런 퍼즐 구성 방식이 호감이었다. 여기에 더해, 게임 내 퍼즐의 개수가 364개로 퍼즐 개수가 결코 적은 게임이 아니여서, 이렇게 퍼즐들이 술술 풀려도 분량이 부족하다는 생각은 전혀 들지 않았다. 오히려 소코반 자체의 난이도는 어렵지 않다는 특징 때문에 "신박한 퍼즐게임은 해보고 싶지만 고난이도의 퍼즐들로 머리를 뜯기는 싫다" 라는 사람들에게 추천하기 좋은 게임이라고 생각한다. 실제로 게임의 엔딩만을 볼 생각으로 메인 퍼즐들만 풀다 보면 약 4 ~ 5시간 정도에 엔딩을 볼 수 있을 정도로 퍼즐 메커니즘들을 모두 찍먹하는 게 부담스럽지 않고, 메인 게임이 너무 쉬웠다면 챌린지 레벨들을 풀며 두뇌를 발열할 수 있으니 말이다.


결론적으로, 상자 속에 상자를 집어넣는 발상에서 다양한 방향으로 가지를 친 나무를 보는 듯한 수많은 퍼즐 메커니즘 + 적절한 수의 레벨과 점진적 난이도 상승 분배 + 소코반에 알레르기가 있는 사람들도 부담없이 플레이 할 수 있는 난이도 세 가지가 합쳐져서 나온 수작 퍼즐게임. 오랜만에 굳은 뇌를 풀어주면서 어느 정도의 참신함이 섞여 있는 퍼즐들을 즐기고 싶다면, 한 번 해보는 걸 추천한다.

여담) 모든 퍼즐들을 풀면 캐릭터의 표정을 무표정에서 썩소로 바꿀 수 있는 기능이 열리는데, 이 표정이 은근히 귀엽다.

113197975.review:
[h1] 一起来推[箱[箱[箱子[箱[子]]]子]子]箱子吧！ [/h1]
	一款神奇的推箱子游戏，把递归思想具象化，用创意关卡的形式做成解谜。在可爱音画的辅助下，这款推箱子解谜拥有神奇的魅力，对谜题爱好者来说是一部不可多得的佳作！啊，前有箱子，接下来R会很有用！

[h1][quote=]
[table]
    [tr]
        [th]　欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38287879]网易UU鉴赏家培养计划[/url][/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]　来这里找优质游戏、开黑日友、白嫖UU时长卡　[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]　加速Steam社区、游戏记得用UU哦_(:з」∠)_　[/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[/quote][/h1]

简评：
+ 递归推箱的绝佳创意
+ 海量高阶的特色关卡
+ 美丽优雅的解谜思路
+ 丰富的Eureka时刻
+ 美术可爱氛围轻松过
+ 适合碎片化时间游玩
- 对于普通人来说难度偏高
- 缺少主题单元目录
- 没有任何提示方式真要命啊

[h1] → ∞ ← [/h1]
	游戏的核心机制只有一个：箱子可以进入箱子——递；箱子可以从箱子里出来——归。基于此，谜题的设计充分利用了空间的奇思妙想，以单元的形式做成关卡，在每个单元，你都能享受到有主题有思路的谜题。难度循序渐进，向后的单元谜题更加综合，并且这些谜题在递归思想的组合下变得非常美丽和谐，经常能给你带来“Eureka！”的激动时刻。

	体验下来，解谜最深的感受就是：我去，我又∞了。诶诶！我能解开了！游戏中的主题关卡非常有创意，从初始关“入门、进入”两单元结束后，就是“空白、吞食、参照”这些难度一阶的关卡，再往后“调换、居中、克隆、转移、开放、翻转”等一些高阶关卡，每关必须完成对应关卡数目内容才能解锁下一关。比如令我印象很深的“吞食”单元，推箱子的方向对解谜的思路影响很大，而这一整个单元都是用大箱子推小箱子并吃掉的思路解题，箱子进入箱子仅仅通过方向的调换就创造了吞吃的感觉，不但创意很棒，而且非常美丽！后续还有例如“克隆、转移、翻转”的设计思路都令人惊艳，越往后越发现单纯的推箱子竟然还可以这么玩，整个解谜过程中的体验就是“哇哦好厉害→痛苦死了解不开→哇哦好厉害→痛苦死了解不开”。

[h1] 既有轻松的关卡，也有困难的挑战 [/h1]
	游戏大关由比较简单的主线关，高难度的挑战关，略显诡异的数字关等等。你并非一定要破解单个单元里的所有谜题才能体验下一关。设计师在最开始就给了你几个非常有用的提示“倒推解谜思路、排除无用思路”，并且鼓励你在卡关的时候尝试其它的关卡以寻找思路。不得不说真的很有用，运用排除思维和倒推思想顺利帮我解开了不少关卡。不过设计师还给了你一些更实用的建议“保持心平气和，别想迅速解开”“多用反悔键Z和重开键R”。是的呢，R已经被我按的快没了。

	虽然谜题非常硬核，但游戏美术非常舒适，游戏也不单纯是枯燥的推箱子场景，有着设计感明显的色块美术，推箱子的主角是一只叫帕特里克的箱子，它也非常可爱。加上本作有着十分符合谜题意境的音乐，足以让你在谜题烧脑之余抚慰你的心灵。此外，本作的谜题有着非常强的可重玩性，一关就算你解开了，许久之后再次做题还是会陷入沉思，和数学考试非常像，不过本作非常鼓励你轻松愉快地进行解谜，因此整个游戏都是十分愉快的氛围。美中不足的大概是两点：1.没有一个大单元目录，每次切换别的单元只能手动跑。2.没有提示啊，完全没有提示啊，真的全得自己动脑子想！

[h1] 总结：创意绝佳，解谜硬核，轻松愉快，Eureka！[/h1]
《Patrick's Parabox》有着能够打上满分的创意，和无数基于“递归”原点创造的美丽、和谐、有难度的关卡，是解谜狂热者一定会喜欢的作品。此外本作轻松愉快的解题氛围也不会给人逼迫和局促感，是那种很适合在碎片时间玩一关的游戏，更牛逼的是，本作的Eureka时刻（解谜游戏里的Aha时刻）实在是太多了，几乎每一关都能给你带来这种清爽的成就感，而Eureka正是所有谜题设计师所渴望带给玩家的终极目标啊！所以，冲就完事了！

113151561.review:
《Patrick's Parabox》凭借“递归推箱”的新颖机制，在推出试玩版后已经让许多玩家期待许久，如今终于发售，在充分游玩后我认为，本作果然是一款不负众望的神作。

本作一开始，关卡中只有一个正方形的场景，而场景中除了主角之外，还有一些可以推动的箱子，每个关卡的目标就是将箱子推到指定的地点，然后主角本身也要走到一个目标点上。很快玩家就会发现，一些“箱子”的内部也是一个个正方形的场景，而主角和箱子（不管是正常的箱子还是别的场景）都可以进出这些场景，也就是说，各个场景之间是可以以这种方式“嵌套”的。但“嵌套”还不算是“递归”，在之后的一些关卡中，玩家又会发现，场景中的某些箱子“内部”，包含的就是箱子“外面”的场景本身，这就是真正的递归。在这种不属于层次关系的空间结构下，单纯考虑“里面”或“外面”就没有意义了，考虑空间的连接方式才是更有意义的。

看上去非常烧脑，很多玩家此时会望而却步，而我要告诉大家的是，不用担心，本作并不像一些“同类作品”（其实我只能想到一个《Recursed》）一样死难，仿佛一些数学书给了寥寥几个重要定理后就将一堆复杂证明“留作习题”，相反，本作会通过循序渐进的谜题设计，逐渐让玩家熟悉对“递归空间”的思考，既起到提示玩家的效果，又非常自然，玩家在游玩时应该不会产生“游戏直接告诉了我答案”的想法，从而还是保证了玩家自己解开谜题的成就感。因此，本作实际上是一个相当易于上手的游戏。

具体来说，玩家很容易通过“主线”关卡领略到本作绝大多数的机制，体会到本作优雅的结构、机制和谜题设计，而主线谜题基本只占本作谜题数量的一半左右，还有大量的关卡散布在可选的支路上。带有红色边框的“挑战”关卡，顾名思义，有一定挑战性，体现对规则集、系统和一些主线关卡中出现的点子的深度挖掘，注重对玩家思考能力的考验，或是给玩家展示新奇的可能性。带有蓝色边框的“额外”关卡（其实被叫做Side puzzle，我感觉翻成“支线”关卡比较容易和“主线之外的关卡”混淆，所以就这样）则更偏向彩蛋性质，要么有奇怪的视觉效果，要么注重探索系统中的一些奇怪的“边缘情况”，或者直接引入一些没有做进主线的新机制。通关主线后，还会解锁更多的挑战关卡和额外关卡，甚至有些关卡[spoiler]修改了本作其他关卡中的一些基本的运作机制，探索原本规则之外的可能性，这样的“what if”真有种“平行宇宙”的感觉[/spoiler]。本作其实还内置了玩家自制关卡读取功能，不过并没有特别方便的关卡编辑器，不管怎么说，可以预见在功能完善，且玩家和设计师涌入之后，自制谜题也会充满惊喜。

在这插一段推荐一个我喜欢的自制关卡包：Outside。你可以在社区Discord或者Steam讨论区里找到。这个关卡包是一个模仿本体中一个“大关”形式的17个关卡的集合，主要围绕本体中一个没有深入探索的机制进行设计，其中最后一个谜题是该关卡包作者之前设计的一个很难的谜题，而前面的谜题可以说都是为了设计一个较为平滑的难度曲线而设计的，当然每个谜题也都有自己的亮点就是了。不过这个关卡包还是比所有的本体关卡都要困难，17关就花了我5个小时的时间，其中2个小时以上花在最后一个谜题，而且该关卡包用到了本体后期的机制，所以建议通关甚至100%本体后再玩。

总之，本作的核心机制和对核心机制的诸多扩展都非常有创意，谜题设计非常出色，几乎处处都是惊喜，在游玩这个游戏的十几个小时中，我没有一秒不在感受解谜的喜悦或赞叹本作的设计。我可以列出很多我喜欢这个游戏的点，但最终我发现，基本上每个谜题我都很喜欢，而说到具体的谜题解法的话也只会剧透，所以就这样吧。

结论：[b]强烈推荐[/b]。

At first it was like "ok this is kinda weird but I understand" 

And then it became "this is getting out of hand I have no idea what I'm even doing anymore but by some act of God the puzzles are getting solved" 

And then "I am the God solving the puzzles, I see in 4 dimensions and have complete control over the will of the boxes, the laws of this universe are exposed to me" 

And then finally right back to "wtf is even going on anymore I understand nothing"

In all seriousness, this is the most consistently fun puzzle game I've ever played because the pacing is PERFECT! If you like puzzle games this is one of the best.

Patrick's Parabox is a block pushing puzzle game on the level of Baba is You.

The basics are simple: push block here and stand here to finish level. What this game does uniquely is include recursion. Boxes can go into other boxes. Boxes can go into themselves infinitely. Those infinite patterns can layer onto itself.

The learning curve was excellent at letting the player figure out properties themselves. Nothing felt like filler and all levels explored different concepts in different ways. Also appreciated are the dedicated undo/redo/restart buttons, and the ability to undo a restart. The game also lets you unlock or relock all puzzles at any time. Music, UI, and aesthetics are also great.

I generally dislike puzzle focused games but have some exceptions: Portal 1/2, Antichamber, Baba is You. I can now add Patrick's Parabox to that list.

113140065.review:
I really despise Sokoban, so much so that I hated Baba Is You even when everyone else loved it, because the sokoban part of the game was constructed in a boring way that I'd seen a hundred times before, even if there were labels on some tiles. I've been doing sokoban since I was playing nethack every day and I never need to do it again unless there's a good reason.

Parabox has the best Sokoban puzzles that I've ever seen. Truly, even beyond the amazing set of mechanics that are introduced per world, the puzzles themselves are lean and don't have any trick alleys designed to confuse you from the correct solution--if there is a level with a single fixed block in it, you can be certain that that fixed block is used in the ultimate solution. I appreciate this immensely--it often means that once the *concept* of a level is understood, the solution is trivial. (Also there are literal nethack tribute bonus levels, which made me so happy.)

And the paraboxical mechanics are great! Recursion, references, mirroring, with very natural interactions between every one. The game really reminded me of a Zachtronics game in the sense that you are putting together a set of transformations with your movements to achieve a final product.

The one complaint I would have is that the linear nature of the world unlocks means that you have to substantially complete each world before doing the next. Sometimes this causes me to bounce off games because I hit a wall, but the puzzles here are so fun and relatively easy that that hasn't happened, but I do worry about it in general for this style.

First two worlds in the full version are 90% the same as the demo.
But then there are more worlds.
How many? I dunno man, I'm like 8 or 9 deep currently with no obvious way to see how much farther it goes.
If you can imagine busting out a hypothetical level editor just to see "But what would happen if..." then the full game apparently has levels which rely on the answer to exactly that question to solve the puzzle.
What if you could step outside a level in a different direction than you're currently pushing it?
What if you could step into the smaller copy of the level you're already in directly?
What happens if you try to step directly from one small level to another?
What about the above but *the levels have different resolutions*?
What happens when you try to step into a level that has more than one exit?
Or huge exits?
Or.. Christ, the level doesn't even have walls?
What crazy crap goes on if you have multiple levels each nested within the other?
Sokoban++ your way through this and many other questions, until you finally have mastery of every ridiculous mechanic possible!
That's okay, Patrick will just tell you "congratulations! Now enjoy this NEW mechanic you've never seen before, and it renders the entire zeitgeist you've learned into a mere tip of an iceberg of new madness". 
And rinse and repeat
AND rinse and repeat.

In the late 70s Warren Robinett invented and perfected the Hyperlinked Map Mechanic to make devious, physically impossible mazes for Atari Adventure, Rocky's Boots, and eventually Robot Odyssey.

I think that Warren would be floored to see how Patrick has tortured and twisted and eldritchified the mechanic here.

Sokoban with a twist so gameplay changing that it's genuinely one of the first box shoving puzzle games I've ever seen that outright can't be called a Sokoban clone anymore.

The best part of this game is that it keeps changing the formula with new features. First you start with boxes that you and other boxes can go inside of. Then you get boxes that contain themselves. Then it follows up with boxes that have copies of itself. I've also come into contact with mirrors recently, and I can't wait for what other new twists the game will throw at me.
--EDIT: Having finished all of the puzzles now, I must say I'm sticking with my review. Absolutely. Amazing Game. Enjoyed every mind numbing puzzle right up to the end with every twist it threw at me and kept surprising me.
I was hoping for rotational puzzles as well, but even this is explained in-game to be too complex code-wise, which I can understand, but can't help but cross my fingers that it might still be added at some point.
In the end I finished it almost within a day, but worth every brain melting penny.--

The puzzle mechanics themselves are introduced in an extremely kind way, where you first get to learn the basics, and are even forced into pulling off fun tricks before it throws you into the deep end with (optional) much harder puzzles. I personally really enjoy the ASCII version where you have to visualize everything yourself with all the things you've learned so far.
It's just superbly crafted and just really well thought out. Couldn't recommend any puzzle game more.

Can't wait for the sequel to this game where you make the exact same game, but in 3D.

推箱子这个玩法想必大家都不陌生，在互联网都不是很普及的“上古时代”就已经有不少非常风靡的推箱子游戏了。很多推箱子游戏虽然看似有所创新，但实际上核心玩法并无太大突破。但今天为大家介绍的这款《Patrick's Parabox》就不一样了，这款游戏在玩法的设计上可谓脑洞大开，为我们带来了完全不一样的游戏体验，可以说是“你没有玩过的船新版本”。

《Patrick's Parabox》这款游戏并非出自大厂，而是由一位名叫Patrick的独立游戏开发者设计和制作，游戏名字也因此而来。游戏的核心玩法依然是大家熟悉的推箱子，但推箱子属实是被这位开发者玩明白了——他在设计关卡时不再拘泥于传统推箱子游戏的规则，而是大胆地玩起了“套娃”，玩家推的箱子里面还能再套一个甚至多个场景。

简单地说，就是玩家推箱子的时候会遇到一些可以进入的箱子，在玩家进入这个可以进入的箱子之后，可以在箱子里面玩推箱子。因为这种有趣的“套娃”机制，就让很多谜题的解法需要玩家具有相当大的脑洞才能想到。如果将普通的箱子称为一级箱子，将可以进入的箱子称为二级箱子，那么我们是可以将一级箱子推到二级箱子内部，然后在二级箱子内部进行推箱子的操作，有很多时候一级箱子是无法直接推到目标地点的，必须通过在二级箱子内部进行推箱子的操作，将其从正确的位置推出来，才能解决谜题。但这还仅仅只是开始，随着关卡的推进，还有三级箱子——进入之后还能再进入一层，以此类推，越来越复杂，越来越考验玩家的脑力。

不仅如此，后面的关卡还会有各种新的机制加入，给玩家的决策带来更多的挑战。有时候需要我们从整个大局来考虑，而通过目标地点的位置和关卡场景来反推出解谜路线，也是一个很有效的思路。

《Patrick's Parabox》虽然是一款单人开发的独立游戏，但却有相当丰富的内容，共计350多个富有挑战性的关卡，加上本就新意十足、脑洞大开的玩法，可以说诚意满满。喜欢推箱子玩法的解谜游戏玩家非常适合游玩本作。

Patrick's Parabox is clever and is a refreshing take on the Sokoban genre. The answers are deliberate and rewarding. The developer does not waste space or employ cheap tricks: the puzzles are created from someone who truly enjoys sokoban puzzles and is able to explore the concept thoroughly. Parabox is as much a game as it is an evolution and exploration of the genre.  

The tutorial feels natural and it evolves into the game play quickly. The game moves at the players pace and is never weighed down by redundancy. Each puzzle feels like a clever branch of the last without holding you back or pushing the player too far forward, it builds on concepts and it's up to the player to execute them.  Whenever I got stuck on a puzzle I liked being able to play the other puzzles in the sequence again to find the missing link or move ahead and come back to the puzzle with fresh eyes. 

I've managed 53 of the 350+ puzzles so far at the time of the review. I can't wait to jump back into the game. Solving the puzzles feels natural and the more difficult moments have a good balance of challenge and eureka moments wrapped in. 

Additional notes! The game is disability friendly: great UI/accessability, full control remapping, the ability to add a grid, clear legible font, undo/redo buttons, good contrast in the colours and is colourblind friendly in its design.

Of the small handful of puzzle games I've played, this one definitely feels like it properly sets forth a Beginner Level of sorts - Not boringly easy, mind you, and there are certainly a few brainbusters to test your knowledge of the game.
I could draw similarities between this and Portal - The mechanics are all laid out cleanly in the earlier levels, each Level Set covering the various niche mechanics until, by the end, one should have a clear understanding of the ins and outs of the outer-ins and inner-outs of this game's rendition of Recursive Block Pushing.

I'll not spoil any of the mechanics you'll find, but each and every one adds a unique twist that's explored in depth, and isn't fully abandoned once you progress deeper - Every ounce of knowledge gained eases one through the later levels

I beat the game in under 8 hours, and despite getting absolutely stumped at one stage, I was able to progress to the deeper stages thanks to the lenient level completion requirements to proceed to the next stage, before coming back once I'd gotten a better grasp of what that level set was going over thanks to working with it with more intricate (and somehow easier for me to understand) mechanics

Getting 100% was fun, and, save for having watched Aliensrock's first episode on this game (covering the first two or three level sets), I managed to do it without any guides or outside help. And once the credits roll, there's a lot more to do! Even a subset of levels that make yet more interesting twists on the mechanics!

As long as you remember to step away from a level if it's stumped you, there's a good balance of brain busters, progression rate, and deep thinking moments provided by this game. Would absolutely recommend.

好玩不难，机制很有趣，关卡很有意思。

门槛真的非常低，在我玩过并且比较喜欢的游戏里，上手难度跟braid和elechead差不多级别，强烈推荐大家来玩。

——以下内容写于全成就通关后——

支线关卡的话，三个附加章节的难度不是很大，但是挑战关合集的难度完全超出了其它关的总体难度。

很多关都有2个或更多的非平凡点，并且相当一部分非平凡点也是很多时候难以注意到的机制边角料。

而且，有个别关卡我卡关时间也超过了半个小时，甚至有一关卡了2个多小时。可以说这部分还是有一定难度的，和其它的那些低门槛关卡不是一个级别了。

当然，只要那些点想到了，关卡自然也就过了。这一点游戏始终是非常收敛的，每关除开几个非平凡点外，没有使人卡关的非核心要素。这的确导致了游戏前中期较低的难度，但这也正是这个游戏的可贵之处。

那么决定一关用时的因素，也就是想到这个关卡的核心点需要的时间有多久。

38个挑战关占用了我总游戏时间的40%，但我始终坚持没有看任何攻略或者提示，最后解出了全部关卡。

所以，尽管一般认为这个游戏的难度只是入门级别，但看到有人说游戏难度低时，也不要轻信。多看看不同人的说法有利于更好地了解游戏的实际难度。

[h1]不用看，解谜游戏玩家无脑入手就对了。[/h1]

《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》是由Patrick Traynor制作发行的一款以推箱子玩法的解谜游戏。对于推箱子解谜游戏，相信大部分玩家小学时候有在学习机上面玩过，虽然操作上简单不过依旧可以玩得很入迷。若你也跟我一样有沉迷过推箱子解谜游戏的话，那么本作绝对能够给你带来更加有意思、同时也更加烧脑的推箱子解谜。

制作者在游戏商店页面中提到本作在2020年独立游戏节中获得设计卓越奖项，就游戏体验来说个人认为本作确实也值得这个奖。一般的推箱子游戏都是设定在一个固定的场景中，玩家只要把箱子推到对应的位置就OK了，而本作就如其游戏名字一般，毕竟是箱子无穷奇遇嘛，其箱子是一层套一层，箱子套着箱子、箱子套着箱子多重箱子的循环式套娃解谜。

其套娃的特性体现在，从最开始只有普通的实心方块变成了有内置通道的方块，玩家需要利用好内置通道的特性，将实心方块先推进至内置通道的方块，在将含有实心方块的内置通道方块移动的正确前置位，最后再进入导内置通道的方块中将实心方块推出，放置到标记好的位置上。这还是最基础的套娃，后续的关卡中还会有更多的新机制给玩家进行思考挑战，比如放大场景跟缩小场景的结合，玩家在方块内部的行动，场景内的方块也会体现出来，如何利用好方块的出入口来完成解谜则是玩家需要考虑的因素。

《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》提供了超过350多个关卡，玩家需要完成每个关卡中规定的关卡数量后才能解锁进入到新的关卡，就游戏的耐玩性来说是相当充足的。不过考虑到本作的烧脑程度不低，为了让玩家也能够体验到后续关卡，制作组在设置中加入了解锁全关卡游玩的选项，虽说每个大关卡中的小关卡都是对应着本关卡的主题，但个人建议还是循序渐进。前面的关卡都完成不了了，对于机制不熟悉的话，后面的话就更加折磨了。

游戏性方面表现优秀，音画体验的话也同样让人满意，极简画风观感清新，音乐部分则是如制作组所说一般令人心旷神怡，如果有单独的原声集推出一定要入一份，很适合工作学习时听。总的来说作为一款解谜游戏《帕特里克的箱子无穷奇遇》的游戏质量在线，充足的挑战性也能够满足解谜游戏爱好者的游玩需求，强烈推荐解谜游戏玩家入手游玩。

A fabulously smart puzzle game. Despite its complicated premise, it's built to be friendly to those (such as myself) who are not great at solving hard puzzles. It also provides its fair share of genuinely difficult levels for people who are more well versed in puzzle games. It may seem like a generic box-pusher puzzle at first glance, but the further in you get the more you see how much this game turns the genre on its head. 

There's plenty of content to enjoy, with hundreds of levels that introduce more mechanics the further in you go. It isn't too hard to "beat" the game by mainlining through all the required puzzles, but the real meat lies in the optional challenge puzzles that use the skills you learned already to really test your creative thinking and problem solving skills. Your perception of space and direction will be warped as you push boxes into other boxes, or sometimes a box into itself. There's even a special achievement for creating a paradox and breaking everything. That's fun.

Highly recommended for any puzzle enjoyers, or even for people who may not be so strong with puzzle games. Every puzzle feels like a new puzzle, and you are always discovering new ways to interact with the funky world our little purple protagonist inhabits. For the developer's first commercial game release, this is a big achievement! Huge props. Love ya Pat.

(DISCLAIMER: I tested this game. My name's in the credits. Also I suggested a mechanic that ended up making it into the game. Also also, while Steam shows that I have 8.9 hours on record at review time, my actual game time is longer since I beat the game in pre-Steam builds, and have been keeping up with new/edited levels in build updates; at review time, my savefile actually reads 14 hours 34 minutes.)

Patrick's Parabox is a game about what Patrick's Parabox is a game about.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/edderiofer/recommended/497780/]Ahem, sorry, I'm thinking of Recursed. Lemme try again.[/url]

Patrick's Parabox is a recursive Sokoban game. Boxes are rooms and you can push them into and out of other rooms. Sounds complex, you say? Yes! And you don't even know the half of it.

If you've ever played Recursed, your main question is going to be how similar this game is to Recursed. My answer is "a bit, but not really". Unlike in Recursed, rooms are not instanced; the boxes can therefore be thought of as [i]portals[/i] to existing rooms, rather than the "chests that spawn new copies of rooms" of Recursed. This of course leads to a different set of puzzles, which leans less on the Sokoban as Recursed does on platforming.

Like with every other pure puzzle game separated into distinct worlds and levels, every world introduces a new mechanic. Here, there's a mix of classic "new mechanic discovery", where you are introduced to an explicitly new type of puzzle element (e.g. boxes that are mirrored, boxes that are clones of other boxes), and have to grapple with what it does; and of SSR-style "new mechanic discovery", where you discover a new interaction between existing elements that was only impossible earlier because the level layout didn't permit it. Obviously I won't say too much about what those are, since Puzzle Solutions Are Spoilers™. If you must know, however, there is at least one mechanic that is not represented in the trailer (and it's the best one in the game because I was the one to suggest it).

Difficulty-wise, though, Patrick's Parabox is quite gentle; far moreso than the trial-by-chest lategame of Recursed. The music is quite chill and friendly, too, as is the general vibe of the game, so it's clear that this game was designed for a more general audience. However, that's not to say there's nothing for hardcore puzzle fans. Each world has plenty of optional levels if you really want to bash your head against something, and there are additional challenge levels once you beat the game, as well as bonus levels that outright change the rules of the game, too (how might the game have been different if you could push a box from within itself?).

Despite this, Patrick's Parabox didn't really hold any crazy surprises for me, unlike many modern puzzle games. But maybe that's just because I also watched some developer streams so I had some idea of what to expect going in. I can't claim this to be universal, and certainly you yourself may end up being surprised.

(As a technical note for those who care, Patrick's Parabox is provably in PSPACE.)

In conclusion, this is definitely a must-play puzzle game of 2022 if you have any interest in puzzle games, no matter how casual or hardcore of a puzzler you are. I enjoyed my time with it and if you care enough to have read this review, you probably will too.

Sokoban con más de 350 niveles, su dificultad sube en cada sección y muestra mecánicas únicas que van implementandose. Un título de puzles difícil que rompe la 4º pared en ocasiones.
--------------------------------------------------------------------

1980 fue la primera vez que vimos un sokoban, muchos no sabréis ni de qué hablo pero lo cierto es que el género ha ido aumentando sus títulos poco a poco. Un ejemplo de Sokoban es el famoso y laureado "Baba is you". 

Para quien no lo sepa, un Sokoban, se trata de un juego de rompecabezas donde el jugador debe almacenar las cajas en los espacios de destino. Puede moverse en las cuatro direcciones y empujar (pero no tirar) de una caja a la vez. Una vez que se han colocado todas las casillas (a veces es un verdadero rompecabezas ), se pasa de nivel y el jugador pasa al siguiente nivel , que generalmente es más difícil. En definitiva, Patrick Traynor nos trae su visión sobre un género poco conocido. 

[h1]¿Qué hace especial a Patrick 's Parabox?[/h1]

Lo cierto es que se trata de un juego de puzles, iremos avanzando por sus distintas secciones desbloqueando nuevas habilidades que son implementadas in Game como si de un tutorial invisible se tratase. Lo cierto es que el grado de dificultad en Patrick Parabox se va acrecentando, el título cuenta con 350 rompecabezas. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2786585696

[b]Lo primero que nos dice es que se trata de un juego difícil, por lo que es normal que en ocasiones tardemos más de la cuenta en dar con la respuesta.[/b]

En cuanto a las mecánicas, dividido en un sin fin de secciones, iremos progresando por las distintas zonas que forman nuestro circuito, en cada zona veremos habilidades únicas. Estamos en un sokoban, su mecánica principal será la de arrastrar cajas pero Patrick Parabox Rompe la 4 pared, jugando con nuestra percepción. Por ejemplo: En ocasiones podremos meter una caja dentro de otra para resolver el puzle o incluso tendremos que crear un bucle para liberar la solución. Por consiguiente, en los puzles solo he descubierto una solución única pero posiblemente más adelante haya múltiples resoluciones.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2786585441

Por último, decir que  no todo son simples puzles de cajas. Lo cierto es que Patrick es un firme seguidor del género y podremos encontrar puzles con cierto aspecto diferente que nos recuerdan a los primeros sokoban que salieron. 

[h1]Apartados técnicos[/h1]

[b]En el apartado visual[/b] vemos que es donde más peca Patrick 's Parabox, lo cierto es que tiene un diseño extremadamente simple, dejándolo todo a sus cientos de rompecabezas y sus tremendos juegos de cámara. Sin duda no es su fuerte, el apartado gráfico. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2786585769

[b]La parte sonora[/b], la trae Priscila Snow conocida por traer la música en otros títulos como Skin deep. Lo cierto es que en Patrick 's Parabox está melodía se trata de una música ambiental que nos permite centrarnos de lleno en los rompecabezas.


[h1]Conclusión[/h1]

En definitiva, Patrick 's Parabox se trata de un Sokoban atípico, aquí no solo moveremos cajas, se irán implementando mecánicas de forma recursiva. El título cuenta con 350 niveles llenos de sorpresas, posee un apartado visual muy simple y una música ambiental que permite centrar la acción en su rompecabezas. Sin duda un título muy recomendable para amantes de los puzles y como no los sokoban.


[h1]🥈Nota: 8.5/10[/h1]
